News.title: Trump rambles from his under-construction White House ballroom after Election Day disaster
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

President Donald Trump’s first public appearance after devastating Republican losses in midterm elections was on the bare floor of his under-construction White House ballroom.

Trump — whose closing campaign message was delivered from his recently renovated Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool on Monday afternoon — did not mention his party’s blowout loses and Democrats’ historic victories that will see his opposing party winning both chambers of Congress as he spoke about the ballroom, uninterrupted, for more than 15 minutes.

Instead, he rambled about his multi-million dollar ballroom project while microphone feedback repeatedly screeched into the public address system.

“I grew up with you … Maybe in a different form, maybe genetically, maybe it was your fathers or your mothers, but I grew up with construction sites,” he said at one point.

After demolishing the East Wing of the White House, Trump envisioned an ornate White House ballroom stuffed with gold finishes and marble floors to replace it. But court filings over the last several months have detailed what officials called “top secret” designs that revealed the primary purpose of the 90,000-square-foot ballroom project.

The ballroom is “a knitted, unified, cohesive part of the East Wing Project, which is vital for National Security, and is being constructed to ensure that the President can perform his constitutional duties in a safe and heavily secured facility,” government lawyers wrote in court documents this summer.

Trump’s first morning-after reaction to massive Democratic victories in midterm elections saw him revisiting some of his favorite headlines.

The president posted images of the print edition of The New York Post’s Tuesday story hailing the so-called “Donroe Doctrine” and his strongman, military-driven foreign policy dominating the Western Hemisphere by killing hundreds of people accused of trafficking drugs and launching a military operation to arrest Venezuela’s ousted leader Nicolàs Maduro.

It was Trump’s first post to his social media platform after election night, which also saw him call into Fox News to muse about the results after he complained about the network’s coverage.

Trump has repeatedly distance himself from Tuesday’s losses, claiming that his party would have fared better if his name was on the ballot.

“I wasn’t on the ballot, and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE,” Trump wrote on Truth Social on Tuesday evening.

He said the same to reporters from inside the ballroom site on Wednesday.

This is a developing story

News.title: Is there a vaccine for Ebola? The treatments being developed for the Bundibugyo strain
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A British healthcare worker in the Democratic Republic of Congo has tested positive for Ebola.

Reports indicate that the patient will be flown back to Britain by medical evacuation from the DRC. The patient is said to be in a stable condition and is expected to arrive on Wednesday or Thursday.

The healthcare worker, who has not been named, was sent to the DRC by a humanitarian organisation in a bid to support the response to the outbreak.

A Foreign Office spokesperson said: “A British citizen currently in the DRC has tested positive for Ebola. The risk to the UK public from Ebola remains low.”

Global health authorities are still seeking medical solutions to combat the Ebola outbreak, linked to the Bundibugyo strain of the virus.

open image in gallery The Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) carries a significant fatality rate, reaching up to 40 per cent ( Reuters )

Unlike the more common Zaire strain, for which approved vaccines and treatments exist, there are currently no specific medical interventions for Bundibugyo.

According to data released last week, the death toll from Ebola has surpassed 5,000, with more than 10,000 people thought to be infected.

The Bundibugyo ebolavirus (BDBV) carries a significant fatality rate, reaching up to 40 per cent.

A limited number of experimental vaccines and therapies are under evaluation, while global health bodies are also investigating whether any existing Ebola treatments could offer protection, though current evidence is restricted to animal studies.

Most of these experimental options have not yet undergone human trials, necessitating emergency or compassionate-use authorisation before they can be deployed in Congo.

The WHO recently advised prioritising several experimental drugs, including antibodies, antivirals, and vaccines, for both the treatment and prevention of BDBV.

open image in gallery Dr Elizabeth Furaha, medical director of Karibuni wa Mama, speaks with a relative of a patient at Sofepadi Hospital in Bunia, Congo ( AP )

Here is what we know of these candidates so far:

Ebola vaccines

1. The WHO has said a single-dose rVSV Bundibugyo vaccine being developed by the International AIDS Vaccine Initiative is the most promising candidate to prevent BDBV.

The vaccine, rVSVΔG/BDBV-GP, which uses the same technology as Merck's approved vaccine Ervebo for the Zaire strain, has shown survival benefit in non-human primates in a 2023 proof-of-concept study.

The WHO earlier said that development of the vaccine would likely take seven to nine months before it is ready for assessment in a clinical trial.

The International AIDS Vaccine Initiative said it is advancing the candidate towards a clinical trial and preparing for manufacturing, including transferring the vaccine virus and processes for Good Manufacturing Practices production.

2. The WHO has recommended prioritising another vaccine candidate, ChAdOx1 Bundibugyo, being developed by Oxford University and the Serum Institute of India.

The potential vaccine is based on ChAdOx1 technology, which was used in the Oxford/AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine, and is being manufactured by the Serum Institute.

The company started production under its "emergency response framework", alongside partners Coalition for Epidemic Preparedness Innovations, or CEPI, and the University of Oxford, as soon as it got word of the outbreak in May, a spokesperson said.

Doses could be ready within two to three months for efficacy assessment through a clinical trial, the WHO said at the time, adding that additional animal studies have yet to be conducted.

The WHO said experts considered a single dose of the vaccine candidate potentially suitable for contacts of Ebola cases, while a two-dose regimen might be used for high-risk but unexposed groups, including healthcare workers and frontline responders.

The vaccine candidate has now been recommended to enter the pivotal Phase 2/3 clinical trial in the DRC, in a significant step towards tackling the virus.

open image in gallery Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus announced two more vaccines are being investigated ( Reuters )

The WHO has recommended adding two new Ebola vaccine candidates to the ongoing Tumaini clinical trial in the DRC, marking the first time vaccines specifically designed to protect against Bundibugyo have been recommended.

The two vaccine candidates are ChAdOx1, developed by the university of Oxford with the Serum Institute of India, and Moderna’s mRNA-1469.

WHO’s independent Technical Advisory Group on Candidate Vaccine Prioritization recommended both for further clinical evaluation this week, based on available preclinical and early clinical evidence.

The companies were informed about the trial on Monday, and the vaccine candidates will enter the trial following national approvals.

Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO Director General, said: “The fact that these vaccines are ready to enter clinical trials is a testament to the power of science and partnership.

“I thank the scientists, health workers and partners in the DRC and around the world who have brought us to this point, and especially to the people taking part in the trial.

“The participation will generate vital evidence that could help save lives. Vaccines alone will not end this outbreak, but they could become a powerful new tool for bringing it under control.”

open image in gallery Four vaccines are currently in development for the Bundibugyo strain of the virus ( Getty/iStock )

Antibody drugs

1. The WHO has recommended prioritising privately held Mapp Biopharmaceutical's pan-ebolavirus antibody drug, MBP134 – a combination of two human monoclonal antibodies – for clinical trials among confirmed BDBV cases.

Initially studied for the Sudan ebolavirus strain, the drug was found to be safe and well tolerated in early-stage trials. Development has been backed by the U.S. Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority, or BARDA.

BARDA said it is coordinating shipments of the investigational treatment for potential use in high-risk Americans exposed to the virus.

Mapp said MBP134 has shown similar activity against all known ebolaviruses and that it is working with the WHO and other authorities as part of the response to the Congo outbreak.

2. Regeneron Pharmaceuticals' antibody drug candidate, maftivimab, is also being explored as a potential treatment by the WHO. According to the company, it has been shown in a lab to be active against the Bundibugyo Ebolavirus.

Regeneron said it is working to prepare existing supply of maftivimab for use in upcoming clinical trials, after having been recommended for study as a monotherapy.

open image in gallery Ituri military governor Lieutenant-General Johnny Luboya Nkashama (left), Congolese Minister of Communication and Media Patrick Muyaya Katembwe (centre), and Congolese Minister of Public Health Roger Kamba (right) address the media during a press briefing on Ebola response operations ( Getty )

The FDA has approved a combination of maftivimab and two other antibodies, atoltivimab and odesivimab, under the brand name Inmazeb, to treat Zaire Ebolavirus infection in adult and pediatric patients.

The company said, in September 2025, it donated 500 doses of Inmazeb to the WHO, which could be used if found helpful.

"Supply of Inmazeb is already on the ground in the DRC, should WHO wish to utilizs it for immediate treatment or as an additional component of the study," Regeneron said.

3. Human monoclonal antibodies isolated from Bundibugyo survivors have also been explored as potential treatments.

One candidate, BDBV289-N, demonstrated efficacy in a 2018 animal study. The study, conducted by a group of researchers with support from the US National Institutes of Health, showed the antibody gave up to 100 per cent protection in infected monkeys, even when treatment started up to eight days after the infection.

Antiviral drugs

Gilead Sciences' experimental oral antiviral drug obeldesivir is being considered as a potential post-exposure treatment by the WHO to prevent those exposed to Ebola from developing the disease.

Once-daily obeldesivir given for 10 days provided up to 100 per cent protection in monkeys against the Zaire and Sudan Ebola strains when treatment began 24 hours after exposure.

"Obeldesivir is predicted to be active against this particular (Bundibugyo) strain. While not approved for this, we do have preclinical data that shows positive results," a company spokesperson said.

Gilead's antiviral remdesivir has shown activity against the Bundibugyo virus in laboratory studies conducted by researchers at the University of Texas Medical Branch. Some data suggest the drug, given as an intravenous infusion, may have stronger activity against BDBV than against the Zaire Ebola strain.

Researchers in the DRC began enrolling participants in a trial testing the experimental antiviral drug in early July.

Congo’s National Institute for Biomedical Research and France’s ANRS Emerging Infectious Diseases – with support from humanitarian aid groups, Alliance for International Medical Action (ALIMA) and Medecins Sans Frontieres – continue to lead the trial in Ituri province, the epicentre of the outbreak.

The WHO has also recommended a combination therapy using a monoclonal antibody and remdesivir for evaluation.

Tests

News.title: Move over doomscrolling — everyone is hopescrolling after the blue wave
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

The midterm elections have left millions of Democrats across the country feeling hopeful for the first time in a long time, resulting in a flurry of internet activity.

Celebratory messages and memes captured the jubilant mood among Democratic voters, resulting in what’s been deemed “hopescrolling.” The trend emerged virtually overnight as Democrats took back the House and the Senate, in direct contrast to doomscrolling, the constant consumption of negative content.

Online users posted videos of newly elected leaders giving speeches overlaid with text reading “hopescrolling,” while others shared the term in blue wording on a simple blue background, signifying the color of the Democratic Party.

Mental health expert Matt Grammer has told The Independent that hopescrolling can be a good way for voters to relieve stress after a political cycle.

“Reading positive posts can be a good way to engage with others and take a mental break from stressful posts. There is nothing bad with appreciating a good post,” said Grammer.

It’s not entirely different from “bloomscrolling,” which puts a positive spin on doomscrolling by encouraging social media users to curate their feeds around uplifting, positive content.

Social media users have felt and shared the impacts of hopescrolling, with one person writing on Instagram, “Hope scrolling. For real tho. I can’t even describe some of the weight I’ve been carrying lifting.”

“What is this feeling!? Could it be…hope?” another commented as someone else said, “Right! What a strange new feeling.”

While it feels good to reshare these positive posts and inspiring speeches of newly elected officials, there can be downsides to relying on the internet for those warm fuzzy feelings.

“Feeling hope is a more complicated human experience. Experiences through the lens of social media tend to be short, but intense,” psychotherapist Dipesh Patel told The Independent.

open image in gallery ‘Hopescrolling can be a good way to relieve stress after a political cycle,’ one mental health expert said ( Alamy/PA )

Grammer warns that hopescrolling can lead to someone being in an echo chamber, where one person’s beliefs are repeatedly reinforced by internal communication.

He said: “Hopescrolling becomes bad when it turns into a way to seek reassurance. One of the most dangerous side effects is that it can make users think that because they see a lot of positive posts, that means that everyone shares that optimism and that all negative consequences of this election will go away.”

Psychotherapist Dr. Aditi Bhalla also warned not to be fooled by the algorithm, which is essentially designed to keep you active on your respective social media apps.

“It’s still a feed designed to keep you scrolling, and that keeps your body in a busy, switched-on state. Part of you keeps chasing the next little reward, and part of you stays on alert, checking that you’re not missing something,” said Bhalla.

Still, Grammer said that hopescrolling “can be a good way to engage with others and take a mental break.”

“I think that hopescrolling will be a short-term feature that people engage with,” he continued. “Hopefully it will create a way for people to share positive thoughts with each other.”

News.title: Budget cuts and ministerial churn has weakened aid spending transparency, report finds
News.content:
The UK has become less transparent in how it spends its aid budget, amid repeated cuts and ministerial turnover, according to a new report.

The 2026 Aid Transparency Index, the world’s only independent peer-reviewed assessment on aid transparency evaluates how well major donors, development banks, and UN agencies disclose their spending and activity data. In the latest ranking the UK’s transparency score fell 13.9 points from “very good” to “good”.

The Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) lost points for its lack of “comprehensive forward-looking country and organisational budgets and strategies, and project objectives”.

Twenty of the 33 ranked international organisations, over 60 per cent, scored “good” or “very good”, with just three rated “poor” or “very poor”. Germany, the US and the UK gave over 40 per cent of all overseas development aid in 2025, yet all three saw their transparency scores fall, according to the index.

“It’s not like [the FCDO] made a conscious decision to do anything badly or to miss anything… Our gut feeling is they’ve just taken their eye off the ball,” said Gary Forster, CEO of Publish What You Fund, a global campaign for aid and development transparency, which published the index.

“The FCDO hasn’t had a meaningful strategy since 2023,” he told The Telegraph.

For over two decades, the Department for International Development (DFID) operated as its own cabinet level ministry after it was set up in 1997 by Tony Blair, then Labour prime minister. In 2020, Conservative prime minister Boris Johnson merged it with the Foreign Office to create the FCDO.

The responsibility for aid was downgraded from a secretary of state to a minister of state position. Even then, there has been rapid ministerial turnover, with four international development ministers in the past two years.

The UK’s development budget, which funds programmes to tackle poverty and is a lifeline to millions around the world, has been repeatedly cut in recent years.

The UK historically prided itself on committing to spend 0.7 per cent of Gross National Income (GNI) on Official Development Assistance (ODA). In 2020 that figure was cut to 0.5 per cent and last year, Sir Keir Starmer, former prime minister, cut the target to 0.3 per cent of GNI.

News.title: Emery endures heaviest European defeat as Villa manager to old foes Barcelona
News.content:
“[Barcelona] have [Lamine] Yamal. He is a special player. You can see in him as a player who could end up being the best. He needs a few things but he could end up being a great player. Rodri gives personality to the team. They have [Anthony] Gordon giving them speed and hard work. They have Pedri or Fermin [Lopez] as offensive midfielders.”

Barcelona started strongly in the Champions League, winning their first two games, but lost 4-2 at defending champions PSG last time out. They warmed up for this match with an emphatic 6-1 win over Alaves in La Liga on Saturday. That victory gives them a two-point lead at the summit of La Liga.

“We know that at this level, anything can happen,” Barcelona boss Hansi Flick said. “Against Real Madrid, the result could have been different. These are special matches, but we are staying confident. It is normal to focus more on our last two defeats, but I have confidence in my team, which showed it again on Saturday. Now, we are focused on the Champions League, with the goal of finishing in the top eight. For me, he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world and he has reaped extraordinary successes. His team’s style of play is clear and very well organised. Just look at how they execute set pieces; it is something impressive. Their confidence in themselves is unmatched. It will be a tough match against a great team and a great coach.”

Team news from Nou Camp to follow shortly.

News.title: Man Utd show fight on night of chaos to give Carrick a glimpse of hope
News.content:
So maybe there is some fight left in the old dog yet?

At half-time, Manchester United looked down and out and Michael Carrick’s reign as manager as good as finished.

Roma were 2-0 in front and coasting, gorging on a desperate United’s litany of errors, and there was full-scale mutiny in the stands at Old Trafford. A fifth defeat in six matches and the club’s longest winless run for 48 years beckoned. It was toxic on and off the pitch.

And then something changed. United, from being a dishevelled, disorganised mess, suddenly seemed to remember who they were supposed to be and what they were supposed to represent. Surrender gave way to fight. A team that had been feeling sorry for themselves discovered some pride. A crowd that had been baying for blood turned Old Trafford into a bear pit of a very different kind, and Roma simply did not know what had hit them.

This club have served up some famous comebacks over the decades, but it was hard to think of too many occasions when the mood and momentum had shifted this violently from one half to the next.

United fans were in open revolt in that first half, releasing green and gold balloons in protests before kick-off and then throwing tennis balls on to the pitch amid furious chanting against the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe. The players looked like they would rather have been anywhere else.

News.title: Gabonese TikTokers fight back against toxic skin lightening products
News.content:
There is a buzz among the pupils at Nzeng-Ayong 2 primary school in Libreville, the capital of Gabon. At least among those who use TikTok. Black Choco is here: social media personality, entrepreneur, and a bona fide celebrity. With the fervour of a revivalist preacher, she takes over the lesson. Today’s topic is kwandza, the Gabonese term for skin-lightening.

“Is kwandza good? No! It’s like pouring boiling water on your skin. And we don’t do that, do we?”

Why do people want to become white, she asks the pupils – boys and girls between eight and 12 – before answering the question herself.

“To please other people! Aren’t you proud of your skin? Our skin is our identity!”

She asks a handful of pupils to stand up. “Look at them! Aren’t they beautiful with their dark skin? Let them hear it!”

“Gloire, you are beautiful,” the whole class chants.

News.title: Newcastle fans turn on Jaissle as defeat triggers relegation concerns
News.content:
Newcastle United did not just lose to Everton, they lost the home crowd, whose enthusiasm to back their team has drained from them at alarming speed.

This was a performance that belonged in the pre-takeover era, those bad old days under Steve McClaren, John Carver and Steve Bruce. It was a hugely satisfying evening for Everton manager David Moyes, who insisted there was “a way back” for Jack Grealish, even though he was once again left at home after he missed training last week without permission.

The atmosphere went flat early and gradually turned into anger and frustration. The crowd initially tried to stay with their team but were repeatedly punched in the face by the grim reality of the spectacle in front of them. They do not like the style of play, they do not like the application of the players and they cannot accept the results. They are fed up with pretending otherwise.

This was another miserable performance from Matthias Jaissle’s side, who did not manage a shot on target until the 86th minute. He has only been in the job three months, but nothing seems to be getting better.

News.title: US dairy worker dies from bird flu as outbreak rages in cattle
News.content:
“People at greater risk include dairy workers and others who have close or prolonged contact with infected animals or environments contaminated with the virus. Transmission of avian influenza between humans is extremely rare and has never been documented in the United States. Public health officials are continuing to monitor individuals who had close contact with the patient for symptoms,” the health district said in a statement.

Experts say the US bird flu outbreak is not only costing the dairy industry millions of dollars but also raises the risk that the virus could mutate to spread more easily between mammals. They are also concerned that authorities are doing little to check the spread.

Marc Johnson, a virologist at the University of Missouri, told the Telegraph last week that the outbreak in dairy cattle was “completely preventable”.

“Cattle infections last only a few weeks before the animals recover. If infected herds were simply isolated until the outbreak fizzled out, it would stop.

“But cattle keep being moved around, spreading it into new states,” said Dr Johnson, referring to the way the US dairy industry operates, in which cows are routinely transported across state lines, whether to join new herds, for breeding, or to replace animals at large milk-producing operations.

A bird flu outbreak has also been raging on a mink farm in Utah for the last couple of months, according to news outlet ProPublica.

Jonathan Ball, professor of molecular virology at the Liverpool School of Tropical Medicine, said allowing a virus to rage unchecked raises the risk of it mutating.

“Viruses like influenza are constantly exploring new hosts, and more often than not, it burns out. It’s not quite got the right combination of genetic changes to allow it to efficiently infect, efficiently replicate, and then efficiently transmit to the new host. But the longer these steps - adaptive changes, so genetic changes - are happening in these sporadic outbreaks, the more likelihood you’ve got of it mutating. It’s a bit like a one-armed bandit machine - if you keep pulling that handle, eventually you’re going to get three cherries,” he said.

News.title: First ever trial of long-acting injection against malaria to launch in Africa
News.content:
Dr Cristina Donini, executive vice-president of research and development at MMV, said the compound would be “complementary” to existing tools, rather than replacing them.

“The vaccine is doing a fantastic job in infants but if you could add onto that another tool that can cover a broader population with a longer regimen then we would be in a very good position to eliminate the disease,” she said.

Children in malaria-endemic regions are already given prophylactic drugs during the malaria season and studies have shown that these combined with the vaccine are highly effective. However, resistance has developed to these drugs and they have to be given monthly.

The malaria season in Africa varies by region but usually peaks after periods of rainfall. If the season lasts longer than three to four months it’s likely that people would need two injections. However, Dr Donini and her colleagues are working on a second generation LAI which they hope would provide year-long coverage.

Full costs have not yet been worked out but Dr Donini said affordability was an important factor in assessing the LAI’s suitability.

“It’s too early to say whether it will be cheaper than an injection - hopefully, yes. The beauty of it is that if you simplify it and decrease the number of injections needed you decrease the cost,” she said.

LAIs are gaining traction in the fight against infectious diseases - Lenacapavir, now being rolled out after being approved in 2025, provides almost 100% protection against infection from HIV and many believe it could help end the HIV pandemic. There are also LAI candidates in development for the prevention of tuberculosis, treatment and prevention of which usually relies on daily pills being taken over many months.

Lottie Renwick, global campaign director at Malaria No More UK, welcomed the launch of the trial.

“Thanks to sustained investment in malaria science including here in the UK, we are now on the brink of a number of breakthroughs which could turn the tide on the fight against the disease. And the long-acting injectable, specifically, could be a valuable addition to this toolbox as it has the potential to provide sustained protection from a single shot, avoiding the need for repeat doses.

“This phase of the trial also builds on earlier research conducted in the UK, highlighting the importance of the UK’s ongoing role as a malaria science superpower and the value of continued investment in malaria R&D. We look forward to the trial progressing further and eagerly await the results.”

MATHEUS CUNHA has dodged a UEFA punishment after having to be escorted off the pitch against Roma.

The Brazilian came up with two crucial goals to complete United’s thrilling comeback at Old Trafford on Tuesday night.



His celebrations for the second finish, tucked home in the 86th-minute, saw him excitedly whip his shirt off as he ran towards the home fans, earning himself a yellow card.

That came back to bite him five minutes later when he dived in on Leonardo Balerdi, receiving a second yellow and a sending off in the first minute of injury time.



The 27-year-old watched the final moments of the contest while sitting on the pitchside advertising boards, and entered the field of play after the final whistle to celebrate with his team-mates.

But, fearing that he would fall foul of Uefa rules and incur more than the one-match ban he was already facing, Michael Carrick tried to guide the star into the tunnel.

The IFAB Laws of the Game state that players must leave “the vicinity of the field of play and the technical area” after being sent off.

That means Cunha was not allowed to enter the pitch again at full-time.

But Uefa have since confirmed that he will not face any punishment for his return to the field as it was not reported by officials at the time.

A Uefa spokesperson wrote: “The UEFA official reports did not mention anything about this incident.

“Therefore the automatic one-match ban following two yellow cards should not be extended for this reason. We are not investigating further this matter.”

While Cunha dodged any punishment from the organisers of the Champions League, he might have to explain himself in regard to his treatment of Carrick.

The forward was clearly fuming at being denied the chance to celebrate the win he was largely responsible for, and was seen arguing with his manager as he tried to usher him back down the tunnel.



He even appeared to shout something back towards the pitch while being escorted away by a club official.

The Minas Gerais Under-20 Championship saw Uberlandia take on Mamore with 43 players and eight members of staff sent off after a mass brawl which lasted for almost 40 minutes.

According to the Guinness Book of Records, the previous high was 36 after a brawl in a game between Atletico Claypole and Victoriano Arenas in the the fifth division of Argentine football.

Sports.title: Former Arsenal star who won two FA Cups retires aged 38 as he hangs up boots in emotional statement
Sports.content:
Next

ARSENAL hero David Ospina announced his retirement from football with an emotional message that led to some touching tributes from legendary team-mates.

Ospina, 38, was the Gunners’ No1 from 2014, when he moved to the Emirates from Nice after an impressive World Cup with Colombia, until 2019.



The famous goalkeeper helped the North Londoners win two FA Cup honours in 2015 and 2017 until his departure for Napoli, where he spent a year on loan before his permanent move to Italy.

After four years with the Serie A giants and another two with Al-Nassr, the Colombia legend returned to boyhood club Atletico Nacional where he decided to hang up his gloves.



Ospina posted the following message on Instagram along with a clip of his career’s greatest highlights: “To Football I say Thank You! Not giving up on me…… I will go where the smile takes me!”

A number of fellow legends took to the comments’ section to give him his flowers after an impressive 21-year career, such as superstar keeper Thibaut Courtois.

Courtois posted: “Congratulations on your career buddy! I wish you all the best in your new stage of life! A big hug.”

And many of Ospina’s iconic Colombia team-mates soon followed after the ex-Chelsea star.

James Rodriguez wrote: “You are a great No1! Thank you for the joys and for your exemplary career. Proud to know this great human being I feel privileged to be able to call you BROTHER.

“We have fought together, laughed together, cried together! Many battles, I wish you the best in this new stage of your life. I love you.”



Juan Cuadrado added: “Excellent, my boss and leader. An honour to have shared so many battles together. You made history. Blessings for what’s to come.”

Luis Diaz commented: “What an honour and privilege to have shared the dressing room with you, brother.

“Beyond a great goalkeeper you are an amazing human being. Thank you so much David. You will always be an example to everyone.”

And Radamel Falcao stated: “Dear friend, it has been an honour to share with you part of this journey.. I wish you the best in what is coming for your life. Big Hug!”



Ospina amassed a total of 70 appearances with Arsenal and 131 caps with Colombia.

CHELSEA’S Moroccan Messi made an instant impact – but could not stop the Blues’ kids suffering European humiliation.

Ibrahim Rabbaj, 17, the diminutive winger compared to Argentina legend Lionel Messi, scored barely a minute after his half-time introduction to restore the Blues’ lead against Estonia’s Flora Tallinn.



Yet the visitors rallied to beat their Premier League opponents 3-2 and send Chelsea crashing out of the Uefa Youth League 5-4 on aggregate.

Blues manager Xabi Alonso, star player Cole Palmer and legendary captain John Terry were all watching as Flora sprang a shock to match Fleetwood’s Carabao Cup win over Arsenal.



A number of the Estonian players – including 14-YEAR-OLD Denis Zotov – have senior experience in their country’s top tier.

And by the end it felt like men against boys as Zotov won the penalty from which Flora first-team star Sander Alamaa scored the winner – his fourth strike across the two legs.



Chelsea are absent from all senior European competition this season after the disastrous 2025-6 campaign.

Now the Blues’ Under-19 side has fallen at the first hurdle of their bid to reach the knockout stages of the youth equivalent of the Champions League.

Harry Hudson’s Blues were hot favourites to go through to the next round after having two players sent off in the 2-2 first-leg draw in Tallinn.

But they followed up that ill-disciplined display with a lacklustre home performance – despite a brilliant start.

Winger Mathis Eboue, son of former Arsenal star Emmanuel, scored after just a minute and a half.

Released by Chizzy Ezenwata’s header, Eboue, 18, stood his man up, took a touch out of his feet and hit a firm left-foot shot across the Flora goalkeeper and into the net.

But a terrible mistake by Blues centre back Alfie Osborne gifted Flora a 17th-minute equaliser.

Osborne failed to deal with a long clearance and was robbed by Alamaa, who beat home goalkeeper Freddy Bernal.

Chelsea were mediocre for the rest of the half and boss Hudson took action.



Off came Osborne and on came Rabbaj into a more conventional 4-2-3-1 formation.

Straightaway, a fine pass by Reggie Watson, 16, son of Wigan FA Cup final hero Ben, found Eboue on the left.

With just under 15 minutes left, Blues captain Olutayo Subuloye fouled Zotov in the box. Up stepped Alamaa, 18, to bury the spotkick.



Hudson threw on attacking players and Andrew Pennie had an effort cleared off the line.

But Chelsea could not stop Flora claiming a famous win.

In the restructured Uefa Youth League, Under-19 teams from all 36 clubs in senior Champions League compete in a league format.

The top 22 youth sides go through to the knockout stages.



Meanwhile domestic youth champions from other leagues compete to be one of the 10 teams to join them in the last 32.

Estonian winners Flora beat HK, of the Faeroe Islands, 7-1 in the first round.

Chelsea, as winners of the Premier League Under-18 title last season, went straight into the second round.

And straight out of the competition after deservedly being beaten by Flora.

Next

KASPER SCHMEICHEL has implored Manchester United fans to get behind their team more.

The former Premier League-winning goalkeeper – who is also the son of United legend Peter Schmeichel – insists he understands why fans are protesting against the ownership at Old Trafford.



But the Dane also believes those very protests are not helping the current crop of players on the pitch.

Boss Michael Carrick got a much-needed victory with a hard-fought, comeback win over Roma in the Champions League this week.



It was the club’s first win in 10 games and with two tricky fixtures looming, Kasper thinks the fans need to give the team all the support they can.

He said on BBC Radio 5 Live: “I’d still be very tentative, particularly considering your next two games are Aston Villa and Liverpool. That’s a tough ask even if you’re on a good run.



“If you want to force a change, you have to a little bit get on the bandwagon to promote the positivity.

“I like that the fans, they stayed. They could have gone at half time and been frustrated and missed the traffic, but I like the fact that they stayed.

“And once the first goal went in, that was enough to create the atmosphere. Now the fans have their chance to influence what’s going on on the pitch for the next game. Now they have the chance to go and back it up.

“I completely get wanting to protest and all of that, but like I say, for the players, it just doesn’t help.

STEVEN GERRARD has emerged as a potential candidate to take charge of Wrexham amid growing pressure on manager Phil Parkinson.

The Liverpool legend is reportedly open to replacing Parkinson, whose future has come under scrutiny following the Welsh club’s disappointing start to the Championship season.



Wrexham sit 18th in the table after suffering a 1-0 defeat to Sheffield United on Friday, leaving them eight points adrift of the play-off places and just five clear of the relegation zone.

According to talkSPORT, ambitious Hollywood owners Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney are considering their options after setting their sights on promotion to the Premier League this season.



However, any decision to part company with Parkinson would be a difficult one given his remarkable achievements since taking charge in 2021.

The 58-year-old has guided Wrexham from the National League to the Championship, overseeing three consecutive promotions and transforming the club’s fortunes.

His success has earned him enormous respect from Reynolds and McElhenney, who are understood to have effectively promised him a job for life.

But the arrival of sporting director Steve Nickson has brought a fresh perspective, with chief executive Michael Williamson and director Shaun Harvey also expected to have a say in any managerial decision.

Back-to-back defeats against Blackburn and Sheffield United have increased concerns behind the scenes, with the club now reportedly drawing up contingency plans.

SLOVAN BRATISLAVA manager Yaya Touré hit a brutal milestone with a 14th consecutive Champions League loss.

A 4-0 defeat to LASK in Austria on Tuesday extended a run in the competition’s main phase which extends back to 1992.



Marseille held the previous record with 13 losses between March 2012 and November 2020.

The all-time record of 16 from the old European Cup is the next mark, with Jeunesse Esch of Luxembourg having the dubious honour at the moment.



Manchester City icon Touré, who took the job in June, is the first African manager in the competition’s history and a previous winner from his time at Barcelona in 2009.

The 43-year-old said: “It’s very difficult, to be honest.

Slovan have lost four games this season with upcoming home clashes against Real Betis and Shakhtar Donetsk a chance to avoid more unwanted history.

Two more defeats would see them equal Jeunesse, who drew 1-1 with Liverpool in September 1973 to snap a streak.

Worryingly, Slovan are at risk of not qualifying for next season’s competition.

Touré’s team are eight points behind Slovakian league leaders FC Dac.

He added: “It’s not easy, but the season is long.

Touré was a highly-decorated player and is climbing the rung as a manager.



He served as an assistant manager at Ukraine‘s Olimpik Donetsk, Akhmat Grozny in Russia and Belgian outfit Standard Liege.

Fans get golden chance to buy 2022 World Cup trophy lifted by Lionel Messi

Lionel Messi finally lifted the famous trophy in 2022 after he guided Argentina to World Cup glory in Qatar - with fans now able to purchase a replica at auction

View 3 Images Argentina won the FIFA World Cup in 2022 (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The replica World Cup trophy carried by Lionel Messi after Argentina's victory in 2022 will go under the hammer as part of an exclusive auction.

‌



‌



The replica will headline the inaugural Sports Memorabilia Auction by Richmond Auctions on 7 November, with one of sport's most iconic pieces up for grabs.

‌



The trophy was carried onto the pitch by the legendary Messi after one of the greatest finals ever played, with the Argentinian scoring twice to fire his country to a third global triumph despite Kylian Mbappé netting a hat-trick for France.

‌



As the celebrations rolled on long after the final whistle, the replica made its way from the stands into the players’ hands and was passed from champion to champion for 45 minutes during their on-pitch celebrations.

Patrick Stewart snubbed Cristiano Ronaldo to fulfil wife's Lionel Messi wish READ MORE :

UEFA make Matheus Cunha decision after Man Utd star returned to pitch despite red card READ MORE :

It went on to star in many of the most widely shared images from that night, including Messi lifting and kissing it - a picture that, nearly four years on, remains the most liked in Instagram's history.

Before the night was over, the replica was also signed by eight members of the victorious squad, with the item’s proof of provenance referencing players including Lautaro Martínez, Leandro Paredes, Guido Rodríguez and Ángel Di María, who scored Argentina’s second goal in the final.

‌



View 3 Images Messi finally lifted the game's biggest prize in 2022

Jordan Richmond, Founder of Richmond Auctions, said: “Some objects tell the story of a sporting moment; very few were physically part of it. This replica started life as one supporter’s tribute and ended up at the heart of one of the greatest nights football has ever seen, passed from player to player and lifted by one of the greatest players of all time. To launch our first Sports Memorabilia Auction with a piece carrying that kind of history is a real privilege, and we expect strong interest from football collectors all over the world."

‌



The auction will take place on Saturday 7 November 2026 at 4:00pm GMT (11:00am ET). Alongside the replica, included in the same lot will be a 2022 Panini Instant Lionel Messi #118 FIFA World Cup Qatar/PSA 10 GEM MINT, creating a unique connection between the collectible card and the moment it commemorates. The card captures Lionel Messi celebrating Argentina’s victory over France, holding the replica World Cup trophy, and represents a long-awaited milestone in his legendary career.

View 3 Images The Panini trading card also up for auction

‌



The sale itself features a further 363 lots, from rare trading cards to signed memorabilia spanning basketball, baseball and American football. Other highlights include a 1952 Topps Mickey Mantle, one of the most sought-after cards in the hobby, and a Michael Jordan autograph card from Upper Deck's 2001-02 Buybacks set, numbered 1 of just 10.

Richmond Auctions is a US-based auction house specialising in rare, investment-grade advertising and automotive collectibles. The November sale marks its first move into dedicated sports memorabilia.

"Will Lankshear is as good a finisher as I've seen since Alan Shearer".

If you've started to hear the hype around Middlesbrough's record £20m striker, get ready for even more.

England manager Thomas Tuchel is reportedly sending one of his scouts to see if Lankshear can add to his 13 goals in 13 Championship games against Wrexham on Wednesday night, with Friday's England squad an outside possibility.

Pundits are already queuing up to make classic number 9 comparisons, with veteran EFL manager Neil Warnock heaping praise on the 21-year-old's "unbelievable, special finishing".

‌



Lankshear, who has 15 goals for Boro in all competitions this season, also scored on his England Under 21s debut in September.

And his Tottenham origins, predatory goalscoring instincts, and humble, hard-working personality are allowing commentators to make the obvious Harry Kane references.

How Michael Carrick channelled Sir Alex Ferguson to turn around 'embarrassing' Man Utd display READ MORE :

The lack of up and coming English forwards behind Kane has been an issue for years. Can Lankshear jump the queue and gatecrash Tuchel's Euro 2028 plans?

‌



'Baffling decision for Spurs to sell Lankshear'

Football London's Tottenham correspondent Alasdair Gold has described Spurs' decision to sell Lankshear as "baffling" and expects him to pass the 20-goal mark "within weeks".

Gold makes the stark contrast to Tottenham's underperforming forwards and says Boro fans must be "laughing at their fortune".

In fact, since joining the Boro, Lankshear has only scored one fewer goal than Tottenham have as a whole team.

Tottenham sporting director Johan Lange made the decision to cash in on Lankshear in the summer - reportedly £8-10m up front and the rest in add-ons.

‌



Gold said: "Lankshear's second goal in the victory against Charlton was reminiscent of a certain Ballon d'Or winner he looked up to in training.

"He will become a very good Premier League striker and it's mind-boggling that Spurs did not simply loan out a player who was not desperate to leave permanently, or even heaven-forbid, give him a chance to prove himself."

However, Gold says the north London club have matching rights on any future offers for Lankshear as well as a 20% sell-on clause that would benefit them regardless of whether they or another club signs him down the line. It is against the rules to have a buy-back clause with EFL clubs so that not an option.

'He had offers from bigger clubs'

After Middlesbrough manager Kim Hellberg arrived in November 2025, no team created more chances in the Championship - but no team in the Championship missed more big chances either. They needed an elite finisher to go again for Premier League promotion.

‌



In the summer, Hellberg, head of football Kieran Scott and head of recruitment Chris Jones drew up their transfer shortlist, with Lankshear described by one insider as a "dream" target.

The Spurs man had been a long-term target for Boro after they tracked his progress for many years. They tried to sign him in January, but he opted to honour his loan at Oxford.

Scott told Teesside Live: “We have to use our sales pitch. Someone like Will for example, he has a burning desire to be in the Premier League and play at the top level.

“I don't want to embarrass the lad but he had several opportunities that were financially a lot more rewarding for him. I would argue that some clubs were bigger because they were playing in Europe.

‌



“But he bought into this, really liked what we were about. He saw himself as a No.9 here and he's about feel. He gets a good feel Will, and the more time I spent with him you realise he's not flash, he's not looking for the biggest and best training ground."

Everyone at Boro has been blown away by just how successful he’s been so far.

‌



A one-touch finish expert

Lankshear's instinct in the penalty area is ‘elite’ already.

That might feel like a big claim given he’s only playing in the Championship, but that trait doesn’t really matter what division you’re in. Lankshear just has that knack of being in the right place at the right time, as shown by the fact that 10 of his 13 league goals have been one-touch finishes.

‌



Coaches I’ve spoken to say that instinct is hard to teach. Lankshear just has it.

Hellberg is a coach who focuses massively on individual development.

‌



Lankshear has yet to register an assist this season, and Hellberg has spoken a lot about working on other sides of Lankshear's game, in terms of his pressing and his back-to-goal stuff.

And it’s not just on the pitch where Lankshear has impressed. People behind the scenes at Boro talk of a young lad who’s mature and has his head screwed on, but is also humble too.

‌



He’s also said to be a really driven character, and obsessed with improving all the time. A typical centre forward, Hellberg and his team-mates have joked about his intensity in front of goal in training.

Hellberg added: "He even celebrates if he scores a small goal on a possession drill - he still celebrates all his goals with a fist. I think that's why he scores so many goals. Even if he touches the ball very few times in a game.

‌



"He's come here and is taking a massive development through the season. I think he was top from the first day in the box and how he finished, but he has increased his quality in the run-and-turn game.

"It comes from massive pressing. He has taken big steps, and he works so hard every day to improve, and that's what's taking him here. But at the end of the day, also having fantastic teammates that set it up in a brilliant way helps.

Team-mate Riley McGree jokes: “In training he loses his head when he doesn't finish and score! It's really good to see, because I can relate to that as well.”

This is a young player that’s been compared to fellow former Tottenham striker Harry Kane for many years. Even moving to Boro for a record fee brought with it attention and therefore pressure.

‌



He’s handled everything so far with class and maturity. Let's see what happens next.

Sports.title: Gianni Infantino chosen for bonfire effigy as FIFA chief could be grilled on Trump links
Sports.content:
Gianni Infantino chosen for bonfire effigy as FIFA chief could be grilled on Trump links

Gianni Infantino is clinging onto his position as FIFA president ahead of his re-election bid in March, but he remains the firing line following a series of controversies

View 2 Images Donald Trump and Gianni Infantino worked closely (Image: Tasos Katopodis - FIFA/FIFA via Getty Images)

FIFA president Gianni Infantino has been selected as this year's effigy for an annual bonfire in Kent. The Edenbridge Bonfire Society unveiled Infantino's cartoon effigy ahead of their celebrations on Thursday.

‌



‌



The society explained that he'd been chosen for his 'string of decisions that have left their mark on the world of football in the wake of the World Cup'. Previous celebrity targets have included former UK Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer and US President Donald Trump, whose face is part the effigy.

‌



Infantino worked closely with Trump during the US-held Club World Cup in 2025 and this year's international edition. The FIFA chief could now face questions over his links to the Commander-in-Chief after the Democrat Party seized control of Congress at the midterm elections in the US.

‌



In July, Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee confirmed that they'd launched an investigation into a 'sustained campaign' by FIFA and Infantino to curry favour with Trump. They also requested that Infantino submit documents and appear before the Committee.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



A spokeswoman for the Committee Democrats then said in September that Infantino and FIFA's level of co-operation with the investigation had been 'woefully inadequate'. The spokeswoman for the Committee Democrats also said on September 23 that staff had received a briefing on litigation relating to the FIFA bribery scandal.

She added: "FIFA has yet to turn over any priority documents requested by the committee - including those that would show how much money FIFA has given the Trump family - answer key questions around the awarding of the FIFA Peace Prize or explain how the Kushner-Infantino scheme to sell off the World Cup was conceived."

‌



Two days after the Committee's investigation was launched, on July 28, The Times reported Infantino was developing a plan to sell stakes in a company, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), to private investors.

Later the same day, FIFA confirmed the proposal was that FFE should run the commercial interests of the World Cup and other FIFA competitions, and that the leader of the private investor group would be Thrive Capital. Thrive was founded by Joshua Kushner, the brother of President Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner.

‌



Should Gianni Infantino resign? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino is this year's bonfire effigy in Kent (Image: Gareth Fuller/Press Association)

‌



The FFE plan was rejected by three continental confederations, including European football's governing body UEFA, which threatened to boycott FIFA tournaments unless the plan was abandoned. Infantino announced the idea had been withdrawn on August 1.

UEFA nevertheless said it had 'lost confidence' in Infantino over the affair and has pledged to identify a candidate to stand against him in next year's FIFA presidential election, though nothing has been announced so far with two weeks to go until the deadline for candidacies to be submitted.

‌



Infantino appears to have strong support for re-election in Africa, Asia, Oceania and South America. Campaign group FairSquare has called on national associations to challenge Infantino’s eligibility to stand for a fourth term.

FIFA's statutes say no person may serve as president for more than three terms, but on the eve of the 2022 World Cup final it was announced FIFA Council had taken the decision to discount Infantino's first term between 2016 and 2019, leaving him free to run again in 2027.

Sports.title: Matheus Cunha leaves Micah Richards and Jamie Carragher in stitches with Man Utd response
Sports.content:
Matheus Cunha leaves Micah Richards and Jamie Carragher in stitches with Man Utd response

Jamie Carragher, Kate Scott, Micah Richards and Thierry Henry interviewed Matheus Cunha live on CBS Sports after Manchester United's comeback win against Roma in the Champions League

View 2 Images Matheus Cunha made the CBS Sports studio laugh on Tuesday

Matheus Cunha made Jamie Carragher and Micah Richards burst out laughing midway through a live interview after Manchester United beat Roma in the Champions League. The forward scored twice in four minutes to complete the comeback victory at Old Trafford.

‌



‌



Cunha removed his shirt while running over to the home fans during his celebrations after the winning goal. He was issued a yellow card, then a second in added time, resulting in a red card, leaving United with ten men.

‌



However, he was still in high spirits after the match. Cunha spoke with Carragher, Kate Scott, Richards and Thierry Henry.

‌



The former Manchester City player asked Cunha about the celebration. He then focused on the impressive physique he showed off.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Richards said: "You're in good shape, eh? You been going to the gym?" Caught off guard, Cunha replied, "Yeah, I did," prompting laughter in the studio. "Thank you, thank you. My wife needs me to be good."

That comment elicited an even louder response, with Carragher's booming laugh heard and Richards left face down on the desk in stitches. The latter had to exhale audibly while attempting to compose himself as Scott took over the questioning and continued their interview.

‌



Cunha had earlier spoken at length about the emotion of his celebration. He said: "I think this is too much Brazilian, no? I think I always dreamed of having this celebration, to be honest.

View 2 Images Matheus Cunha was sent off after scoring twice for United (Image: CBS Sports)

‌



Make sure you don't miss the best Man Utd coverage by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

"When I went, I saw the fans. It was a bit tricky because it (the winning goal) was in front of the Roma fans' section.

‌



"Then I don't know if it's Roma fans or our fans, and then I felt like if I jump, 'oh my God, it will be tricky!' But yeah, I'm happy because they celebrated me, and it was a very beautiful moment."

Before the interview concluded, Cunha spoke about what comes next for United after their comeback. He said: "I think we need to change, no?

‌



"After this hard moment, we tried everything and nothing more than a night like today. Champions League and with a comeback, as we did.

"I think the second half was a real Manchester United team, with all the passion, all the duels - everything you can show on the pitch. I think we need to do more and more of these kinds of things, and I hope this will be a beautiful comeback for this season."

Sports.title: Forest Green Rovers cover changing room in houseplants following research discovery
Sports.content:
Forest Green Rovers cover changing room in houseplants following research discovery

Forest Green Rovers have collaborated with Plants & Flowers Foundation Holland to transform the high-pressure environment during Stress Awareness Week

View 2 Images Kairo Mitchell pictured during the changing room takeover by Plants & Flowers Foundation Holland at the world’s greenest football club, Forest Green Rovers, to highlight the wellbeing benefits of indoor plants for International Stress Awareness Week. (Image: imagecomms)

The ‘world’s greenest football club’ have transformed their dressing room with hundreds of plants to reduce anxiety and boost performances on the pitch.

‌



‌



Forest Green currently sit mid-table in the National League, England’s fifth tier, and recently saw high-profile manager Robbie Savage leave the club to join League One side Peterborough United. But the collaboration with Plants & Flowers Foundation Holland saw potted plants placed in the changing rooms at The New Lawn to transform the high-pressure environment during Stress Awareness Week in a bid to turn their fortunes around.

‌



Midfielder Oliver Ewing said: “I’ve never seen anything like it – it’s brilliant. I think everyone loves nature themselves, loves plants. It’s quite homey. The changing rooms can definitely be a very stressful environment, especially after a game if you’ve lost. I’ve been in many dressing rooms where it feels like there’s no place you would rather be than right here and now.

‌



“I know a lot of people use plants in their homes and daily lives to sort of release anxiety and this and that. Hopefully, it can get us a few wins but I think it already has a bit of a calming effect around the ground.”

Indeed, studies have found that interaction with indoor plants lowers nervous system activity, reduces mental fatigue and elevates positive moods. Forest Green Rovers are well known as the world ’s greenest club, implementing ideas such as serving exclusively vegan food, using recycled materials for their kits, and running their stadium in Nailsworth on 100% green electricity.

View 2 Images Akai Bonnick, Oli Ewing, Freddie Sass, Gabe Kircough, Jose Marquez pictured during the changing room takeover by Plants & Flowers Foundation Holland (Image: imagecomms)

‌



First team coach Yan Klukowski said: “I think as human beings, we have that innate piece of our makeup that brings a lot of calmness and decreases stress when you’re in the outdoors.

“So the more that people in general, not just footballers, get outside, get fresh air, and be in nature, I think that can only benefit people who move forward. Looking after mental health is incredibly important. I think that the psychological and physical side of the game go hand in hand.

‌



“We all know the psychological benefits of physical activity and how physical activity can make us feel from a mental health perspective, so they come hand in hand.

“We have to provide strategies to help our players cope with the high stress environment that we’re in. I think we do a good job of that here.”

Article continues below

Defender Gabe Kircough added: “People are more aware of it and it’s becoming easier to speak about it because of that awareness. It’s a huge thing in any walk of life, but professional sport as well, the intensity and the scrutiny on us as players and staff and anyone else working here.

“You want to create an environment where people are happy to be open and honest and speak about any problems they’ve got and are always checking on each other.”

Sports.title: Thousands of heartbroken Tenerife fans gather at vigil for tragic star Jesus de Miguel
Sports.content:
Tenerife fans gathered at the club's stadium on Tuesday night to pay tribute to Jesus de Miguel following his tragic death aged 30.

The Tenerife striker passed away in hospital after colliding with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono in a Spanish Segunda clash on Monday. Owono was sent off for the challenge, which left De Miguel motionless on the pitch and saw the game abandoned.

De Jesus suffered head and chest injuries. His condition was described as serious but stable on Monday night, but he passed away on Tuesday morning after his health deteriorated.

Spanish authorities have opened an investigation for possible involuntary manslaughter against Owono, who reportedly 'broke down' in the dressing room after the match. However, Santa Cruz de Tenerife chief prosecutor Jose Luis Sanchez-Jauregui has said that criminal proceedings against the 25-year-old were "very unlikely".

View 5 Images Tenerife has gone into a period of mourning for Jesus de Miguel (Image: Getty Images)

A minutes' silence was observed before Champions League matches across Europe on Tuesday night and will be repeated on Wednesday. And there were emotional scenes at Tenerife's ground, Estadio Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez, on Tuesday night as fans gathered to mourn De Jesus.

Supporters laid flowers, lit candles and left photos and messages for De Jesus. One message read: “Today the heart of Tenerife is in mourning. It’s hard to find words when someone who has been part of our history leaves too soon.”

Another fan wrote: “Your departure hurts us. It hurts us to think that we will no longer see you defend this shirt, that there will be no more celebrations, more hugs or more shared moments.”

View 5 Images Fans lit candles and left flowers for Jesus de Miguel (Image: Getty Images)

It came as the club announced six days of mourning, which will see all activities suspended as a mark of respect. De Jesus' funeral will take place in Navahermosa, Toledo, with all of his teammates attending, along with club staff.

Tenerife invited fans to gather at the stadium on Saturday evening for "a solemn tribute". They added: "The family of Jesus de Miguel is grateful for each and every expression of support received, and also requests, from the bottom of their hearts, the utmost respect for their privacy during these terrible times."

"We are torn by the news," Fran Leon, president of Tenerife's federation of supporters' clubs, told the BBC. "All of the island is in mourning. All of Canarias is in mourning. It's a shared pain."

View 5 Images There was a huge amount of emotion at the gathering on Tuesday evening (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

De Jesus joined Tenerife from Castellon in 2025 on a three-year contract. He contributed 11 goals and seven assists in 35 appearances for the club.

Tenerife midfielder Juanjo Sanchez wrote on social media: "You let me into your heart, and you earned a place in mine, as we shared moments of laughter every single day and took walks barefoot after our training sessions.

"I cannot let this moment pass without highlighting what a wonderful person you are. You never had an unkind word or a sour expression for anyone, and you always displayed exemplary conduct, despite all the challenges you faced. You will always be with me, my friend."

View 5 Images A minute of silence was observed for Jesus de Miguel before Tuesday's Champions League games (Image: Joan Valls/Getty Images)

"Thank you for everything we experienced together - for your camaraderie, your character, your humanity and the exemplary attitude you always showed," Tenerife striker Enric Gallego said. "I feel very fortunate to have shared a locker room with you. I'm going to miss you so much."

His death has been keenly felt across the footballing world, with Barcelona star Raphinha among those to pay tribute. "Today I don't want to talk about football," he said after scoring twice in Barca's 3-0 win over Aston Villa in the Champions League Tuesday night.

"I want to send a message to the family of Jesus - may he rest in peace. From the club, I want to send a message of strength to the family."

Lionel Messi, Cristiano Ronaldo and Spanish tennis legend Rafael Nadal were among those to post messages of support on social media.

Sports.title: Brady returns to Patriots as commentator for first time
Sports.content:
Tom Brady will make an emotional homecoming this weekend when he returns to New England as a broadcaster for the first time since retiring from football.

The seven-time Super Bowl champion will serve as colour commentator for Fox Sports at Gillette Stadium for the first time when the Patriots face the Green Bay Packers, live on Sky Sports NFL from 9.25pm.

Brady appeared at nine Super Bowls and won six across a historic 20-year career with the Patriots, accompanying Bill Belichick to forge one of the NFL's greatest dynasties.

"It'll be certainly emotional. I mean, every inch of that stadium, I've been through so many times.

"From the locker rooms to the media rooms to the field. Just so many memorable plays in that stadium. Big games, championship games and rivalry games, division-clinching games."

Brady, drafted with the 199th overall pick at the 2000 NFL Draft, won three MVP awards while passing for 74,571 yards and 541 touchdowns before leaving in 2019.

"And the Patriots just always seem to do things the right way."

The Patriots enter Sunday's game 5-3 and second in the AFC East as they strive to remain in Super Bowl contention after falling at the final hurdle against the Seattle Seahawks in February's season finale.

It awaits as a matchup of the two franchises with the winningest records in the NFL since the Packers beat the Patriots at Super Bowl XXXI at the end of the 1996 season. The Patriots have built a league-best record of 327-166 over the 30 years since that game, followed by Green Bay's regular-season return of 310-180-3.

New England won all six of their Super Bowls in that time and reached the playoffs in 22 of 30 years, while the Packers clinched two Championships and have also made the playoffs on 22 occasions in the last three decades.

Sports.title: Leicestershire's relegation confirmed as points deduction for 'poor' pitch stands
Sports.content:
Leicestershire's relegation to County Championship Division Two has been confirmed after the club's points deduction for breaching pitch regulations was upheld.

The Foxes were hit with a 27-point penalty, later cut to 19, after the surface at Grace Road was rated "poor" by the match referee following the win over Glamorgan in August.

Leicestershire, who argued the state of the pitch was due to the unscheduled shooting of a Bollywood film days before the Glamorgan fixture, had eight points from the original punishment of 27 reinstated but then appealed against the 19-point sanction.

However, the appeals panel supported the initial finding that the Midlanders had failed to act reasonably in preparing the wicket and, as a result, the club have slipped into the second tier of the Championship after finishing 17 points behind third-bottom Essex.

The panel rejected Leicestershire's attempt to introduce fresh evidence, presented by the Pakistan Cricket Board's chief curator Tony Hemmings, saying the "the club is the author of its own misfortune" and there appeared to be "a woeful lack of understanding" of regulations by those in charge.

Had the appeal been successful and Leicestershire awarded all of their points back, Essex would have joined bottom team Hampshire in going down to Division Two.

A section of the County Championship's playing conditions stipulates that teams charged with producing a pitch rated as poor or below average earn zero points from that particular game.

Leicestershire earned 19 points from the 42-run win over Glamorgan - 16 for the victory itself and a further three bonus points.

The club had said the filming of the Bollywood movie prevented the pitch from being covered for eight hours in heatwave temperatures.

Leicestershire have 'deep frustrations' over appeal process

Leicestershire chief executive Emma White said in a statement that the club "acknowledges and respects the conclusion of this process" but she also voiced "deep frustrations" that new evidence was not allowed to be presented.

Image: England spin-bowling all-rounder Rehan Ahmed is one of Leicestershire's key players

White wrote: "As part of our appeal, we sought to introduce fresh expert evidence from one of the world's leading curators. We were not permitted to do so.

"We firmly believe this evidence would have made a significant difference to the outcome, and it is deeply frustrating that it could not be heard.

"From the outset, the club felt rushed and under considerable pressure throughout this process."

White added: "Pitch regulations are vitally important. They exist to ensure fairness across our competition, and we fully support them.

"However, the club believes there is an opportunity to bring greater clarity and consistency to pitch inspections, ratings and the processes that follow.

"We recognise the challenges involved in assessing pitches and would welcome further dialogue with the Cricket Regulator and the ECB to help counties better understand how decisions are reached."

Image: Leicestershire lost their final match of the season to Championship winners Warwickshire

Leicestershire chief executive: We will not allow this to define us.

The Foxes - who finished runners-up to Middlesex in this season's One Day Cup - were playing in Division One of the County Championship for the first time since 2003 having won promotion by winning the second tier in 2025.

White added: "We are hugely disappointed by this outcome, but we will not allow it to define us.

"Our grounds team continues to have my full support, and I remain immensely proud of the work they do.

"Come pre-season, we will be ready to battle it out in Division Two, and to fight our way back."

Durham and Kent will take Leicestershire and Hampshire's spots in the top flight next season after finishing first and second respectively in Division Two in 2026.

Sports.title: Atherton: Lancashire did not handle Anderson release badly
Sports.content:
Michael Atherton sees no issue with Lancashire's handling of James Anderson's release from the county - but would have been tempted to hand the veteran seam bowler a new contract.

Anderson, 44, bagged 50 wickets at an average of 17.68 in the County Championship during a 2026 season in which Lancashire finished second bottom of Division Two under his captaincy.

Anderson was informed in a meeting with the Red Rose hierarchy that he would not be offered a new deal at a county he first represented in a first-class match in 2002, with new director of cricket Paul Farbrace wanting to build an attack for the future.

The decision came a little over two years after the fast bowler was retired by England against his wishes, with his final Test coming against West Indies at Lord's in July 2024.

Speaking on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast, alongside co-host in Nasser Hussain who had questioned the way Lancashire dispensed with Anderson's services, Atherton said: "I think you can argue about the merits of the decision as he was Lancashire's best bowler by a country mile last season.

"Forget age, young or old, if you are good enough, you are good enough, so you can make a perfectly good argument he should still be leading that Lancashire attack.

"Where I disagree with some of the comment elsewhere is that it has not been handled well, both by England and Lancashire.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Talking on the 'For the Love of Cricket' podcast, Stuart Broad called Lancashire's decision not to renew Anderson's contract was 'disrespectful' (Credit: For the Love of Cricket)

"When somebody like Paul Farbrace comes in as director of cricket at Lancashire, or in England's case Rob Key, when they've decided to move on, how do you do that?

"In both instances, Anderson was told face-to-face. It wasn't done behind his back. Jimmy wasn't expecting [his Lancashire release], it took him by surprise, but it was face-to-face.

"They told him the rationale and then when the members meeting was held, I think Farbrace was abroad, but he dialled in and didn't hide behind the decision. He took full accountability for it.

"So I don't think you can say it's been handled badly.

"I thought England were right to move on at the stage that they did but Lancashire, if I'd have been in that position, I might have tried to get a season out of him next year."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Nasser Hussain and Kumar Sangakkara reflect on Anderson's Lancashire exit

Where next for Anderson if he carries on playing?

Anderson is poised to play in the Italia T10 League in Rome later this month, having also been named as co-owner for Napoli Knights.

Speaking publicly for the first time since his departure from Old Trafford, on BBC podcast Tailenders, Anderson said he had not yet decided whether he would extend his county career.

He replied "wouldn't have thought so" when asked whether he could see himself turning out for Lancashire's fierce rivals Yorkshire.

If locality is high on the seamer's priority list then Durham could be an option.

However, the Chester-le-Street club, promoted to Division One at the end of the 2026 season, are well-stocked with pacers, especially if England keep overlooking Matthew Potts and Brydon Carse.

Image: Sir James Anderson has not yet decided whether he will extend his playing career in county cricket

Leicestershire, Worcestershire and Derbyshire are also not an enormous trek from Manchester, so Anderson may perhaps be tempted to go to there, pass on his wisdom to younger bowlers, and try to help engineer promotion pushes from Division Two.

The early murmurings following Anderson's Lancashire release were that Division One clubs were interested in signing him, so maybe we should add Nottinghamshire, Warwickshire and Somerset to the list of possible destinations?

With Josh Tongue now an England regular, there may be space for Anderson in the Notts attack, while Somerset, still pursuing a long-awaited maiden County Championship title, could be eager to pair the veteran and Craig Overton as a new-ball duo.

Image: Could Anderson and Chris Woakes (right) link up at Warwickshire?

If Anderson were to join Warwickshire, the 2026 Championship winners, he could bowl in tandem with former England colleague Chris Woakes and a player in Ethan Bamber who perhaps deserves to be in the conversation for international honours after 69 wickets at an average under 20 last term.

Many factors will play into Anderson's decision of whether to play on or not - who wants him, where he wants to go, how much money he is being offered - and if one of them is romance, then let's not rule a career-ending spell with Middlesex.

While Old Trafford was Anderson's home ground for a quarter of a century, he has enjoyed a love affair with the 'Home of Cricket' in Lord's, a venue where he bagged 123 wickets in 29 Tests during his England days, including seven five-fors.

Anderson's England career ended with an enforced retirement at Lord's. Maybe his domestic one could end on his own terms at the same place?
