Sports.title: Alexa Rendell joins Sky Sports F1 team ahead of Sao Paulo GP
Sports.content:
Sky Sports has strengthened its award-winning Formula 1 team with the appointment of Alexa Rendell as F1 Multimedia Journalist, as the broadcaster looks to bring even more fans closer to the sport.

In a newly created role, Alexa will work across Sky Sports' social channels, live Formula 1 programming and Sky Sports News, bringing fans closer to the personalities, stories, and moments that make Formula 1 one of the world's most compelling sports.

Her appointment comes as Formula 1 continues to attract a broader and more diverse audience, with younger fans and women playing an increasingly important part in the sport's growth. Since becoming the home of Formula 1 in the UK and Ireland in 2012, Sky Sports has seen viewing among under-35s increase by 120 per cent, while its female audience has more than doubled. The 2025 season was also the most-watched in Sky Sports' history.

Alexa will help build on that momentum, creating content that reflects the evolving ways fans enjoy and engage with Formula 1, while making the sport more accessible and bringing audiences closer to the action. From the biggest stories in the paddock, to the personalities and rivalries beyond the race weekend, she will play an important role in connecting with both established fans and those discovering the sport for the first time.

As part of her role, Alexa will report from across the Formula 1 paddock and Sky Sports' live coverage, interviewing drivers, team principals, and other key figures from across the sport. She will join the Sky Sports F1 team in Brazil for the upcoming Grand Prix, where she will begin bringing fans closer to the action.

Alexa Rendell, F1 Multimedia Journalist, said: "I'm really thrilled to be joining the Sky Sports F1 family. Formula 1 has always been my first love, and Sky has been part of my journey in the sport since I was a teenager, when I got my first taste of the industry through its access events. To now be joining the team feels like a really special full-circle moment.

"I can't wait to get stuck in from Brazil and tell the stories that make this sport so incredible. With a new generation of fans coming into the sport, I'm really looking forward to helping connect with those audiences and sharing F1 in fresh and engaging ways."

Billy McGinty, Director of F1 at Sky Sports, said: "We're delighted to welcome Alexa to the team. She is a rising star in motorsport broadcasting and has an instinct for connecting with audiences. Formula 1 is evolving, with more people than ever discovering and connecting with the sport, and it's important that our coverage evolves too - finding new ways to tell the stories and bring fans closer to the personalities and moments that make F1 so compelling."

Alexa joins Sky Sports with experience as a creator, reporter, and presenter across a broad range of motorsport, including Formula E, the FIA World Endurance Championship, Extreme E, and F1 Academy.

Sky recently agreed a new long-term partnership with Formula 1, securing its position as the home of the sport in the UK and Ireland until the end of the 2034 season. In the UK and Ireland, Sky and NOW are the only places to watch live coverage of every practice, qualifying session, Sprint, and Grand Prix.

Formula 1 heads to Brazil for the final leg of the triple header with the Sao Paulo Grand Prix this weekend, live on Sky Sports F1. Stream Sky Sports with NOW

Sports.title: Goalkeeper Owono posts of 'most difficult days' after De Miguel's death from collision
Sports.content:
Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel died after a collision with FC Andorra's goalkeeper Jesus Owono, who has now released a statement; Lautaro Spatz also took to Instagram to defend his team-mate, who has deleted his account on the social media platform

Jesus de Miguel: Goalkeeper Jesus Owono experiencing 'most difficult days of my life' after Tenerife forward's death following collision

Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono walks off the pitch after he collided with FC Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel

Jesus Owono says he is going through the most difficult ‌days of his life in a statement released by his club FC Andorra on Wednesday, following the death of ‌Tenerife forward Jesus De Miguel.

The Tenerife forward died on Tuesday morning following a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday.

Owono was sent off for the clash having raced from his goal and struck 30-year-old De Miguel at force, with the Tenerife player subsequently suffering a cardiac arrest after being taken into intensive care.

"These are the most difficult days of my life," ‌Owono said in a statement. "I struggle to find the words, and I find it very hard to ​process what has happened. I know there will be many questions to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

"But right now, honestly, ​I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the ⁠pain we are experiencing. Rest in ⁠peace, Jesus."

Owono deactivated his Instagram account on Tuesday after receiving abuse online.

Andorra said that they were offering psychological support to anyone at the club who needed it following De Miguel's death.

Andorra centre-back Lautaro Spatz defended his team-mate ‌Owono on Tuesday evening.

"I also want to say a few words about my team-mate, goalkeeper and friend, who is deeply affected by what has happened," Spatz said on social media.

"Those of us who know him know the kind of person he ⁠is, how much he is suffering at this moment, and ​that he would never intentionally hurt anyone."

"In football, unfortunate ​incidents can happen, but no one could imagine that one of ​them might end with such tragic consequences," continued Spatz, also sending his ⁠condolences to De Miguel's family and Tenerife.

The Equatoguinean Football Federation expressed support for Owono in a statement on Tuesday, adding that the 25-year-old was going through a situation of ⁠profound sorrow and grief.

Owono has made 47 ​international appearances for Equatorial Guinea.

Meanwhile, Can Vidalet goalkeeper Michel Owono said on social ​media that he was receiving racist abuse, with people confusing him with the Andorra player.

Spanish national police have opened a ‌routine investigation into De Miguel's ​death.

Fans gathered at Tenerife's Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium to lay tributes to De Miguel, with the club declaring six days of official mourning.

Image: Tributes were paid to Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel outside the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez Stadium in Santa Cruz

A memorial service will be held at the ground on Saturday evening for the striker, with supporters invited to attend.

Tuesday's domestic Spanish games were called off as a mark of respect but Champions League matches went ahead, including Barcelona's clash with Aston Villa at the Nou Camp.

A minute's silence was held ahead of the contest, which Barca won 3-0, with Raphinha scoring twice.

Speaking to CBS Sports afterwards, the Brazilian refused to talk about the game, saying: "I want to send a lot of strength to the family of Jesus. Today I'm not going to talk about football.

"For me, the truth is it was quite difficult (to play). After seeing the news, of course I didn't have good feelings. He's a fellow player and it could have happened to anyone, it could have happened to me.

"He was the same age as me, I don't know if that's why it affected me more. It's been a difficult day. Personally, it touched me a lot."

Arsenal also held a minute's silence at their training session to remember De Miguel, while manager Mikel Arteta addressed the situation in his press conference.

"Absolutely heartbreaking," said Arteta. "Watching back the action, the incident, what happened, to see a colleague lose his life in such a manner, it's beyond any words that I can put today.

"So, on behalf of everybody at the club, we want to send our condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel, all his loved ones, and to Tenerife as well because it's been a really difficult day."

The Tenerife match was suspended after the incident, which occurred in stoppage time, with distressed players calling for immediate medical attention.

A statement from Tenerife announcing De Miguel's death read: "We stand alongside his devastated family, alongside his loved ones… that today weep for this cruel outcome."

In their own statement on Tuesday evening, Andorra said the club were "deeply shocked", adding: "The first thing we want to do is express our most sincere condolences to his family, CD Tenerife and all those who were close to him.

"We know that no words can ease such pain, but we want them to know that we are by their side and that we deeply share their sadness."

Sports.title: Real Madrid close on agreement to sign Manchester United 16-year-old JJ Gabriel
Sports.content:
Real Madrid are closing in on signing JJ Gabriel, though Manchester United will consider legal action if the club believe any rules have been broken.

Madrid have offered the 16-year-old forward a multi-year contract and, subject to final talks, hope to bring him to the club in January. Gabriel is registered with United’s academy until the end of the season and it is understood the club have yet to be contacted by the player’s camp or Madrid regarding the proposed move.

Madrid intend to sign Gabriel via a Fifa loophole that allows clubs in the European Union to tie down young players to professional contracts if they have an EU passport, which Gabriel is eligible to acquire through both his parents.

Fifa would have to sign this off and United are on alert regarding any potential breach of regulations. A compensation fee would be due to United if Gabriel joined Madrid or any other team. Madrid have been approached for comment.

Gabriel walked out on United in September and is believed to be training in Spain. A move to Madrid offers the prospect of progression to senior football via their B team, Castilla, who play in the regionalised Spanish third tier.

Gabriel played in a pre-season friendly for United against Atlético Madrid in Stockholm in August at the age of 15 and had been training with the first team. If he had not informed United of his wish to depart, he would have been in Michael Carrick’s squad for the 3-2 Carabao Cup defeat by Brighton on 16 September. Had Gabriel featured, he would have become the youngest player in the club’s history.

Gabriel last season became the youngest winner of United’s academy player of the year award and was the Premier League’s Under-18 player of the season.

Sports.title: ‘She can do what Beckham did’: Océane Hurtré making waves at Birmingham
Sports.content:
At the conclusion of Birmingham’s warm-up, the players quietly and carefully placed their footballs into a draw-string bag. All except one, Océane Hurtré, who nonchalantly chipped hers straight into the bag from about 15 yards. It was an innocuous moment that might have escaped most onlookers at Hednesford Town’s Keys Park but it demonstrated the swagger with which she is playing.

To observe the 22-year-old warming up before last week’s 1-1 League Cup draw at Aston Villa was to witness a player making skills look easy, taking one touch where others took two and pulling off no-look passes. She is backing up that panache in the Women’s Super League, as the joint-second-highest goalscorer with six from the promoted side’s opening eight matches. Only Khadija Shaw has scored more.

Add in two WSL assists and a goal and an assist on her France debut last month and it has been a breakthrough campaign for Hurtré that very few expected, except perhaps those who followed her career in France closely. They include the former France head coach Olivier Echouafni, who gave a 16-year-old Hurtré her professional debut for Paris Saint-Germain during the title-winning 2020-21 campaign, the only time a side have stopped OL Lyonnes from finishing top in the past 20 years.

“She listens to everything the coach says, she’s very attentive, she’s very focused,” Echouafni says. “She’s like a sun, because when you speak with her, there’s a big light. She was always quite skilful, moving the ball quickly to draw out her opponent, and had a good shot and delivered quality crosses.

“Back then, she lacked athletic stamina, the ability to sustain repeated bursts and sometimes also struggled in one-on-one situations because she was so young, but she has made great progress since then. She has also made great progress mentally – her move to Birmingham has done her a world of good.”

WSL fans are enjoying Hurtré’s pace, skill and general attacking threats, but imprinted in Echouafni’s memory are her defensive efforts as a youngster. He recalls Hurtré, on her second league appearance, against Paris FC in May 2021, replacing the Canada full-back Ashley Lawrence with two minutes remaining. “She cleared the ball off the goalline and prevented the equaliser,” he says. “It was a very important action because, one week later, PSG won the championship.”

To describe her as surrounded by experienced professionals at PSG would be a big understatement. When she had made her debut, in Europe against the Polish side Gornik Leczna, she was on the same team as a 42-year-old Formiga. Her gratitude to PSG is clear: she was spotted at the Joie Stadium last week watching Manchester City take on PSG in the Women’s Champions League, sitting just above her former club’s bench. PSG loaned Hurtré to Dijon in 2022 to gain more first-team experience and to Bordeaux in 2023-24. An injury at each affected her game time but she left a strong impression.

“I wanted to sign Océane for two main reasons,” says Sylvain Carric, Dijon women’s general manager from 2022 until 2026, who now runs Strasbourg’s women’s teams. “The first was, naturally, the quality of her left foot – it’s magnificent; she can put the ball exactly where she wants it. The second was her versatility. She’s capable of playing as a left-back, a winger or a No 8.

View image in fullscreen Océane Hurtré’s form at Birmingham has led to an international callup with France, where she scored on her debut. Photograph: Natalie Mincher/SPP/Shutterstock

“Océane left a fantastic impression during her time at Dijon. She had the intelligence to come to Dijon to grow, rather than remaining on the bench at PSG. She was a very good player and an excellent teammate, always smiling. She has been supported by a very good inner circle, especially her father, who I believe played an important role in her success. As for her potential, it was obvious, especially given that left foot, but she just needed to adapt her physique for the elite level. Now that she’s brought all those elements together, I’m certainly not surprised.”

Hurtré took a risk when she joined second-tier Birmingham in the summer of 2025 but it has paid off after she helped them win promotion and she has goals against clubs including Arsenal, Brighton and Manchester City.

Birmingham’s head coach, Amy Merricks, said last month: “We’re incredibly proud of her. I’m not going to share it but, if I did share where she was when she first came in, people wouldn’t quite believe the turnaround. There were so many areas that she needed support with, transitioning to a different country at a young age. She’s learned English, which is a massive step.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“Everyone sees her work on the pitch but we are fortunate to see the amount of work she’s done of it, and it absolutely translates. She’s diligent, she’s a student of the game, and she thoroughly deserved the call-up [for France].”

Hurtré was rewarded for her strong start with September’s WSL player of the month award. Sylvain Jamet, a women’s football writer for the French magazine footofeminin, saw her play at the Under-20 Women’s World Cup in Costa Rica and believes Hurtré has become “a lot faster” at Birmingham.

“Her technical ability and her set-piece deliveries with her left foot stood out,” Jamet says of Hurtré’s six years representing France’s youth teams. “Since she’s arrived in the UK, they must have worked on her speed.”

View image in fullscreen Océane Hurtré caused problems for the Latvia defence during her international debut last month. Photograph: Eddy Lemaistre/Icon Sport/Getty Images

Hurtré’s goal contributions in France’s 9-0 win against Latvia have boosted her hopes of a place in next summer’s World Cup. Jamet, comparing her to Chelsea’s left-sided France player Sandy Baltimore, says: “They’re competing for the same place with France now. She’s less explosive than Sandy, but she’s better technically for the crosses and passing. Baltimore’s obviously fantastic, more like a one-v-one player, taking on defenders.

“Hurtré can cross from anywhere, she can do what [David] Beckham did, basically, crossing from deep, crossing from anywhere. She had very good first cap for France. There’s a good chance she will be in the squad for the World Cup. I really expect her to get one of those 26 places.”

Sports.title: Football Daily | Manchester United’s unlikely one-match winning streak and hard-to-please fans
Sports.content:
DO CALL IT A COMEBACK

Considering they’d just gone nine games without a win, assorted Manchester United fans carping about the manner of their team’s Bigger Cup win over Roma on shouty radio phone-ins on Tuesday night struck Football Daily as the type who’d complain about a firefighter refusing to wipe their boots at the front door before rescuing them from a burning house. Yes, it’s true that United played appallingly in the first half and were lucky to be only 2-0 down. And yes, the penalty was somewhat fortuitous against a knack-ravaged Serie A side who have form in coughing up two-goal leads in the competition. However, when your once mighty side has spent the opening months of the season looking more like a broken washing machine full of spanners falling down an escalator than an elite football team, complaining about the artistic merit of a highly unlikely comeback win seems unnecessarily churlish, even if Matheus Cunha’s celebration of the winner was a little over the top.

United were well represented on Amazon Prime’s coverage, with club alumni Nicky Butt, Ashley Young and Wayne Rooney all present to offer their views which reflected a performance of two incredibly contrasting halves. During the break the trio understandably got the collective funk on over their former side’s timidity, cowardice, and lack of ideas, confidence and belief but less than an hour later they were whistling a far happier tune.

“The second half was amazing, they were front-footed and they deserved to win the game in the end,” cheered Rooney in his post-match analysis. “The first half was terrible, but we saw the passion and fight we wanted in the second half. The crowd got right behind the team and you felt like they could go on to win the game.” While most in the Old Trafford crowd gave the team their full support, the cameras did inevitably cut to ashen-faced club blazers Jason Wilcox and Omar Berrada half-heartedly applauding their team with all the enthusiasm of dinner party hosts forcing a smile as the cat proudly drops a dead mouse on the cheeseboard.

With United now on an unlikely one-match winning streak, much of the post-match discourse focused on what this win might mean for Michael Carrick’s future as head coach. Widely regarded as a dead man walking before the game, he may well have bought himself a stay of execution and a scenic detour to the gallows. A pardon seems unlikely but another home win against Aston Villa on Sunday would further endear him to fans who really want him to succeed. It would also make life extremely difficult for his increasingly unpopular employers before an international break they had almost certainly boxed off as the ideal time to hand him his P45.

QUOTE OF THE DAY

“For Real Madrid and for all Madridismo it is a great pride that a figure of his sporting and human dimension, a benchmark in Spanish and world sport, becomes part of our board of directors and contributes, from this responsibility, to the present and future of our club” – there’s a new man on the Real Madrid board – and it’s 22-times grand slam-winning tennis legend Rafael Nadal. It’ll make for some interesting family chat when he next sees his uncle, the former Barça stalwart Miguel Ángel Nadal.

View image in fullscreen No wonder he’s looking sheepish. Photograph: Atilano Garcia/Sopa Images/Shutterstock

LIVE ON BIG WEBSITE

Join Simon Burnton at 5.45pm GMT for red-hot MBM coverage of Fenerbahce 0-2 Liverpool, while Dominic Booth will be on hand at 8pm with a Bigger Cup clockwatch taking in the goals from RB Leipzig 0-2 Manchester City and Slavia Prague 0-2 Arsenal.

double quotation mark Roma managed to capitulate to Manchester United while being 2-0 up. Even Man Utd haven’t managed to do that too many times but I wouldn’t describe their second half performance as ‘a comeback for the ages’. Their opponents just didn’t turn up” – Nigel Sanders.

double quotation mark These suggestions of paper and velcro shirts seem overly complicated. (yesterday’s Football Daily letters). If teams would just commit to using body paint instead of clothing, the foul becomes impossible to commit unless a defender is possessed of both long fingernails and a cavalier disregard for the health of their opponent. Also, no more tedious yellow cards for removing the shirt after a goal. Win win” – Ben Mimmack.

If you add Roberto di Matteo (he clung on for one more game) and spoiling Alex Ferguson’s leaving do with a 5-5 draw we were responsible for nine dismissals in seven years between 2010 and 2017. I think that’s pretty impressive. We’ve been quiet since then but perhaps we’re going for another run – championship managers beware” – Tom Levesley.

Sports.title: Has a footballer ever run a marathon faster than James Milner? | The Knowledge
Sports.content:
It came as no surprise to the Knowledge that James Milner had spent the early months of his retirement training for – and then running in – the New York City Marathon. Yes, the bleep test-loving former Brighton, Liverpool and Manchester City player recorded an excellent time of 3hr 9min 4sec, an average of 7min 13sec per mile. Not bad for a 40-year-old whose physique is more like that of a wrestler than a whippet. “A few years ago, I feel like I could have definitely done sub-3:00,” he said, lamenting his late-career injuries for hindering him.

In 2012 we ran a column listing footballers’ fastest marathon times, with the former Leicester playmaker Muzzy Izzet leading the pack on 3hr 22min 36sec at the 2011 London Marathon. That very respectable time has now been surpassed by the Premier League’s record appearance maker, so we thought we had better take a gulp of our isotonic energy drink and run through a few more tales of football’s marathon men and women.

More recent marathon attempts by either active or former footballers puts Izzet down in 12th place, just behind André Schürrle, who clocked 3hr 21min 25sec in Berlin last year, though clearly wanted a greater challenge than a mere 26.2 miles. This year, the 35-year-old completed the 167.7-mile six-stage Marathon des Sables in 51hr 41min 16sec, placing 675th overall. He also climbed Mont Blanc. But back to marathons, where the fastest time we can find for a female footballer is 3hr 40min 30sec by the former USA midfielder Lauren Holiday. She is closely followed by her good friends from the USWNT, Leslie Osborne (3hr 41min 33sec) and Abby Wambach (3hr 44min 25sec).

The Fulham manager, Álvaro Arbeloa, is 11th on our overall list (3hr 15min 21sec, Valencia 2019), with Kevin Kilbane, who always looked like he had a marathon runner’s spring in his step, 10th on 3hr 14min 44sec (London, 2013). A tip of the hat now to Danny Mills, father to the GB Olympic runner George Mills, with Mills Sr running the 2023 London Marathon in 3hr 12min 18sec at 45 years of age. Meanwhile, Milner’s run places him eighth as we approach some of football’s more serious runners.

The former Dundee United and West Ham defender Christian Dailly clocked a seriously impressive 3hr 6min 26sec at the 2013 London Marathon. “In 1990, I went from boys’ football in May to my Dundee United debut in August,” said Dailly after the race. “We’d be down at the beach, and all of a sudden, I’d be running through the sea at St Andrews or up and down the sand dunes. When I got to pre-season at Dundee United, I was flying, running away from everyone.” Dailly went into athletics coaching when his football career ended. We did not expect a goalkeepeer to be jostling for position towards the front of the pack, but the former Derby County and Sheffield Wednesday stopper Lee Grant hared around London in 3hr 0min 33sec this year.

And so we get to the hallowed ground of a sub-three hour marathon and a select group of only five. The Real Madrid legend Raúl González was clearly being cheered from the rafters as he ran his home marathon in 2hr 59min 22sec in 2019. “It was only the second marathon of my life. I wanted to break three hours, and I’m very happy with what I’ve accomplished,” he said. The Oxford United manager, Aaron Ramsey, used his relative youth at 35 to tear up the Stockholm Marathon this summer in exactly 2hr 59min. Arjen Robben was known for his blistering pace over short distances in his glittering career but he showed that he could blend speed with stamina as he raced round Rotterdam in 2023 in a time of 2hr 58min 33sec.

View image in fullscreen Aaron Ramsey poses before Cardiff Half Marathon last month. The Welshman ran the Stockholm Marathon this summer in under three hours. Photograph: Huw Fairclough/Getty Images

Before setting out on his managerial career, Luis Enrique trained like a demon for the Florence Marathon, with his hard work paying off as he came home in 2hr 58min 8sec. He has since continued his fitness regime, competing in the Frankfurt Ironman event and the Marathon des Sables.

But the gold medal for the fastest former footballer to run a marathon goes to Alexei Smertin. The former Chelsea and Russia utility man took endurance running seriously when he retired in 2008 and hit a peak of 2hr 48min 17sec at the Kazan Marathon in 2020, aged 45. That is an incredible pace of 6min 25sec per mile. He has since tried switching to longer distances as he has aged but believes he may still have one or two quick marathons left in him. “I’ve been leaning toward ultras. One reason is that speed declines with age,” he said recently. “I thought I’d never be able to improve my personal best [2:48:17] … [but] I have a few more years to improve my speed.”

Let the ink dry

“What is the soonest a manager has been sacked after signing a contract extension?” asks Dave Smythe.

Adam Clark comes in hot with the first suggestion: “Leam Richardson, then of Wigan Athletic, signed a three-year contract extension on 25 October 2022 and was sacked 16 days later on 10 November 2022. Wigan then recruited Kolo Touré on a three-and-a-half year contract, who subsequently lasted just nine games.”

“I’m pretty sure when Watford sacked Glenn Roeder in 1996 he’d signed a contract extension about a fortnight earlier?” suggests Daz Pearce. Good shout, Daz: Watford were not yet in their era of sacking a manager every month, but Roeder – initially appointed at Vicarage Road in 1993 – was given the boot by Watford just 10 days after signing a new one-year contract extension in February 1996. “I am sure I have learned from this experience,” said Roeder, who announced his intention to stay in the game. He would not get another managerial job for another five years, enjoying a successful stint at West Ham from 2001-03.

Not a contract extension but Kevin Cullis’s appointment at Swansea City in 1996 lasted just seven days. Cullis, who never played professionally, had only ever previously coached non-league Crawley Town’s youth team and was later jailed for fraud in 2003, and didn’t get off to the best start in Wales with Swans players reportedly ignoring his tactics at half-time against Blackpool during just his second game in charge. Cullis resigned shortly afterwards.

Elsewhere, Dave Bassett lasted less than four days at Crystal Palace in 1984, Marcelo Bielsa resigned as manager of Lazio after just two days in the job in 2016 and Leroy Rosenior’s 10-minute stint at Torquay United is Knowledge folklore. You can read more about that here.

Surf’s up

We have received some new responses to last week’s Knowledge archive, which features some 2016 answers to the question: who were the first football club to have an official website?

“Last week, Martyn Amos reported an Ipswich fan website started in 1990,” wrote a sceptical Alan Terlep (and others), “but history records that the first known website went online in August 1991, so if that’s correct he has a claim to fame well beyond the Knowledge. A fan site that was already active in 1993 may well be the oldest or there though.”

Fellow reader Mark Francome, who works at a global IT service provider so should know a thing or two about this, emails that “Luton Town fans had ‘WHOSH’ (‘Worldwide Hatters On The Super Highway’), which dates from 1994,” while “Millwall also had ‘You’ll Never Make The Station’ from around the same time. No records exist to confirm the internet rumour that Millwall admins hacked their Luton counterparts and ripped up the HTML.”

Knowledge archive

“Portsmouth’s new kit has names of fallen soldiers on it. Are there other examples of clubs recognising war victims on their kit?” asked Simon Cook in August 2014.

Andrew Walker points us towards Raith Rovers’ away kit for the 2014-15 season, which has been designed to pay tribute to the 16th Royal Scots regiment, a battalion formed of sportsmen, seven of whom came from the Kirkcaldy club. Three Rovers players – Jimmy Todd, Jimmy Scott and George McLay – were killed during the conflict.

“We wanted to do something completely different for next season in terms of kit colours,” the Raith chair, Turnbull Hutton, told the Dundee Courier,” but at the same time the board has been considering a suitable way to mark this centenary in an appropriate manner, so we have brought these two ambitions together with our new green and black strip. “We hope that it captures the imagination of the Scottish footballing public and, through next season’s sports pages, that it ensures that we really do remember the sacrifices of our players and so many others 100 years ago.”

And in Wales, Aberystwyth Town are also commemorating the 100th anniversary of the outbreak of the first world war. “We’re the kit suppliers to Aberystwyth Town Football Club in the Welsh Premier League,” write the good folk at RM Teamwear, “and this season we produced their home strip honouring the centenary of the first world war, more specifically on the sleeves we have the names of players who played for the club and lost their lives in the Great War. Their name, rank and regiment are on players 1-14 in the war veteran player’s position he used to play. Others have “In Memory of Players of This Club Who Fell in the Great War” as seen in the attached photo.”

Can you help?

“Not only were Rangers v Dundee United and Manchester City v Barnsley in 2004-05 the only British league matches to finish 7-1 that season, the same opposing goalkeepers also played in both matches,” flags Stephen Toal. “Ronald Waterreus played for Rangers and Manchester City while Nick Colgan turned out for both Dundee United and Barnsley. Are there any other examples of opposing goalkeepers coming up against each other twice in the same season for a different set of opposing teams?”

“Following Coventry City’s 3-1 victory over Sunderland, I noticed a potentially unique statistic involving Luke O’Nien, who has now played in defeats against Coventry in all four divisions of English league football. Is this a first?” ponders Kirk Savage.

“Has ever been a headed goal awarded goal of the season?” wonders Rupert Sheard. “I can think of a few belters, but awards tend to go to ones kicked in.”

“Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?”

Sports.title: West Ham confirm Scott Parker as head coach after sacking Nuno Espírito Santo
Sports.content:
Scott Parker has been confirmed as West Ham’s head coach, taking over from Nuno Espírito Santo, who was sacked on Tuesday. The club’s former midfielder arrives on a two-and-a-half year contract with the team eighth in the Championship and takes charge of his first game at Cardiff on Wednesday.

West Ham hope that Parker, a promotion specialist, can spark a revival after defeats in their past two matches. The 46-year-old has led Burnley, Bournemouth and Fulham into the top flight.

West Ham kept faith with Nuno after last season’s relegation from the Premier League but acted after they were beaten at home by West Brom last Saturday. Parker has been out of work since leaving Burnley after their relegation from the Premier League last April.

Quick Guide How do I 

Parker said: “My energy levels, my enthusiasm, my desire, my passion – it’s absolutely running through and that’s the feeling I had as soon as there was a conversation that this was possible. That’s exactly why I’m here and why I want to be here.”

He said he was excited to return to the club for whom he made 129 appearances between 2007 and 2011. “It is a very proud moment for me to step into this role and return to a club that means so much to me and my family. A lot of very fond memories of my time here – four years of probably the best football I played in my career.

“There was a warmth, a love, a feeling that I probably didn’t have anywhere else. There was something which stood out constantly and that was the relationship that I built up with the fanbase here. That rapport and respect, that I felt instantly.”

Sports.title: Choke of the century? Chengdu collapse sets up thrilling Chinese Super League climax
Sports.content:
With four games of the Chinese Super League to go, Chengdu Rongcheng needed just a point to clinch their first title. With one game to go, they still need a point. What was a formality has become a formidable task. The biggest bottle job in Asian football history is very much on and it would be as popular as it would be dramatic.

The coach of the Sichuan club, the former Portsmouth and Coventry striker John Aloisi, has seen a 12-point lead over Dalian Yingbo cut to just three before Sunday’s showdowns. Whatever happens, this is a positive and thrilling end to a season that started negatively – literally – with nine of the 16 top-tier clubs kicking off on minus points. They had been punished as part of a “special campaign to crack down on match-fixing, gambling and corruption in the football industry”, said a joint statement from the Chinese Football Association, the Ministry of Public Security and the General Administration of Sport at the time.

Chengdu were one of the seven to start on zero, above the defending champions, Shanghai Port, who lost five points and the runners-up, Shanghai Shenhua, who were hit with 10. It robbed the usual favourites of energy and it was all a bit surreal.

It almost felt over as soon as it started with Chengdu opening up a big lead, dropping just two points from the first 12 games while the usual powers struggled to get going.

Chengdu is a major city more known for its fiery Sichuan cuisine, genteel temples and cute pandas than football, despite English attempts to change that. In 2006, Sheffield United bought a local club but the Chengdu Blades were eventually dissolved in 2015. Four years later, City Football Group bought a stake in Sichuan Jiuniu but then moved the club to the southern city of Shenzhen in 2024.

Chengdu Rongcheng were formed in 2018, coming up through the divisions to finally, this season, be within touching distance of the championship. But just two wins from the last 13 and three straight defeats mean the leaders are not limping to the line but have collapsed right next to it.

It should have been over weeks ago. On 10 October, more than 40,000 fans were ready to celebrate the title but an added-time goal from Alberto Quiles gave Tianjin Jinmen Tiger a 1-0 win and postponed the celebrations. Next up was a trip to Shanghai Port but that ended in a 3-0 defeat. The penultimate game of the season came against challengers Dalian Yingbo, when again, just avoiding defeat was needed. It was another painful experience as they lost 1-0 after missing a first-half penalty and having a 90th-minute equaliser ruled out by the video assistant referee.

Chengdu have not scored in almost seven hours of football while Dalian are the form team with four consecutive wins. If they win a fifth against Tianjin then Chengdu need a point at fourth-placed Shandong Taishan as the league is decided by head-to-head results before goal difference. Not many think they will. Even fewer hope so. Dalian and the 60,000 fans that attend home games are the people’s choice. Chengdu are not popular because their fans have developed a poor reputation. Last November, the club was fined about $70,000 (£52,200) after some home supporters racially abused Henan FC’s Ghanaian striker Frank Acheampong, just weeks after a punishment of $3,000 after travelling supporters at a Champions League game in South Korea threw bottles at the Ulsan HD players.

Whatever happens it is an unexpected and dramatic ending to a season that started in shock and the usual negative international headlines that surround Chinese football. The grandstand finish is welcome and average attendances have risen. They are set to finish at about 30,000, a considerable jump from last season’s 25,755 and, by some distance, the best in Asia. Regional leagues have been enjoying some popularity too, showing that there is genuine love for the game in the country; a passion that grows better when it is organic from the bottom rather than organised from the top.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The national side is still a problem, though, and even for a fanbase well accustomed to disappointment the recent 5-0 defeat to Palestine at home, the fourth-biggest loss in history, was tough to take. As one journalist said, being thrashed by Brazil, Japan and Wales is one thing, but Palestine was another. There were some mitigating circumstances in that a number of national team players were at the Asian Games, where China actually performed well, losing narrowly to old nemesis South Korea in the bronze final.

View image in fullscreen The former Coventry striker John Aloisi is looking to avoid the biggest bottle job in Asian football history. Photograph: Masashi Hara/Getty Images

There are signs that the gap behind Korea is not as wide as it used to be. China reached the final of the under-17 and under-23 Asian championships this year before losing both against Japan. Compared with the rest of Asia’s best, young Chinese players are closing the gap at a technical and tactical level. Exporting more players to Europe is necessary to play at a higher level and if that happens, that senior national shirt may feel a little lighter.

Failure can, however, be hard to shake off as Chengdu Rongcheng may well find out if they mess this up.

Sports.title: talkSPORT host reveals what Xabi Alonso will do about Estevao after claims from sources
Sports.content:
talkSPORT host reveals what Xabi Alonso will do about Estevao after claims from sources

Chelsea and Xabi Alonso remain 'delighted' with Estevao despite his lack of playing time - he isn't going anywhere.

That's the latest from talkSPORT's Andy Jacobs, who has revealed all from conversations in the directors' box at Stamford Bridge about the Brazilian starlet, amid concerns he could look to leave the club.

4 Estevao has slipped down the pecking order at Stamford Bridge this season Credit: Getty

Doubts have emerged over Estevao's future in west London, with the winger appearing to be out of favour under new boss Alonso.

After an impressive debut season, the 19-year-old has struggled for minutes this term - highlighted by him being left on the bench during Chelsea's Carabao Cup exit against Liverpool last week.

Alonso then admitted the teenager 'could be happier' - having only had 47 minutes of Premier League action to his name - sparking further fears the Blues could be set to lose their young talent.

However, Estevao was handed his first league start against Manchester United on Saturday and instantly proved his worth.

The Brazilian was a real threat in the 2-0 win, having two goals ruled out for offside, leading to calls for him to feature more regularly.

However, with Alonso's system favouring a back-three, Estevao has found himself playing back-up to Pedro Neto at right-wing-back this term, unable to play as an out-and-out winger.

Meanwhile, in his preferred No.10 role, he has to compete with superstars Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, while Geovany Quenda started ahead of him in the 2-0 defeat to Tottenham as Rogers was forced to deputise up front.

Estevao situation explained

Amid growing fears Estevao could see his future elsewhere, talkSPORT host and Chelsea fan Andy Jacobs has now reassured fans that talk of this is unfounded.

Having sat in the directors' box at Stamford Bride for the United win, he revealed that Alonso is, in fact, a huge fan of the teen

On Estevao, Jacobs told talkSPORT's Hawksbee and Jacobs: “[He's] going nowhere. Apparently the manager loves him.

4 Alonso's preferred system has seen Estevao struggle for game time Credit: Getty

4 But the teenage sensation starred for Chelsea against Man United and the latest is that the teenager is happy at Stamford Bridge Credit: Getty

“The only concern he has is about his physicality with regards to the Premier League - which is why he played against Manchester United because they're not a physical team.

“So he's worried, he's seen things. I've seen him play against Leeds twice where he's just got blown out of the pitch.

“They're working on building him up."

As for Estevao himself, Jacobs insisted the player remains happy at Chelsea despite his lack of minutes.

He added: "He's very happy. He's no trouble and is a very good trainer. Very good kid off the pitch and they're delighted with him.”

After Jacobs gave Chelsea fans reassurances over Estevao's future, South American football expert Tim Vickery was quick to remind them of the huge talent they have on their hands.

4 Estevao is considered the next Neymar, but Chelsea recently faced fears they could lose their Brazilian star Credit: AFP

Having previously dubbed the the 'next Neymar', he insisted the winger ranks ahead of some huge other Brazilian names.

Vickery declared on talkSPORT: "This includes Vinicius Jr and Rodrygo - I think he's the best talent to come out of Brazil since Neymar without any of the baggage."

Estevao joined Chelsea in the summer of 2025 as one of the most highly-rated teenagers in world football, with Barcelona, Real Madrid and Arsenal among the other clubs chasing him.

But he picked the Blues - and in his first campaign, he impressed, having a hand in 12 goals in 36 games in all competitions.

So far this term though, he's not scored or assisted in the first nine matches, although his one league start only came against United.

Sports.title: Police launch murder investigation after death of footballer Ezekiel Williams
Sports.content:
Police have launched a murder investigation into the death of non-league footballer Ezekiel Williams.

Officers have arrested three men after Williams was allegedly attacked in Milton Keynes in the early hours of Sunday morning.

2 A murder investigation has been launched after Williams' death

The 26-year-old, who played for eight-tier Hendon, later died from his injuries.

Williams joined Hendon in September and recently scored his first goal for the club.

Thames Valley Police has now confirmed a murder investigation has been launched following his death.

Officers have arrested two men in their 20s on suspicion of murder, with a third man, aged 30, arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender.

Thames Valley Police statement

In a statement, the force said: "Two men, aged 21 and 28, both from Luton, have been arrested on suspicion of murder.

"A third man, aged 30 and also from Luton, has been arrested on suspicion of assisting an offender. All remain in custody.

"Officers remain in the area and there will continue to be an increased police presence around The Hub and city centre while enquiries continue.

"A dedicated Major Crime Unit investigation is underway."

The investigation comes after a GoFundMe page was set up in Williams' memory.

Those who wish to support his family have been given the opportunity to make a donation.

2 Police have arrested three men after an alleged attack on Williams Credit: X @HendonFC

Meanwhile, Hendon's London Senior Cup tie against Woodford Town, which was scheduled for Wednesday, has been postponed.

Hendon pay tribute to Williams

In a post on social media, the club said: "We are stunned and heartbroken to announce the sudden and tragic passing of midfielder Ezekiel Williams aged 26.

"A humble, unassuming and generous individual with a razor-sharp wit.

"Eze joined the club in September and quickly established himself as a highly popular member of the dressing room.

"Our thoughts and prayers are with Ezekiel’s family, friends, and everyone who knew him at this devastating time.

"He will be very sadly missed by all of us at Hendon Football Club."

The midfielder scored his first goal for the club in a 4-2 home defeat to Jersey Bulls on October 24.

His last appearance for the Greens came three days later against Egham Town.

Sports.title: Tottenham told they have elite talent working under Roberto De Zerbi as prediction made
Sports.content:
Tottenham have been told they have an elite talent on their books but he's working on the touchline rather than out on the pitch.

Spurs have come on leaps and bounds in recent weeks with Roberto De Zerbi, winning three consecutive Premier League games.



5 Tottenham are on the up after a tough two years Credit: Getty

Tottenham are on the up

The run of form, paired with early season performances that didn't get the desired result, have fans dreaming of an end to a dismal almost two-year spell.

Tottenham spent big money in the transfer market bringing in Sando Tonali and Mateus Fernandes to their pedestrian midfield.

But improvements to players already on the books have also been clear.



Micky van de Ven now looks comfortable in possession, Archie Gray has improved his defensive output, while Conor Gallagher, Mathys Tel, and others have also had notable progression.

Already Spurs look a far cry from the side which was crumbling under Thomas Frank and elite coaching appears to have been the catalyst.



It's not surprising to Wales national team manager Craig Bellamy though.

Who is Andrew Crofts?

One of his assistants, Andrew Crofts, who played for Norwich, Gillingham, Brighton, and Charlton, joined Tottenham in the summer as assistant head coach.



And the ex-Liverpool and Newcastle forward couldn't be more effusive in his praise for the former Gillingham captain and his ability on the training ground.

He told reporters: "I think he's one of the best coaches I've ever been anywhere near. I think he's that top. Honestly, I think he's immense. And I love my relationship with him as well. And I love his enthusiasm for the game."

Speaking exclusively to talkSPORT, Bellamy added: "His enthusiasm and the way he sees the game really motivates me. I'm sure it really motivates the players, and it's not saying he's a motivational coach. He says with enthusiasm, but he says it with clear detail, and that is something I really love.

5 Crofts came to the fore coaching at Brighton and is now assisting De Zerbi with Tottenham Credit: Getty



5 Crofts (third from the left) is a key member of Bellamy's Wales staff Credit: Getty

"I couldn't speak any higher of him. He's been massive for me, and his loyalty, the person he, is something that I don't take for granted. I can see why De Zerbi wants him near him. I would in a heartbeat.

"He, to me, has been really a breath of fresh air, and he allows me, the way I look at the game, to bring it really to life as well. So, it's nice. [I'm] a huge, huge fan."

How are Crofts and Bellamy linked?

While Bellamy and Crofts played together at international level, this hasn't been a career-long connection.



He added: "We were in squads together, and I really liked him, but I liked his professionalism.

"I could see [him becoming a coach]. But we weren't close as in friendship and ringing each other. It wasn't that. But I was always aware, even when I went into coaching, and seeing the experience of where he stepped up and who he's with, and then spoke to him before a game once when we played Brighton, and had nice conversations.

"He is someone I looked at, and I was like, I'd love to be able to work with this guy. I was lucky enough when I got this role, and I spoke to him. There's other people out there as well. It's not my friends. I never work that way. It's who's going to give me that little bit extra Who's going to do this? Who's going to do that? He's definitely done that.

5 Crofts has linked back up with De Zerbi this season - and Van Hecke Credit: Getty



"We have a big friendship now, but it always wasn't the case.

"You're always looking for someone who can improve you, who can bring something to the group.

"There's others out there that I would love to work with, but I'm lucky enough at the moment, I have him as well, that I'm enjoying every second with."

Tottenham prediction

And Tottenham's upturn in form, with Crofts by De Zerbi's side is no surprise and he predicts their fortunes will continue to improve.

"I have to be honest," Bellamy said. "They played Liverpool in the League Cup. And I know they lost. But in those moments in that game, I was like, they're getting closer.



"They're going to get close. This is not going to be too long. Now, I understand the criticism that kept leading towards it. They've signed this player, it's that player.

5 Crofts was one of a number of stars who began taking on player-coach roles as their careers came to an end Credit: Getty

"No, they can't play this way. You ain't got this. It's normal. Everyone's very good at telling you what you can't do.

"But honestly, and I remember speaking to him after, I was like, 'You're close. You're close'. And I just feel we've seen it. And I honestly, and I feel with Crofty and the manager he has, but also with the players they have, they're just going to keep improving.



"I feel it's going to be a good season."

Sports.title: Premier League Panel admits error to not give star straight red card
Sports.content:
The Premier League Key Match Incidents Panel has found that Cole Palmer should have been shown a straight red card against Tottenham.

Palmer was sent off in the London derby on October 24, but for two yellow cards following separate incidents of foul play.



3 The Premier League Key Match Incidents Panel have admitted that Palmer should have been shown a straight red card for his barge into Fernandes Credit: Getty

His first booking came after a clash with Spurs' Mateus Fernandes, who prevented him running clear with a handball.

Fernandes slid in and swiped the ball away from the Chelsea star's path with his arm, resulting in the latter losing his cool.

Palmer rushed straight over to Fernandes and barged into him as he stood back up, colliding into his face.



The England international was only shown a yellow card for that incident in the game that Spurs won 2-0.

However, the Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel have now admitted that the decision was an error.



And Palmer should have instead been shown a straight red before he did eventually go on to get sent off for a second yellow, which he received for a mis-timed challenge on Spurs midfielder Conor Gallagher.

Premier League panel admit error

The five-person panel deemed the on-field decision made by referee Chris Kavanagh at Stamford Bridge was incorrect.



Three of the panellists felt Palmer's action on Fernandes was violent conduct worthy of a straight red, stating there was 'clear contact to the head' and that his action was 'unnecessary, dangerous and made with excessive force'.

On the other hand, two of the panellists supported the on-field call as they viewed the action as aggressive with no excessive force.

As for the opinion on VAR's lack of intervention in the incident, all of the panellists supported the decision to not intervene and supported the referee’s call given that a yellow card was awarded on-field.

3 Palmer was only shown a yellow card on-field by referee Kavanagh after crashing into his Spurs rival in retaliation Credit: Getty



3 But the panel determined that he should have seen red earlier than he eventually did via a second yellow card later in the game Credit: AFP

What other errors did the Premier League panel find?

It was also found that Aston Villa should have been awarded a penalty in their win over Manchester City last month.

Elliot Anderson brought down Johan Manzambi in the box, but nothing was awarded by the officials.

The Premier League Match Incidents Panel have since found that a spot-kick should have been given, as three of the five panellists felt Anderson made no attempt to win the ball.



Two panellists also felt that VAR should have intervened to give the penalty after it wasn't awarded on the pitch.

In total, over the weekend of the eighth round of the season, 30 big calls were made and 26 were deemed to be correct.

And across the season as a whole so far, the Premier League have said that 88 per cent of 162 incidents reviewed by the panel have been deemed to be correct.

Sports.title: James McClean reveals one regret from poppy saga and why he will never forgive Sunderland
Sports.content:
James McClean reveals one regret from poppy saga and why he will never forgive Sunderland

James McClean has a few things he would like to set straight.

The Ireland international sat down with talkSPORT's Jim White to reflect on his long-standing refusal to wear the poppy and the backlash he faced in English football because of it.

3 McClean has always withdrawn from Remembrance Day commemorations Credit: Getty



McClean has maintained that he would wear the poppy if it only represented victims of World War One and World War Two.

But as a man from Derry, where 14 unarmed civilians were killed on 'Bloody Sunday' in 1972, he does not support the Royal British Legion's broader and more universal appeal.

Six of the victims were specifically from Creggan, where McClean grew up surrounded by the Troubles in the nineties.

The Royal British Legion has historically backed McClean, as it did when ex-Manchester United, Chelsea and Serbia midfielder Nemanja Matic opted against wearing the poppy in 2018.



However, a large number of English football fans have always seen it differently, with McClean subjected to widespread abuse throughout his career in the Premier League and the EFL.

The hostility peaked in 2020 when McClean, then at Stoke City, posted a photo of what he described as a 'history lesson' with his kids while dressed in a balaclava - a not-so-subtle nod to Irish Republican Army violence.



He told talkSPORT: "Would I put it on social media [today]? Absolutely not. That's the only regret.

"I knew there would have been certain elements of backlash. Did I know it was going to be as big as it was? Naively, no.



"I thought it would have been taken for what it was. It was a joke. It was supposed to be a joke.

"And I get the insensitivity in thinking that. But for people to genuinely believe that I sat there and actually educated my children on politics is insane.

3 McClean was fined two weeks' wages by Stoke over the social media post Credit: Instagram

"I captured it as a history lesson because of the whole homeschooling [during the pandemic]. So I thought it was funny.



"Quite clearly, to a lot of people, it wasn't funny. And putting it on social media wasn't funny.

"And I took the blows from it. And rightly so."

Sunderland criticised by McClean

McClean holds Sunderland responsible for exacerbating the issue surrounding his decision on the poppy and failing to protect him.

The Black Cats published a statement explaining McClean's stance in November 2012, while insisting it did not represent the club's values.

It read: "As a club, SAFC wholeheartedly supports the Remembrance commemorations. It was James' personal choice not to wear a shirt on this occasion."



A threat was made on his life days later before a trip to face Fulham at Craven Cottage.

"They just completely distanced themselves," McClean said.

"I just turned 23. So my belief was that Sunderland had a duty to care and they would look after me. There was no reason for me not to think that.

"My view to this day is that statement made it a much bigger story than it was - because straight away it just put all eyes on the game and put all eyes on me.

"We wore red and white. Realistically, if that statement doesn't go out, who's going to be looking?



"Not a lot of people would have noticed. Why couldn't that have been an in-house thing?"

When asked about Sunderland fans booing him, McClean responded: "This is what I mean when I say Sunderland hung me out to dry.

"I was 23, so I was still young and naive. Even to this day, I don't know anything.

"For them not to protect me and put that statement out... then when I wanted to address the situation like I eventually got to at Wigan - they wouldn't let me.



"They kept telling me it would blow over. Don't say anything. That made it 10 times worse.

"Looking back, would I have pushed more to make a statement? 100 per cent. But I thought they had my best interests at heart. They didn't. They had their best interests at heart."

When asked whether he forgives Sunderland for the statement, McClean said: "No I don't. That year was hell. It was just me and my wife, we were bringing a young baby into the world, that was not a good year.

"But I'm a lot more resilient for it."

Why does McClean not wear a poppy?

The 37-year-old, who recently left Derry City by mutual consent, reaffirmed his position on the poppy during the interview.



3 McClean had been exiled from the first-team squad at Derry since July amid a dispute Credit: Shutterstock

He said: "The Royal British Legion states quite clearly [the poppy] is for all the fallen and all conflicts. Now, the conflict that happened in the north of Ireland... there was a lot of bloodshed by the British Army.

"As did the IRA, by the way, I'm not sitting here and saying they were angels, but there was no IRA without the British Army. Let's make that very clear.

"So the atrocities that the British Army carried out in my hometown and through the north of Ireland.. you're basically asking me to wear a symbol to basically commemorate them.



"Any sane person over here wouldn't wear a symbol to commemorate the patriotic dead of Ireland. It just wouldn't happen.

"So when you put it in black and white like that, I don't understand why there was such an uproar and why there is to this day."

Sports.title: Tennis icon Rafael Nadal lands surprise new job at Real Madrid despite Barcelona connection
Sports.content:
Real Madrid has announced that Rafael Nadal is set to join the board of directors at the club.

The 22-time Grand Slam winner has to wait until Real's members approve his appointment later this month.

3 Nadal has made a number of appearances on the pitch at Real Madrid matches Credit: Getty

It is currently unclear as to what responsibilities Nadal will hold in the role.

The 40-year-old is a boyhood fan of Los Blancos and has previously been involved with RCD Mallorca.

In July 2010, it was reported that he became a shareholder of the club and owned 10 per cent.

Real Madrid released a statement on Wednesday, it read: "The Board of Directors of Real Madrid CF, meeting today Wednesday, November 4,

"Has agreed to submit to the General Assembly of Delegate Members the ratification of the appointment of Rafael Nadal Parera, member number 67,778 of our club, as a new member of the Board of Directors.

"Rafael Nadal, an honorary member of Real Madrid, is one of the greatest legends in the history of sport and one of the most admired and recognised Spanish athletes in the world.

"For Real Madrid and for all Madrid fans, it is a great source of pride that a figure of his sporting and human stature, a benchmark of Spanish and world sport, will become part of our Board of Directors and contribute, from this position of responsibility, to the present and future of our club.

"With his extraordinary record of 92 individual titles, including 22 Grand Slams, 2 Olympic gold medals, 5 Davis Cups with Spain, and the number 1 ranking in the world, Rafael Nadal has forged a legendary sporting career.

"But his figure represents much more than his successes: his talent, his constant drive to improve, his capacity for sacrifice, his competitiveness, his humility, his respect for rivals and teammates, and his commitment to solidarity make him an example both on and off the court.

"All these values ​​are part of Real Madrid's identity and Rafael Nadal has represented and defended them throughout his sporting life, becoming a role model for millions of people around the world."

3 Perez was re-elected to serve a new four-year term as Real president in June Credit: Getty

The Spaniard took to X and shared a photo of himself as a boy in a Real kit. He said: "I want to thank president Florentino Perez and the board for proposing that I join the board of directors of Real Madrid.

"I have accepted this proposal with great excitement, a desire to learn, and a willingness to contribute everything I can."

Jose Mourinho's team are currently third in La Liga and are three points behind defending champions Barcelona.

Nadal's Barcelona links

Nadal has been noted in the past as an avid supporter of Real Madrid, however, his uncle, Miguel Angel Nadal, played for their arch rivals Barcelona.

He has previously said: "When my uncle (Miguel Angel Nadal) was playing for Barcelona, we wanted Barcelona to win. Before that, my whole family was for Real Madrid.

"After my uncle left the Barcelona team, then we're all for the Real Madrid again. I have got nothing against Barcelona, but I prefer Real Madrid to win."

Miguel was a defensive midfielder who played 208 times for Barcelona between 1991 and 1999.

3 Nadal's uncle, Miguel Angel, is a Barcelona legend Credit: INSTAGRAM

Additionally, he provided three goals across 62 appearances for the Spanish national team.

The 60-year-old represented his nation in three World Cups and Euro 1996, and was nicknamed 'The Beast' for his physicality.

Miguel won five La Liga titles during his time at the Nou Camp and the Cup Winners' Cup in 1997.

He was also appointed the assistant coach of Mallorca when Rafael became a shareholder of the club.

Sports.title: Three year plan for JJ Gabriel proposed before getting near Real Madrid first team
Sports.content:
Three year plan for JJ Gabriel proposed before getting near Real Madrid first team

JJ Gabriel has been told that it won't be Real Madrid's plan for him to join the club and get first-team minutes for now - and nor should it.

The 16-year-old is currently training in the Spanish capital as he finalises a move to Jose Mourinho's side from Manchester United.

5 Gabriel did not make a senior appearance for United, but is one of the most highly-regarded talents in the country Credit: Getty

The England Under-17 turned 16 last month and thus is allowed to depart Old Trafford and sign for clubs abroad.

Gabriel, labelled a 'generational talent' by Man United legend Ryan Giggs, caused a bombshell when he asked to leave in September.

The teen's shock announcement came just five days after scoring a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut for the Red Devils' U19s.

Gabriel was due to make his senior bow in their Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton on September 16, but a row over playing time saw his representatives instead demand that United cancel his registration.

As previously reported by talkSPORT, the Red Devils could receive compensation for as little as £300,000 for their No.77.

However, talkSPORT understands that United have not had club-to-club contact with leading suitors Real Madrid at this stage.

Real Madrid's multi-year plan for JJ Gabriel

Gabriel, who has been training away from Carrington, has already been warned that he is not physically ready for the Premier League.

European football expert Andy Brassell has now cautioned the teenager against having any illusion of game time at Madrid either.

He told talkSPORT.com: "Really what you're looking for, though, is a career plan - just because he's going to Real Madrid... if he does go to Real Madrid. I mean, it doesn't mean he won't get minutes. It just means he won't get minutes for Real Madrid.

5 Gabriel was included in United's first-team squad photo Credit: Getty

"I think if they've got a plan, say year 1: 'You play for a team in the Segunda [second division], year two, we'll loan you out to Getafe or Levante, and year three you go to Como', maybe that's acceptable?

"I know there's been a lot written about his dad, but I think we can make a lot of assumptions.

"I don't think anyone could reasonably expect he'll go to Real Madrid and get minutes. It's just not realistic."

A big part of Madrid's development of players includes using them at other clubs

Gabriel only has to look at Endrick, four years his senior and vying for the same forward minutes, to see Madrid's plan for wonderkids.

The Brazilian was hailed as one of the most exciting young talents in the world upon his move to Los Blancos from Palmeiras in 2024.

5 Endrick has barely featured under Mourinho since the Special One returned to Madrid Credit: Getty

Endrick, who scored eight goals and registered eight assists on loan at Lyon last season, has made just one start in LaLiga this term.

The 20-year-old has continually been linked with a move away from Madrid, who boast a stacked attack after completing the signing of Yan Diomande for a fee worth up to £120million this summer.

Vinicius Junior's decision to snub a move to Arsenal further increased competition for places, while 21-year-old Carlos Espi has had to make do with a back-up role after an 11-goal league campaign with Levante.

Brassell added: "If Endrick, who has everything to be a superstar - the talent, the attitude, the application, the communication skills, of course, he has made a few impacts recently, but I think he's going to want more and more game time if he's not to agitate for a move or at least a temporary move away in January.

"But to me, that's got to be part of the plan for JJ Gabriel. If they're looking to take him there, Real Madrid will have a plan.

"A big part of their development of players includes using them at other clubs. You do look at those relationships that they have with other clubs.

"So, to see him maybe have a year at Castilla, which is not top-division first-team football, it's first-team football of sorts, and then you put him in a Getafe-type situation.

"We've talked about Como before; we know they've got a good relationship with Real Madrid in terms of [Nico] Paz and Jacobo [Ramón] and players like that."

5 Real Madrid have buy-back options on both of Como stars, Jacobo and Paz Credit: Getty

16-year-olds under Jose Mourinho Club Exact age Match involvement Michael Woods Chelsea 6–1 Macclesfield

(FA Cup – 6 January 2007) 16 years, 275 days Came on as an 80th-minute substitute for Frank Lampard Angel Gomes Man Utd 2–0 Crystal Palace

(Premier League – 21 May 2017) 16 years, 263 days Became the first player born in the 2000s to play in the Premier League Dane Scarlett Tottenham 4–0 Ludogorets

(Europa League – 26 Nov. 2020) 16 years, 247 days Also made his Premier League debut while still 16 against West Brom on 7 February 2021. Alfie Devine Marine 0–5 Tottenham

(FA Cup – 10 January 2021) 16 years, 163 days Introduced at half-time and scored, becoming Tottenham's youngest-ever first-team player and goalscorer

Ominously for Gabriel, Mourinho has never fielded a 16-year-old in a competitive game for Madrid in either of his two spells in charge.

In fact, across the Special One's managerial career, only four players have had such an honour - only one of which came in a league game.

On Gabriel, Brassell added: "I think there can be a plan for him, but I think the headline shouldn't really distract from what that plan should be.

"I guess, just like if a big club is loaning a player to a smaller club, the bigger club needs a plan on how that player is going to be developed.

5 Gabriel spent pre-season with the United first team Credit: Getty

"And whatever has been said about JJ Gabriel's entourage and his father and whoever else might be in the decision-making process, and there will be loads, obviously, because A, he's big business and B, he is a child.

"I think if they're doing the right thing for him, they will be looking to be taken through that plan for how he's going to get into first-team football in forensic detail.

"And I don't think it's beyond the realm of possibility that Real Madrid could have that plan.

"But I just don't think it will be in the first team for now, and it shouldn't be."

Sports.title: Rafael Benitez eyeing up Premier League return with four managers under pressure
Sports.content:
Rafael Benitez eyeing up Premier League return with four managers under pressure

Rafael Benitez admits he wants a Premier League return, with four managers under pressure heading into the international break.

The former Liverpool manager has not managed in England since he was sacked by Everton in 2022 after only six months in charge.



3 Rafa Benitez is looking for a way back into football Credit: Getty

He has extensive experience of taking charge of English clubs including his time at Newcastle, Chelsea, and Anfield.

Across his spells in England he won the FA Cup, Champions League, Europa League, and the EFL Championship.

Benitez was last managing in Greece at Panathinaikos on a 2.5 year contract before moving on seven months later in May.



Since, he has become a member of the UEFA Technical Observer Group for the current season to help the organisation to analyse matches, study tactical trends, and contribute to reports.

However, he spoke to talkSPORT on Tuesday evening about his desire to return to the dugout.



Asked about a potential return on talkSPORT Drive, Benitez said: "You know that I'm working now for UEFA, but I'm watching games all the time, and especially the Premier League, because I want to know the players, I want to know their style.

"I could see the other day when I was watching Juventus vs Napoli, then I was watching Liverpool vs Arsenal, and you can see the difference.



"So I like the Premier League because of the intensity. Every game, every ball is a challenge.

" I think it's fantastic. The problem is that you need to find the right project. Talking about projects in football now is quite complicated."

Andy Goldstein then asked: "Would that project be in the Premier League, Rafa?"

Benitez responded: "Yeah, yeah, I would be happy with that, for sure."



3 Benitez won the Coppa Italia and Supercoppa Italiana at Napoli

Goldstein responded: "And what about Napoli? Can you see yourself going back to Napoli?"

Benitez added: "Napoli is a nice place, I have very good memories, but they still have a manager.

"So what I am doing is open, because I am working with UEFA, watching Roma against Real Madrid.



"But I watch the French League, La Liga, Serie A, and the Premier League. They are my favourites, for sure."

Next Premier League manager to be sacked

There has not been a single sacking in the top flight so far this season; however, there are many managers under the microscope.

Michael Carrick was close to being sacked from Manchester United after not winning in nine games; however, he has been given multiple chances from the hierarchy and secured victory in the Champions League on Tuesday against Roma.

3 Despite winning mid-week in the Champions League, Carrick knows he must win this weekend Credit: Getty



Meanwhile, Regis Le Bris is under pressure at bottom-of-the-table Sunderland and Pierre Sage is struggling with Crystal Palace.

Additionally, Oliver Glasner at Nottingham Forest challenged the board to sack him after they were defeated 2-0 by Brentford.

Those four clubs currently sit at the bottom of the Premier League table.
