Sports.title: Goalkeeper involved in fatal collision with Spanish footballer speaks out to reveal his 'enormous pain' and says he will 'face whatever comes' after police opened homicide investigation and fans called him 'murderer'
Sports.content:
Jesus Owono, the goalkeeper involved in the fatal collision with the late Jesus de Miguel, has spoken for the first time since the tragic incident.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Owono collided with opposing striker de Miguel in the latter stages of a hotly contested 2-2 draw with Tenerife in Spain's second division on Monday.

De Miguel immediately collapsed following the devastating blow in which Owono's knee appeared to strike the forward in the chest. He passed away in the early hours of Tuesday morning.

Owono has since shut down his Instagram account amid the significant backlash he has received – which saw him subjected to chants of 'murderer' by the Tenerife fans as he left the pitch – but he has now issued a statement alongside his club.

'FC Andorra continues to be deeply affected by the death of Jesús de Miguel,' they wrote. 'In these very difficult moments, our player Jesús Owono wishes to personally share a few words.'

Owono said: 'These are being the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

Jesus Owono has broken his silence after being involved in a fatal collision with Jesus de Miguel

Tenerife striker de Miguel died on Tuesday morning following the horrifying clash with Owono

'I feel an enormous pain for the loss of Jesús. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address; I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

'But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesús.'

The club added: 'FC Andorra asks for the utmost sensitivity and respect.'

Andorra held a minute's silence at the club's training ground today, and the collision has opened the debate surrounding challenges involving goalkeepers and outfield players in football.

Former Real Madrid and Spain international goalkeeper Santiago Canizares, speaking on El Partidazo de COPE, conceded he believed Owono used ‘excessive force’ when going for the challenge.

Canizares, however, offered a defence of Owono by explaining the goalkeeper’s likely thought process and explained that they typically use their knees as protection and to help avoid collisions.

‘It's a goal-scoring opportunity, and what Owono has in his head is “I have to contest that ball,” ball or player,' Canizares said.

‘For me, the problem is that Owono uses excessive force, and he lacks the physical dexterity to pull himself back when he sees he's won the duel.

‘He goes all out and goes all out until the end. That physical dexterity is key when only one of the two is contesting.

‘What happens in this case is that I think the momentum causes the knee to rise due to the force and excessive speed it brings.’

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line

Owono said he could not 'think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing' (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono)

FC Andorra defender Lautaro Spatz has also defended his team-mate, writing that the goalkeeper has been 'deeply affected' by the tragedy.

'There are moments when football loses its meaning. Moments that mark you forever and make you realise how fragile life can be,' Spatz wrote in a statement shared on social media.

'What we went through is something none of us will ever forget. A tragedy that has left us completely broken, speechless, and with a sadness that is difficult to explain.

'First and foremost, I want to express my deepest condolences and all my love to Jesús’s family, friends, and loved ones, as well as to the entire Tenerife community and the entire football family. Since yesterday, the entire FC Andorra squad has been shocked, devastated, and deeply affected by what has happened. It is a tragedy we never imagined we would experience on a football pitch.'

Spatz continued: 'I also want to say a few words to my teammate, goalkeeper, and friend, who is deeply affected by what happened. Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is. We know how much he is suffering right now and that he would never intend to hurt anyone.

'In football, unforeseen events occur, but no one can imagine that one of them could end with such tragic consequences. Today, football doesn't matter. All that remains is to offer our condolences, show the utmost respect, and send all our strength to the family and to all those suffering this terrible loss. Rest in peace, Demi.'

Police investigating de Miguel's death are now probing the emergency medical response as well as the possibility Owono's horror tackle could be involuntary manslaughter.

It emerged yesterday homicide squad officers based in the Tenerife capital Santa Cruz had launched a probe as court officials explained any death 'not resulting from natural causes' automatically triggers a judicial investigation.

Police are investigating the death of de Miguel due to protocol, and they are also now probing the emergency medical response

Legal experts have said they don't expect the ongoing investigation to lead to criminal charges against Owono because the clash occurred during open play, although he is expected to be hit with a lengthy ban.

But overnight it emerged the police probe will also review the medical response to Monday's emergency and seek to address questions about whether de Miguel was given oxygen on the pitch and whether a defibrillator was used from the outset as well as issues around the assistance he received during his ambulance transfer.

The 30-year-old father-of-one died on Tuesday morning at Nuestra Senora Candelaria University Hospital after his club revealed his neurological condition had worsened.

Medical personnel involved in the footballer's care are expected to be questioned and detectives will sift through medical reports as part of the probe.

Sports.title: Revealed: How Arsenal have used NASA to tackle their injury woes - with Google and Apple joining the fight
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta has often stretched the boundaries of quirkiness in his pursuit of excellence at Arsenal - and it can now be revealed that his search for those marginal gains has seen the club quite literally reaching for the stars.

Injuries are once again the focus for Arteta after Bukayo Saka sustained a thigh strain at Bayern Munich two weeks ago. He is expected to be ruled out for four to six weeks. It is the 25-year-old’s 11th injury since September 2024.

Arsenal have been blighted by injury, and Arteta has been fixated on reducing the problem ever since the 2022-23 campaign - where William Saliba’s absence cost them dear in the Premier League run-in.

But what are they doing to fix it? Daily Mail Sport can reveal that Arsenal staff have in recent seasons been tasked with reaching out to blue-chip companies, seeking innovative ways which could help lower the number of injuries and accelerate recovery.

Earlier in Arteta's Arsenal reign, NASA were consulted on their expertise in space physiology, specifically in relation to ACL injuries.

In space, the reduced load on the human body – because of less gravity – contributes to muscle atrophy and bone density loss. As a result, NASA have conducted extensive research into what happens to the body under reduced gravity, and how it responds when back on Earth.

Injuries are the one area that Mikel Arteta has been unable to solve in his quest to find marginal gains

Bukayo Saka went off inside 10 minutes at Bayern Munich last month, having suffered his 11th injury in just over two years

Arsenal believed there could be valuable lessons to apply to their ACL rehabilitation process. This includes exploring areas such as how much weight an injured player should bear at different stages, how quickly that load should be increased, how reduced-gravity exercise can allow players to resume running and loading movements earlier, and how to measure whether a player’s body is actually tolerating those increased demands.

The issue has been particularly pertinent given Arsenal's experiences in recent seasons. Jurrien Timber ruptured his ACL on his Premier League debut against Nottingham Forest in August 2023, ruling him out for nearly nine months, and Gabriel Jesus spent 332 days out when he suffered the same injury in January 2025.

The problem has not been confined to the men’s team. Arsenal women's side have also endured a troubling run of ACL injuries, with several high-profile players affected in recent seasons. Leah Williamson, Beth Mead, Vivianne Miedema and Victoria Pelova all suffered ACL injuries in the 2022-23 season, while Manuela Zinsberger, Michelle Agyemang and Katie Reid have all had the same injury in the past 18 months.

NASA aren’t the only high-tech addition to Arsenal’s crackdown on injuries. It’s understood that Google, one of the club’s official partners, were consulted on data analytics. The company’s expertise in processing vast quantities of information could help identify patterns associated with injury risk, spotting subtle changes in running mechanics or physical output.

Similarly, Apple were consulted about using wearable technology to collect physiological data and build a clearer picture of how players respond to training and rehabilitation. This included the use of Apple Watches to track metrics such as heart rate and exercise intensity.

Arsenal’s global brand helps in these partnerships. It’s ultimately a passport into world-leading organisations, who are often intrigued by the prospect of working with a major sports side.

How effective Arsenal's attempts have been is difficult to measure, as a multitude of factors contribute toinjuries, some of which are out of the club’s control. The number of players injured at Arsenal in recent years, though, have suggested a disproportionate problem compared to other sides.

One noteworthy example, given what has happened since, is the Champions League match against Club Bruges on December 10, 2025. Seven players were out: William Saliba, Gabriel, Cristhian Mosquera, Declan Rice, Kai Havertz, Leandro Trossard and Max Dowman. It took Arsenal’s injury total at that stage to 95 (excluding Rice’s illness) since the start of the 2024–25 Premier League season – only Brighton had more (97).

Jurrien Timber was struck down with an ACL injury in his Premier League debut in August 2023

Gabriel Jesus also suffered an ACL injury in January 2025, ruling him out for almost the entire calendar year

William Saliba's injury in March 2023 proved fatal for Arsenal's title charge, with Rob Holding unable to play in the same high line as Manchester City hunted the Gunners down

The club instigated a mass medical team shake-up last summer kickstarted by the appointment of Spanish physio Joaquin Acedo, a long-term Arteta associate from when he was a Real Sociedad player over two decades ago. Among the other new arrivals are head of medical services Dr Arnaldo Abrantes and physiotherapist Carmen Marquez, who both joined from Aston Villa, head of player rehabilitation Eneko Angulo and fitness coach Jose Jimenez.

A slogan on the wall in Arsenal's medical room which reads: ‘Your best ability is availability’ says it all.

This season, Arsenal have not yet been as badly affected by injuries. Aside from Saliba and Saka, Christos Tzolis, Ben White and Mosquera have all spent time out, while Eberechi Eze recently picked up an unspecified injury.

It is the impact of missing key players at crucial times which has irked Arteta the most. While the 2023 title charge was killed off when Saliba had to be replaced by Rob Holding, who was unable to maintain the same high line and press, the 2024-2025 season fell apart when Jesus and Havertz were injured in January, leaving only midfielder Mikel Merino to play up front.

Last term Havertz started just seven league games after damaging his knee ligaments in the opener at Manchester United.

Perhaps the most Arteta-like thing about all this is that, even after turning to NASA, Google and Apple for answers, the search for an edge never really stops.

Sports.title: Newcastle Confidential: REVEALED - Players 'confused' by Matthias Jaissle's instructions, why formation tweak is a possibility, Joelinton injury worry and new transfer guru's methods explained
Sports.content:
Newcastle’s players are ‘confused’ by what Matthias Jaissle wants from them, a source close to the dressing room has told me.

I've been told the squad remains supportive of Jaissle and there is a determination to get things right for the head coach – senior players accept there is a responsibility on them – but there is also a desire for clarity over what it is they are being asked to do on the field.

Jaissle said in the wake of Monday's 1-0 home defeat by Everton that he could not understand why the team had not followed his instructions and executed the tactics they had worked on in training. He said the plan was not to play ‘long balls’.

Sources also say Jaissle spoke to his players afterwards about their press not being what he wanted and their passing being too slow in the opposition half.

However, I have been told some players are unsure as to the playing style and strategy, and that has led to those in deep positions getting the ball forward as quickly as possible, invariably with a long pass. There are also some within the dressing room wondering why the team continues to play with a No 10 when they do not have a specialist in that position.

Another source close to a senior player says the logical solution is a return to the 4-3-3 of recent seasons. There was word from inside the training ground that Jaissle was considering such a change ahead of the trip to Crystal Palace last month, so it is not off the table.

The demand from supporters to find a place for teenager Sean Steur in the midfield could yet see a tweak to the system, especially as Jaissle believes he and Nico Gonzalez are not suited to playing together as a two.

Newcastle's players are understood to be 'confused' by what it is head coach Matthias Jaissle wants from them

The demand from supporters to find a place for teenager Sean Steur (left) in the midfield could yet see a tweak to the Newcastle system

JOELINTON FITNESS WORRY

Joelinton is a fresh injury concern and medical staff will know in the next 24 hours if he is set to miss Saturday’s trip to Fulham, I can reveal. The Brazilian was feeling some muscle discomfort post-match on Monday and there is hope that the issue is related to a severe case of cramp.

However, I understand that is yet to be confirmed and, given Joelinton’s history of muscle strains, including his hamstring, no chances will be taken. The 30-year-old only returned from a thigh injury three weeks ago having been sidelined since the summer.

FERNANDEZ-PARDO AND MILEY BACK IN ACTION

In better news, Matias Fernandez-Pardo and Lewis Miley are set to return for the game at Craven Cottage.

I understand Fernandez-Pardo wanted to be included in the squad for the visit of Everton but was told by staff he needed more training. The Belgian had missed the previous two matches with what is being described as a ‘tricky virus’ and only returned to training over the weekend.

Fernandez-Pardo arrived on Tyneside insisting he wanted to be used as a central striker following his £51million move from Lille. However, Jaissle currently prefers William Osula in that position and Fernandez-Pardo will likely be competing for a place out wide at Craven Cottage.

Miley, meanwhile, was also pushing for involvement on Monday after recovering from a glute issue. The 20-year-old’s return is timely given the midfield struggles of late, as well as the fresh worry over Joelinton and Jacob Ramsey’s suspension following his red card against Everton.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is available again for Newcastle after suffering with a ‘tricky virus’

NO LOAN FOR BAMBA

One player who almost certainly won’t come in for a start is Aladji Bamba, although we are told he will NOT be going out on loan in January.

The 20-year-old has appeared for just 27 minutes since his £30m arrival from Monaco in the summer, and he has not featured at all since September 19.

But despite potential availability issues in midfield, Jaissle does not feel Bamba is ready to start Premier League matches. That has led to a suggestion among some that he could be loaned out in January, especially as he has made only 12 senior starts in his career.

However, I understand the plan is for Bamba to remain on Tyneside and there has been encouragement with his recent performances in training.

Aladji Bamba has impressed in training of late and won't leave on loan in January despite his lack of first-team minutes

TRANSFER GURU'S METHODS REVEALED

It has been interesting speaking to those who know a little more about Newcastle's new head of recruitment Tomas Amaral, who was virtually unknown in the UK before his appointment last month.

The Portuguese, 35, has been described as a 'bookworm and laptop obsessive', a meticulous talent-spotter who works long into the night. Amaral, who spent four years scouting for Benfica and was most recently sporting director at Spartak Moscow, has also spoken previously of the dangers of clubs signing good players who do not fit the manager's system.

He believes recruitment should begin with a clear footballing identity, rather than collecting talented individuals and hoping they somehow fit together. He also argues that scouts should challenge managers over transfer targets, rather than simply indulge their wishes.

Interestingly, his recruitment strategy involves two lists – one identifying players good enough for the club, the other those specifically suited to the manager's demands. For him, character and adaptability are considered just as important as ability.

He was part of the Benfica scouting team who identified Enzo Fernandez when signing him from River Plate in 2022. The midfielder was sold to Chelsea for a near £100m profit the following year.

Amaral’s arrival at least gives clarity to the recruitment structure inside St James’ Park, and he would appear to have a busy 12 months ahead given what feel like obvious areas for improvement across the pitch. I understand there is scope to spend in January should the club feel it necessary.

GAMBIA KIDS ON TRIAL

Beneath first-team level, Newcastle have cast their scouting net a little wider this week with two promising teenagers from Gambia arriving on Tyneside.

We understand Omar Marong and Alieu Saine, both 16, will stay for a two-week trial and train with the academy. They are products of the Today Makes Tomorrow Academy and have been identified under the club’s new global talent drive.

The pair caught the eye during Gambia’s triumph at September’s West African Under-17 Championship. Central midfielder Marong captained the side, while winger Saine finished as joint-top scorer with four goals. Neither player can join permanently until turning 18 because of FIFA regulations, but Newcastle are keen to assess their potential.

Meanwhile, the club are also set to appoint a specialist scout in Africa.

FERREIRA TUG OF WAR?

Finally, Newcastle prospect Matheos Ferreira could soon be at the centre of an international tug of war.

The 18-year-old, born in Ashington and raised in Berwick, has been called up by Brazil Under 20s for friendlies against Japan and Singapore this month. He is the only English-based player in the squad.

Newcastle prospect Matheos Ferreira could play for England, Italy or Brazil

But Ferreira, whose father is Brazilian and mother Italian, also qualifies for England and Italy. He has previously represented England at youth level and recently obtained an Italian passport.

I have seen him play a handful of times and there is certainly plenty of talent and potential. Interestingly, he has been operating as a No 10 at times this season, having come through the ranks as a winger.

Maybe there is a No 10 inside the club after all…

Sports.title: Unai Emery has closed gap between Aston Villa and Europe's elite - but rampant Barcelona proved there is still a way to go as Lamine Yamal dazzles, writes OLIVER HOLT
Sports.content:
John McGinn heard the question. His eyes darted around Barcelona's packed media auditorium for a second or two on Monday night. What was it like to be about to play in the Nou Camp, the Aston Villa skipper had been asked, as if this were to be some sort of spin off from Bill and Ted's Excellent Adventure. McGinn was careful with his answer. He did not seek to downplay the nature of the occasion or the thrill that comes with lining up in such a majestic arena. But he was determined not to play the wide-eyed ingenu. 'What our club is trying to do now,' McGinn said, 'is make this normal, make this a yearly experience.' So when he and his team-mates walked up the flight of steps from the dressing rooms into the vast bowl of the stadium on Tuesday evening, they were here to show that they were not arrivistes. Villa is a historic club. They won this competition in 1982, ten years before Barcelona ever did. They were not here for a treat or to get patted on the back just for turning up. It is nearly 20 years since Liverpool became the last English club to win here and nobody gave Villa too much chance of ending that drought. They are being told constantly that the odds are stacked against them and that their much-admired manager, Unai Emery, may be tempted by the entreaties of struggling 'giants' elsewhere. That was the reason why this game early in the league phase had attained so much importance. For Villa, it was a symbol of something they aspire to. They want to get used to belonging in this company, to walking up those steps, to emerging into the stadium in the pouring rain, and staring at players of the calibre of Lamine Yamal, Rodri and Pau Cubarsi staring back at them. It still feels as if they stand on the cusp of something bigger but they blew their shot at proving that on Tuesday night. They needed to be at their best to have a chance of beating Hansi Flick's side, which sits atop LaLiga, and they were far too naïve in defence to get close to causing a shock. They are rising but this was a step too far at this stage of their evolution. Lamine Yamal (centre) and Barcelona had plenty to smile about after beating Aston Villa 3-0 Yamal opened the scoring for Barcelona after just seven minutes with this left-footed finish Raphinha (right) doubled Barca's lead after half-time with this strike at the Spotify Nou Camp The Nou Camp, which is still in the midst of an extensive renovation and was only about two-thirds full, was ringed by towering yellow cranes, peering down at the floodlit patch of green. From their lofty vantage point, they saw Villa get off to the worst possible start. Only seven minutes had gone when Emery's team gift-wrapped a present for the home side. Zion Suzuki played the ball out short to Joao Gomes but Gomes panicked under pressure from the Barcelona press and the close attention of Pedri. He played the ball square without looking, straight to Yamal. Of all the players he could have found, Gomes had to find Yamal. The Spain superstar squared up Pau Torres and then curled the ball around him with a gentle caress of his left boot. Suzuki was helpless. The ball nestled in the corner of the net. Barcelona had scored 56 goals in 14 games before this match. Extending the hand of generosity to them must have felt particularly galling for Emery. Villa almost hit back immediately. A stinging volley from Matty Cash was deflected wide and Barcelona looked jittery at the back. Nicolas Jackson played a square ball to Johan Manzambi, who should have equalised but scuffed his first-time effort wide of Joan Garcia. Barcelona were thankful for Garcia's intervention when he raced out of his goal to dispossess Jackson as he charged on to a through ball. Yamal was rampant. His battle with Ian Maatsen was a mismatch and Maatsen was booked after 11 minutes for hacking him down. Villa were still intent on playing themselves into trouble. Suzuki repeated his mistake when he tried to play the ball out to Joao Gomes. This time, Pedri beat him to it and the loose ball fell to Gordon. Gordon hit his shot towards the corner but Suzuki redeemed himself by diving to push it away. Barcelona had the better of the play. They looked like scoring every time they went forward. Time and again, either Raphinha or Yamal found space to run at the Villa defence, which was barely coping. Even in that context, though, it was an open game. Villa had chances, too. Manzambi forced a fine save out of Garcia. A Jackson breakaway was thwarted by a last-ditch block. But seven minutes after the break, Barcelona doubled their lead. Fermin Lopez played a clever ball to Raphinha, who had found a yard of space in the box. Raphinha, LaLiga's leading scorer this season, drilled a left-foot shot goalwards and it deflected off the heel of Torres, wrong-footed Suzuki and rolled over the line. Barcelona put the game out of reach midway through the half when Joao Cancelo forced his way past McGinn on the left flank and hit a sumptuous cross into the box with the outside of his right foot. Raphinha gambled on the path of the ball, darted behind his marker and tucked the ball away. Raphinha completed the scoreline with this cute finish as Barcelona completed their victory For Aston Villa, this will be a learning curve as they look to go far in the Champions League Villa manager Unai Emery will have plenty to think about after another Nou Camp defeat Substitute Leon Goretzka hit the face of a post for Villa late on but the game was already gone. There was no shame in losing to a team who are one of the favourites to win the competition this season but there was frustration in the way Villa had handed their opponents the advantage. Emery looked bedraggled as he stood on the touchline in the rain, arms folded, shaking his head. This was his 15th defeat in 16 visits to the Nou Camp. As Villa's coach fights to edge his team closer to the elite of the game, this game will become just one more bad memory. Sports.title: Michael Carrick might STILL be one game from the sack. A one-night stand of epic proportions was up there with Man United's best but produced more questions than answers, writes CHRIS WHEELER
Sports.content:
What a crazy, chaotic and, frankly, confusing night this was at Old Trafford. The grand old place has seen a few of them down the years, and Manchester United's incredible comeback win over Roma was right up there with the best. By the end of it, the fans were loving United and hating the Glazers in keeping with their doctrine. Michael Carrick was savouring arguably his greatest moment as head coach, and yet might still be one game from the sack. Two-goal hero Matheus Cunha was being manhandled off the pitch and towards the tunnel, furious at not being able to celebrate with his teammates. For Carrick, this felt like the equivalent of Erik ten Hag's win over Manchester City in the 2024 FA Cup final and Ruben Amorim's incredible 4-3 victory over Lyon in the Europa League quarter-final last year. The feelgood factor and sense of elation around Old Trafford was palpable. Neither of those wins were enough to keep Ten Hag and Amorim in a job for much longer, and that is the conundrum for United bosses this morning. If the feeling in the boardroom – and it remains an if – is to relieve Carrick of his duties, can they be swayed by a one-night stand, albeit one of epic proportions. If United can follow this up with victory on Sunday over Aston Villa and Unai Emery – one of the candidates being touted as Carrick's replacement – can they really sack their head coach at the start of the international break? Michael Carrick gave his players the half-time fire power needed to pull off a famous fightback More than just pulling off the much-needed win against Roma, it felt as if his stars were playing for their manager On another night when United fans turned on the Glazers, Sir Jim Ratcliffe, director of football Jason Wilcox and even the players as boos greeted the half-time whistle and the 'play like you mean it' banner made a re-appearance for the first time in three years, it was a reminder that the most popular person at the club might be the man who is about to get the bullet. The players certainly looked as though they are playing for Carrick, and afterwards Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans both gave him their backing. Looking ahead to this game, Carrick had said: 'Whatever happens is going to happen after that in whatever direction it goes in, but we want to make it a big night tomorrow night first.' Those words came true in spectacular fashion. For a while, it felt as though he wouldn't even survive until the Villa game as United's defence fell apart and Roma set a new record for a European opponent taking a two-goal lead at Old Trafford. It could have been worse. Carrick got his players together at half-time and reminded them that it only takes one moment to light the touchpaper here. 'I don't like talking to the lads too much about the history of this place, but it's magical,' he said. 'There's something when we have these nights and we do it the hard way, and one moment can flip the whole feeling.' Kobbie Mainoo put it more bluntly. 'We needed a bit of a kick,' said the United midfielder. It worked. United roared back at Roma, showing a resolve and strength of character that has been missing for much of this season. Fernandes converted a retaken penalty, Cunha levelled and then smashed home the winner late on to give United their first victory in 10 games. The Brazilian's sending-off for removing his shirt after scoring the third and then committing a silly foul on Leonardo Balerdi meant he wasn't allowed to go on the pitch at the end, much to his indignation. Carrick and his staff were there to reinforce the point. Results clearly haven't been good enough this season, but one of the criticisms levelled at Carrick is that performances have been even worse. The combination of those two factors have left him fighting to save his job. On the flip side, it felt like this win and the nature of it counted double. One that raised the roof at Old Trafford and lifted the soul. Yet for so long on Tuesday night, the mood among the United faithful was one of mutiny. They revived the anti-Glazer campaign by bringing green and gold balloons into the Stretford End, and let them loose as the two teams walked out. Rather like the protests against the absent owners who keep a safe distance thousands of miles away in America, they were never going to hit their target by reaching the pitch and floated harmlessly into the night air. A barrage of tennis balls had greater impact, but they too were soon cleared out of sight. Chants against the Glazers, Ratcliffe and Wilcox rang out long before kick-off. 'You can stick your new stadium up your a***' chanted the fans. The game was seconds old when we heard the first rendition of 'sell United and f*** off home' followed by the tribute song to Carrick. Even at a critical point in the game when VAR was studying Gianluca Mancini's challenge on Cunha to see if it warranted a penalty, the United fans broke into a chorus of 'we want Glazers out'. It was the same after Cunha fired the decisive goal as supporters turned on the Americans and voiced their support for Carrick once more. They were caught between wanting to vent their anger at the owners and back Carrick and the team. Fervent and continuing protests against the ownership underscored Carrick's own popularity, despite being potentially days from getting the sack Matheus Cunha might have been the late hero but he was unable to celebrate with his team-mates and manager after taking off his shirt 'The players one hundred per cent feed off the crowd, absolutely no doubt whatsoever,' said Carrick. 'I understand there's frustration and disappointment, I totally get that. 'Probably the time when it was easy for them not to be there, they were there. I felt that there was frustration, of course there was. I get it. But I know what they're like and we've got to give them something to go on.' United managed to do that in the end, but it was a funny sort of night. One that produced more questions than answers. The biggest of them concerns Carrick. Is he doing enough to convince his employers that United can turn a corner? Victory in Europe doesn't alter the fact they are one place above the Premier League relegation zone. There is one more game against Villa and then the choice is very simple: stick or twist?

Sports.title: Man United conjured a miraculous comeback against Roma that was thrilling, visceral and raw... finally Michael Carrick has something to cling to, writes IAN LADYMAN
Sports.content:
Once again they sang Michael Carrick's name and this time it was not out of sympathy. This time it was different.

This time there had been some guts and this time there had been some glory. This time, most importantly, there had been a victory. So the Stretford End sang Carrick's name out of thanks. Finally some respite from the relentless misery of this tortuous season.

How Carrick's Manchester United team pulled off this comeback is hard to fathom. But for now all that matters to Carrick is that they did. For at last he has something tangible to cling to as he tries to drag his club's season back from the jaws of hell.

How on earth do we describe this game? Maybe just with the facts.

Carrick's team were so bad in the first half it was almost impossible to understand. However awful they have been this season, this was worse. Two down to early goals from Matias Soule and Donyell Malen, United presented both to Roma on a plate.

The game looked over. United's Champions League season looked over. Carrick's reign felt over.

Matheus Cunha's late double rescued Manchester United from the jaws of defeat on a night of madness at Old Trafford

Cunha scored in the 83rd and 86th minute to turn the game on its head against Roma

There was still time for Cunha to be sent off in the dying embers of the game - but that failed to take the shine off a memorable night

In the crowd they waved green and gold balloons in protest at the owners the Glazers. Then they threw tennis balls on to the field. The only surprise was that none of the United players put one in their own net.

But then, somehow and almost impossibly, this game changed. Whether it will be enough to prompt a genuine shift in the course of United's season, only time will tell. The chances are it won't. There is too much wrong.

And United were lucky, too.

They were lucky to be given an early second-half penalty and lucky that Bruno Fernandes was given the chance to take it again after he missed the first one. They were then lucky in the 83rd minute when Matheus Cunha was handed an equaliser by a defensive howler.

But luck is no good if you don't ride it. And the winning goal Cunha delivered into the net at the near post with four minutes left was not about luck. It was about a team and a player seizing the opportunity to write a different story.

It was born of desire, desperation and perhaps some anger after the pain of the last few weeks. Within a second, the Brazilian's shirt was off and he was in the crowd.

It was hard to blame Cunha, even if he was to pay a price. Booked for that, he was soon cautioned again for a foul and was forced to leave the scene early. At least it was to an ovation. We have not heard one of those here for a while.

Old Trafford was jumping. Of course it was. Thus far this season has brought United supporters only embarrassment and at times earlier here this had felt like a new low. The way United played in the first half was arguably worse than anything we saw under Ruben Amorim and Erik ten Hag.

Matias Soule had given Roma the lead after only 11 minutes

The game was briefly halted in the first-half when fans threw objects including tennis balls onto the pitch

United boss Michael Carrick suffered a further blow when Carlos Baleba limped off

United were in full self-harm mode and in truth could have been four down by half-time.

There was actually nothing in this game for the first 10 minutes but United hurtled from safety to dire straits in the space of seven minutes. That's the way it tends to go and the first Roma goal was simply extraordinary.

When United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo lost the ball in his own half, his team found themselves a defender short. Diogo Dalot, the left back, was so far up field he may as well have been on the Stretford End.

When Rodrigo Mora switched the ball across into the space where Dalot should have been, Soule had time to cut inside and shoot low in to Senne Lammens' bottom left hand corner.

It was one of those goals that looked stranger the more you studied it. Six minutes later, United presented Roma with another one.

Once again Dalot was out of position as the ball reached goalscorer Soule on the edge of the penalty area. This time only a sliding block from Leny Yoro denied the Argentine his second goal but the ball had struck the defender's raised arm and former Aston Villa forward Malen slid in the penalty.

United were shambolic. Fernandes was booked for being, well, Fernandes. It was a harsh card but sadly the United captain's reputation now precedes him. It's the way it works in sport.

As half-time neared, Malen brought a low save from Lammens before Soule curled one from 18 yards that must have missed the righthand post by no more than six inches.

That was the difference between United being out of the game and still in with the chance of the kind of comeback they eventually produced.

Cunha was desperately fortunate to be awarded the penalty that started it all just before the hour. He seemed to trip himself up. Fernandes was then lucky to be offered a retake after his first kick was saved. The level of encroachment by a Roma defender didn't seem to meet the threshold written in law.

But once Fernandes smashed the retake high into the net Roma suddenly found themselves facing a different home team and a different environment.

Bruno Fernandes' first penalty was saved - but he made amends with his second after the referee ordered a retake for encroachment

Victory eases the pressure on United boss Michael Carrick

Carrick will perhaps argue he deserves some fortune. He certainly didn't get any as his team lost at Chelsea at the weekend. Nevertheless, his team needed some more.

Bryan Mbeumo had struck both posts with one shot after running clear immediately after Fernandes' goal while a header from Harry Maguire at a corner hit an opponent when it appeared to be heading in.

But United's fire seemed to be on the verge of burning out when a harmless 83rd-minute cross from Fernandes was completely missed by Roma defender Leonardo Balerdi to present Cunha with an equaliser from six yards.

Roma were by now a shell of the team that they had been in the first half. They had been knocked from their feet by a red tidal wave, and when Cunha unleashed a hammer shot from an angle three minutes later they were dead.

Sports.title: Charles Leclerc is a father! F1 star and new wife Alexandra announce birth of their first daughter, eight months after their Monaco wedding
Sports.content:
Charles Leclerc is a father! F1 star and new wife Alexandra announce birth of their first daughter, eight months after their Monaco wedding

Formula One star Charles Leclerc and his wife Alexandra have announced the birth of their first child.

The couple, who married in Monaco in February, made the announcement on social media to welcome their new daughter Bianca.

In a joint-post on Instagram, they shared a photo of Bianca's legs and feet wrapped up, with the caption: 'Bianca. 3.11.26', alongside a love heart.

Several fans were quick to share their congratulations in the comments for F1's power couple.

Leclerc flew back to Monaco in the aftermath of Sunday's Mexican Grand Prix in order to attend the birth.

He is expected to head to Brazil in the coming days ahead of this weekend's race in Sao Paulo, although some reports in Italy suggested that Ferrari reserve driver Dino Beganovic could take over his duties for the first practice session.

Charles Leclerc and his wife Alexandra announced the birth of their daughter Bianca (Source: Instagram/Charles Leclerc)

Bianca is the first child of Charles and Alexandra, who married in Monaco in February

Bianca's arrival comes eight months after the Ferrari driver, 29, and 25-year-old art historian Alexandra Saint Mleux tied the knot in his homeland, a week before the 2026 season began.

Their miniature dachshund, Leo, was among those at the picturesque ceremony, and the newlyweds were later filmed driving away in a vintage Ferrari.

Following the big day, Leclerc revealed a number of details in a social media video, including showing off his new wife's dress, the exchanging of the rings and their dog's presence.

Footage also showed the couple being greeted and congratulated by their guests, with another clip showing them driving in the Ferrari.

It was a 1957 Ferrari 250 Testa Rossa, which costs around £9million, driven by the nine-time Grand Prix winner.

It is one of the most valuable vintage Ferraris, particularly given the racing success and significance of the model for the legendary Italian company.

He also posted on X: 'A day we'll forever remember. Part one is done and part 2 will be next year with all of our close ones.'

Leclerc had previously spoken about wanting to start a family alongside his career.

Last year, he said: 'I have more personal aspirations, like starting a family, which I can achieve by continuing to chase the world title.'

Alexandra, 25, is a regular alongside her husband and dog Leo in the Formula One paddock

The couple are regularly seen together alongside Leo at races, although this behaviour was criticised by former British driver David Coulthard back in September.

Leclerc is currently fifth in the drivers' standings and Coulthard claimed his actions in the paddock were doing 'too much'.

'He's good looking, he's got the family, a baby on the way, a dog in the paddock,' Coulthard said on the Up To Speed podcast. 'My opinion is that's all a bit too much, frankly.

'It's not a weekend away picnic, is it? It's a Grand Prix, it's a serious business. It's a dangerous business, but that's probably me being of an older generation.

'They (Ferrari) don't have a choice. They've employed two of the best drivers in the world. You then manage them as best you can.'

Sports.title: Rio Ferdinand makes fresh demand to Man Utd star who 'hasn't been doing it enough'
Sports.content:
Rio Ferdinand makes fresh demand to Man Utd star who 'hasn't been doing it enough'

Matheus Cunha's late brace saw Manchester United see off Roma in the Champions League - with Rio Ferdinand demanding the Brazilian maintain that level

View 2 Images Rio Ferdinand has laid out his demands for Matheus Cunha (Image: Getty Images)

Rio Ferdinand hopes that Matheus Cunha's match winning brace for Manchester United serves to kick on his career at Old Trafford as he concedes the Brazilian has not delivered enough.

‌



‌



Cunha is into his second year in Manchester having moved from Wolves for £62.5million, but has been part of a team that's been regularly criticised following a nine-game winless run. That was snapped with a comeback win over Roma on Tuesday night.

‌



Cunha scored twice in the final 10 minutes as United came back from 2-0 down to win 3-2, leading to huge celebrations at Old Trafford. The Brazilian was sent off in the final moments of the game, but Ferdinand still sees it as the benchmark going forward.

‌



Last term Cunha impressed in patches, scoring 10 times, but his display in midweek was his most defining in a red shirt to date and Ferdinand is now hoping for more.

‌



He said on his YouTube channel: "I think for Cunha this could be liftoff where he starts to catch fire,’ Ferdinand said on his YouTube channel. ‘I think he’s a hugely talented footballer and he showed glimpses, especially last season.

"Could this be the game that unlocks him? Because I haven’t seen it enough yet with him. You see moments, and you go, 'Oh, look at that, that’s why we paid the big money for him', but not enough.

‌



"He needs to be watching back that performance and go, where were the fans feeding off me there? Where was I getting them going? Where was I getting the team and being the pressure point for the team? It was without the ball a lot of the time. And keep bringing that every game."

View 2 Images Matheus Cunha was Man Utd's match winner on Tuesday (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Cunha has had to show his versatility this season with United's only genuine No 9, Benjamin Sesko, out injured. That has seen the ex-Wolves man having to lead the line on occasion.

The 28-year-old acknowledged their recent struggles, but maintained he needed to be the type of player who stood up when the chips were down.

‌



He said: “I think everything, when we tried to do it, being part of Man Utd is very hard because in these kinds of moments in the season, we know we always have these kinds of comparisons with the past. We need to have these kinds of games like today, and then we’ll pass the hard moment. But today was a blessed day for me.

“Being part of this, I have a responsibility. I always talk inside about that – I need to be this kind of guy – to have the responsibility in the hard moments and the good moments. I always need to show up and be there for nights like today.”

Sports.title: Goalkeeper involved in fatal Jesus de Miguel incident breaks silence as police launch investigation
Sports.content:
Goalkeeper involved in fatal Jesus de Miguel incident breaks silence as police launch investigation

The goalkeeper who was involved in the fatal incident with Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel has spoken out for the first time

View 4 Images Jesus Owono has released a statement

Goalkeeper Jesus Owono says he feels "enormous pain" after being involved in the fatal collision with Tenerife star Jesus de Miguel. Owono has released a statement alongside his club, Andorra, expressing that he is going through the most difficult days of his life.

‌



‌



The shotstopper collided with De Miguel close to the halfway line during a match in Spain's second division. The Tenerife ace was hit in the chest by Owono's knee and he quickly collapsed on the floor, with players on the field calling for help.

‌



De Miguel was taken to hospital for treatment but tragically died on Tuesday after suffering a cardiac arrest. A routine investigation regarding possible involuntary manslaughter has since been opened by Spanish police.

‌



The incident has left Spanish football in a state of mourning following the 30-year-old's death. Owono has faced backlash for his challenge, which led him to shut down his Instagram account, but he has now spoken about the tragedy.

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



In a statement, FC Andorra said: "FC Andorra continues to be deeply affected by the death of Jesús de Miguel. In these very difficult moments, our player Jesus Owono wishes to personally share a few words."

Owono said: "These are the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

‌



"I feel an enormous pain for the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address; I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

View 4 Images Jesus de Miguel passed away in hospital on Tuesday (Image: Andres Gutierrez/Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



"But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything else except Jesus and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus."

The club added: "FC Andorra asks for the utmost sensitivity and respect."

‌



Santa Cruz de Tenerife chief prosecutor Jose Luis Sanchez-Jauregui said that criminal proceedings against Owono are 'very unlikely'. The goalkeeper's teammate, Lautaro Spatz, has jumped to Owono's defence.

Spatz wrote: "There are moments when football loses its meaning. Moments that mark you forever and make you realise how fragile life can be. What we went through is something none of us will ever forget.

‌



View 4 Images Fans lit candles and left flowers for Jesus de Miguel (Image: Getty Images)

"A tragedy that has left us completely broken, speechless and with a sadness that is difficult to explain. First and foremost, I want to express my deepest condolences and all my love to Jesus' family, friends, and loved ones, as well as to the entire Tenerife community and the entire football family.

‌



"Since yesterday, the entire FC Andorra squad has been shocked, devastated, and deeply affected by what has happened. It is a tragedy we never imagined we would experience on a football pitch.

"I also want to say a few words to my teammate, goalkeeper, and friend, who is deeply affected by what happened. Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is.

‌



"We know how much he is suffering right now and that he would never intend to hurt anyone. In football, unforeseen events occur, but no one can imagine that one of them could end with such tragic consequences.

View 4 Images Fans of CD Tenerife lay flowers and pay tribute to Jesus de Miguel Alameda (Image: Andres Gutierrez/Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



"Today, football doesn't matter. All that remains is to offer our condolences, show the utmost respect, and send all our strength to the family and to all those suffering this terrible loss. Rest in peace, Demi."

Any death 'not resulting from natural causes' automatically triggers a judicial investigation, meaning homicide officers in Tenerife launched a probe. This will also take into account the medical response to the situation, with questions to be addressed about whether De Miguel was given oxygen on the pitch, whether a defibrillator was used and issues around the assistance he received during his ambulance transfer.

‌



Matches have been suspended in Spain until Friday, while Tenerife suspended all of their club activities as they entered into six days of mourning. They will pay tribute to De Miguel at their home ground, the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez Stadium on November 7 at 6pm and have encouraged supporters who wish to say farewell to the forward to attend.

The first team, coaching staff and club management will attend De Miguel's funeral, which will take place in Navahermosa.

Sports.title: Meg Jones leads way as Six Red Roses named in World Rugby Dream Team of the Year
Sports.content:
Meg Jones leads way as Six Red Roses named in World Rugby Dream Team of the Year

The Red Roses have the best representation in the World Rugby Women's 15s Dream Team of the Year which recognises the standout performers across the international season

View 3 Images Megan Jones of England breaks a tackle against Canada (Image: 2026 Tim Austen)

Six Red Roses have been named in the World Rugby Women's 15s Dream Team of the Year 2026, including captain Meg Jones.

‌



‌



The governing body also awarded France's Pauline Bourdon Sansus with the International Rugby Players' Association (IRPA) Women's 15s Try of the Year 2026, bringing the women’s awards celebrations and the 2026 international window to a close.

‌



The announcements recognise the exceptional individual performances and memorable moments that have defined another compelling year of international women's rugby, following this weekend's presentation of the World Rugby Women's 15s Player and Breakthrough Player of the Year awards to New Zealand duo Kaipo Olsen-Baker and Elinor-Plum King.

‌



England's six selections lead the way in the Dream Team, followed by New Zealand with five, Canada with three and France with one, reflecting the outstanding talent and performances on display across the international game throughout 2026.

The Red Roses are represented by forwards Hannah Botterman, Amy Cokayne and Maddie Feaunati, alongside backs Zoe Harrison, Megan Jones and Jess Breach.

New Zealand also features prominently, with Maiakawanakaulani Roos, Kaipo Olsen-Baker, Ayesha Leti-I'iga, Sylvia Brunt and Braxton Sorensen-McGee earning selection following impressive performances for the Black Ferns.

‌



Canada's DaLeaka Menin, Sophie de Goede and Olivia Apps are also recognised, while France's Léa Champon completes the line-up.

View 3 Images World Rugby's Women's 15s Dream Team of the Year 2026 includes six Red Roses players. (Image: World Rugby)

‌



1. Hannah Botterman (England) 2. Amy Cokayne (England) 3. DaLeaka Menin (Canada) 4. Sophie de Goede (Canada) 5. Maiakawanakaulani Roos (New Zealand) 6. Maddie Feaunati (England) 7. Léa Champon (France) 8. Kaipo Olsen-Baker (New Zealand) 9. Olivia Apps (Canada) 10. Zoe Harrison (England) 11. Ayesha Leti-I'iga (New Zealand) 12. Sylvia Brunt (New Zealand) 13. Megan Jones (England) 14. Jess Breach (England) 15. Braxton Sorensen-McGee (New Zealand)

France scrum-half Pauline Bourdon Sansus has been awarded the IRPA Women's 15s Try of the Year 2026 following a global fan vote.

‌



Sansus claimed the award for her outstanding try against England during the Guinness Women's Six Nations title decider on 17 May, with supporters selecting her effort as their favourite from a shortlist of four memorable tries chosen by the International Rugby Players' Association.

View 3 Images Pauline Bourdon Sansus won the International Rugby Players' Association (IRPA) Women's 15s Try of the Year 2026 (Image: World Rugby)

‌



The French international saw off competition from Olivia Apps (England, v Canada, 19 September), Abi Burton (England, v Australia, 12 September) and team-mate Léa Champon (France, v Scotland, 9 May).

The award celebrates the creativity, attacking flair and individual brilliance that have produced some of the most memorable moments of the 2026 international season.

‌



World Rugby Chair Brett Robinson said: “Congratulations to Pauline on winning Try of the Year and to all 15 players selected in the Dream Team. These awards recognise the exceptional skill, creativity, and exceptional performances we have seen throughout 2026, and are a fitting way to celebrate the players who have delivered so many memorable moments on the international stage.

“From established stars to exciting emerging talents, this year's award winners reflect the incredible depth and ambition of the women's game. As we bring the 2026 international window to a close, there is much to celebrate, and I congratulate all those recognised for their outstanding contributions to another fantastic year of women's rugby.”

Article continues below

As the curtain falls on the 2026 women's international season, the awards provide a fitting celebration of a year defined by outstanding performances, fierce competition and the continued growth of the women's game around the world. The men’s awards will be announced in the final week of November during the Nations Championship.

Sports.title: UEFA make Matheus Cunha decision after Man Utd star returned to pitch despite red card
Sports.content:
UEFA make Matheus Cunha decision after Man Utd star returned to pitch despite red card

Matheus Cunha was sent off in the dying embers of Manchester United's 3-2 win against Roma but re-entered the field of play at full-time before Michael Carrick ushered him away

View 2 Images Matheus Cunha took a risk after the win (Image: Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA/Getty Images)

Manchester United star Matheus Cunha won't receive a further punishment despite returning to the pitch after being sent off against Roma. Cunha, 27, was shown his second yellow card in stoppage time of the Champions League tie for a late tackle.

‌



‌



The Brazilian had picked up his first booking after scoring the winning goal, as he took his shirt off and dived into the elated crowd. Cunha didn't go down the tunnel after he was given his matching orders and waited on the sidelines until the final whistle.

‌



When it sounded, the forward re-entered the pitch before being ushered away by Michael Carrick, who knew that Cunha was risking adding to his one-game ban. But Cunha has avoided an extra sanction, with UEFA confirming: "The UEFA official reports did not mention anything about this incident.

‌



"Therefore the automatic one-match ban following two yellow cards should not be extended for this reason. We are not investigating further this matter."

‌



Carrick admitted that he was 'disappointed' with Cunha's sending off which put United down to 10 men in the dying embers. But the United manager was still delighted with his equalising goal and emphatic winner after a tactical change.

"Matheus can do them things, he's got them moments," Carrick explained. "We put him inside, we swapped him with Bryan [Mbeumo] at half-time to try and get him in the middle of the pitch, try and give us a little bit of different shape, and put him in the centre of the pitch, and he found himself in good positions.

‌



"Disappointed with how it finished, but again just shows how much he cares and willing to do, and when he's in that frame of mind, he's in that mood and he plays like that, that's what we want from him."

Should Matheus Cunha have received a further punishment? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Matheus Cunha will serve a one-match ban (Image: James Gill - Danehouse/Getty Images)

The win was United's first in 10 games, as they earned their sixth point from four matches in the Champions League to boost their hopes of reaching the knockout stage for the first time since 2022. Carrick isn't getting carried away, though, with his future still under the microscope.

‌



"It's one game, so it depends on what happens next," the Red Devils boss said. "We've got to capitalise on that.

"But tonight, the boys showed an awful lot. I thought we came out in the second half and, unfortunately, with Carlos [Baleba] having to go off, Youri [Tielemans] came on the pitch and I thought he was fantastic. He showed everything that he is as a personality and as a character.

Article continues below

"He's experienced, to step into a game like that. The boys just went with the flow, and you could feel how positive it was. It was nice to see this place like that again."

Sports.title: Ciara Mageean's husband carries Olympian's coffin just weeks after their wedding
Sports.content:
Ciara Mageean's husband carries Olympian's coffin just weeks after their wedding

Ciara Mageean married her long-time partner, Tommy Moran, less than three weeks before the former European champion middle-distance runner died at the age of 34

View 7 Images Ciara Mageean's coffin being carried to the graveyard (Image: Press Association)

Ciara Mageean was carried to rest with the help of her husband, Tommy Moran, at a funeral that took place on Tuesday barely a week after celebrating their marriage. Gathered mourners were told of the two-time Olympian's fierce determination to give wedding guests an unforgettable day as she married the love of her life less than three weeks before her death.

‌



‌



Mageean, 34, died on Sunday aged 34. The middle-distance runner was diagnosed with stage 4 bowel cancer last summer.

‌



That announcement came 12 months after winning European 1500 metres gold. Mageean had previously won a silver and two bronzes.

‌



Former Olympic athlete tragically dies aged 34 just weeks after wedding as tributes pour in READ MORE :

Former Olympic athlete's heartbreaking promise to her partner before tragic death aged 34 READ MORE :

She represented Ireland at the 2016 and 2020 Summer Olympic Games before etching her name into the history books in 2024 by becoming only the second athlete after Sonia O'Sullivan to secure an individual European title for Ireland.

Mageean wed her long-time partner, Tommy Moran, last month. The couple held a ceremony at Belfast City Hall before hosting a larger celebration at Darver Castle in Co Louth, just a week before her death.

On Tuesday, hundreds of mourners walked in the funeral cortege as the beloved runner's coffin was carried into the grounds of St Patrick's Church in her home town of Portaferry.

‌



View 7 Images Thomas "Tommy" Moran (front left of coffin) carries the coffin of his wife athlete Ciara Mageean (Image: Press Association)

Rows of young players from Portaferry Gaelic Athletic Club, where Mageean played camogie as a youngster, lined up alongside her husband and family members as her remains were brought into the churchyard. The players formed a guard of honour as the coffin was carried inside the church ahead of the requiem mass.

‌



The homily was delivered by Fr Martin Kelly, who served as parish priest at St Patrick's from 2000 to 2009 and had known Mageean since she was eight years old. He discussed the Olympian's recent wedding and how she was intent on providing her attendees with a "lavish, memorable occasion".

View 7 Images Ciara Mageean celebrates getting married to Tommy Moran (Image: John Gillooley)

‌



Speaking to Mr Moran, he said: "You were the love of her life".

Recounting the pair's festivities, the priest continued: "There were two events for her wedding, and she looked radiant at both of them, at the centre of each event, and I saw her dancing and singing, so full of joy and so happy to be able to celebrate her big day with Tommy. She was determined to give everybody a day to remember.

‌



"After the second celebration, she retired to her hospice bed, and that was it; she sank lower and lower, but she held out until last Sunday, just passed, the Feast of All Saints. What an appropriate day. She was surrounded by her family as she passed on peacefully."

Make sure you don't miss sport's biggest stories and breaking news by making the Daily Mirror one of your Google preferred sources.

‌



Fr Kelly revealed two moments in Mageean's athletics career that stood out in his memory. "The first was when she returned home to Portaferry after winning a world silver medal at the World Under-18s Meeting in Canada," he said.

"When she arrived on the ferry from Strangford, there was a wide circle of Portaferry people to welcome her. She stepped off the ferry onto the slipway like a young sea goddess from the lough, wrapped in the tricolour, with a smile to warm all hearts.

‌



"She gave me the warmest hug you could imagine. I have always treasured that moment. And we were all so proud of her.

View 7 Images Ciara Mageean won European bronze in 2016 (Image: Martin Rickett/Press Association)

‌



"My second standout moment was when, in Rome, at the final of the European Championships in 2024. On the home straight, she was third behind two runners who had boxed her in.

"She said to herself, 'You're not going to box in a Portaferry camogie player that easily'. So she waited, and she waited until an opening came, and she cut through like a knife through butter, hitting the line with her arms in the air, getting gold and becoming European champion."

‌



He added: "She stood on the podium wrapped in a tricolour, listening to the Irish national anthem. We all had tears in our eyes, our hearts bursting with joy and pride."

View 7 Images Ciara Mageean holding an Irish tricolour (Image: ©INPHO/Morgan Treacy)

‌



Fr Kelly recalled paying a visit to Mageean in her hospice room in the weeks preceding her passing, revealing they spoke about the "final big challenge" of death as he administered the sacrament of the sick. The priest recounted how Mageean then proposed they head out for a stroll.

"I couldn't believe it. I wasn't expecting that," said Fr Kelly.

‌



"I said 'sure', thinking that it would be easy, because of her condition, I would be able, even at my age of 85, to match her stride for stride, but for Ciara a walk was much more than a dander.

View 7 Images Ciara Mageean won European gold two years ago in Rome

‌



We did a round of a few streets up round the hospice, and when we got to the top, she said, 'Let's do another round.' I nearly collapsed. Then she said, 'Let's go back to the room'.

"On the way down, she knew I was struggling, and she said, 'Let me link you'. Now there is still a bit of the macho man in me, so I hesitated. Linking arms wasn't me. Then I gave in.

‌



"One of my happiest moments and memories is that of Ciara Mageean linking my arm as we walked back to her room, just a few weeks before she went to heaven. Thank you, Ciara, from the bottom of my heart. May you pray for us all and continue to link all of us now on our journeys through life on our way to heaven, where we will all meet again."

View 7 Images Ciara Mageean won gold barely a year before her cancer diagnosis (Image: Getty)

‌



As the homily drew to a close, Fr Kelly referenced a tribute posted on Facebook by someone who did not know Mageean personally but described her as "a truly remarkable, immensely talented and inspirational human being whose courage, humility, infectious smile and indomitable spirit touched hearts far beyond the world of athletics". The priest then quoted the conclusion of the online tribute: "The brightest lights never truly fade. Their warmth lives on in the hearts of those they touched."

Among those in attendance were Stormont First Minister Michelle O'Neill, SDLP leader Claire Hanna, Gaelic Athletic Association (GAA) president Jarlath Burns and Irish Olympic gold medal-winning gymnast Rhys McClenaghan. Aides of President Catherine Connolly and Taoiseach Micheál Martin also attended the funeral.

Article continues below

Following the funeral, players from Portaferry GAC once more formed a guard of honour as Mageean's remains were carried out of the church and onward for burial in an adjoining cemetery. Mageean is survived by her parents, Christopher and Catherine, sisters Máire and Nuala, and brother Brendan.

Sports.title: INEOS sack manager as Man Utd co-owners make brutal decision after 'lengthy talks'
Sports.content:
INEOS sack manager as Man Utd co-owners make brutal decision after 'lengthy talks'

INEOS' decision to sack the manager came after Sir Jim Ratcliffe put Swiss club FC Lausanne-Sport up for sale

View 2 Images Sir Jim Ratcliffe's INEOS have sacked FC Lausanne-Sport's manager

FC Lausanne-Sport have parted company with manager Luka Elsner after five months in charge as Sir Jim Ratcliffe’s INEOS plans to sell the Swiss club. Lausanne, who are part-owned by INEOS, confirmed on Tuesday that they had reached a mutual agreement with the 44-year-old.

‌



‌



A statement read: "After lengthy discussions about the current sporting situation, FC Lausanne-Sport and Luka Elsner have mutually agreed to end their collaboration."

‌



Elsner was appointed on 1 June but leaves with Lausanne bottom of the Swiss Super League. His departure comes as INEOS have put the club up for sale.

‌



The reported decision to sell Lausanne-Sport comes after INEOS abruptly ended its sponsorship agreements with New Zealand’s All Blacks rugby team and Tottenham Hotspur last year.

Meanwhile, Manchester United manager Michael Carrick has also been under pressure at Old Trafford following a disappointing run of results. United eased some of the pressure on Carrick by coming from two goals down to beat Roma 3–2 in the Champions League on Tuesday, ending a nine-game winless run.

Much of the supporters' frustration has been directed at Ratcliffe and the Glazer family. In the 21st minute, fans threw green and gold balloons onto the pitch and chanted against the owners.

‌



Roma had gone 2-0 up inside 17 minutes, but United hit back in the second half. Bruno Fernandes scored from the penalty spot before Matheus Cunha struck twice to complete the comeback.

Cunha was booked for taking off his shirt as he celebrated the winner in front of the home fans. A later challenge on a Roma player earned him a second yellow card.

‌



View 2 Images Manchester United came from behind to beat Roma but Michael Carrick remains under serious pressure

Speaking after the game, Carrick said: "Disappointed with how it finished, but again just shows how much he cares and willing to do, and when he's in that frame of mind, he's in that mood and he plays like that, that's what we want from him."

On the game, the Reds Devils manager added: "It was a challenging game. I think we started OK in the game, we knew it was going to be tough — they’ve only had one defeat all season. They’re a very, very good team.

‌



"So we talked about what we wanted to do in the game, we started OK and then the goal came from nowhere. We caused ourselves a few issues. In some ways, understandable with the run we’ve been on, a little bit anxious and a few nerves at times.

"This place [Old Trafford] does it. No matter what situation you’re in, how tough it can seem, the supporters are desperate to get behind you and we gave them something to go on. We gave them other opportunities to score and it was close, and you’re thinking, 'That’s another chance gone by,' but we kept looking, kept pushing for answers and we found them in the end."

Sports.title: Man Utd prepare for Real Madrid conflict as JJ Gabriel nears Old Trafford exit
Sports.content:
Man Utd prepare for Real Madrid conflict as JJ Gabriel nears Old Trafford exit

Manchester United are ready to fight for proper compensation if teenage star JJ Gabriel completes a move to Real Madrid after going AWOL from the club

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel is close to joining Real Madrid (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United are ready to launch legal action against Real Madrid in order to get proper compensation for JJ Gabriel.

‌



‌



After considering a handful of European giants, Gabriel, 16, has reportedly agreed to join Real. His future has been the subject of much speculation over the past few months after he decided to cut ties with United.

‌



Gabriel dropped a bombshell in September by requesting to leave the club, having grown frustrated at being made to wait for his first-team debut. The youngster is also concerned by the drop in United's status in recent years and believes his career progression would be better served elsewhere.

‌



He has been courted by Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain and has now set his sights on Real. However, it is not as simple as that, with United still holding his registration and being unwilling to lose one of the most exciting young players in Europe for a minimal fee.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



As Manchester Evening News reports, United have not been contacted by Real or Gabriel's camp over the move. Nevertheless, the club will consider legal action against Real because the compensation fee due once FIFA approve the move would be well below Gabriel's market value, at between £100,000 to £300,000.

The race for the best young talent has ramped up in the past few years, triggering a number of notable tribunal cases between rivals. For example, in February Liverpool were ordered to pay Chelsea £2.8million in compensation for Rio Ngumoha.

‌



Gabriel, who turned 16 in October, has secured a European Union passport, which will help smooth over a move abroad. But there is likely to be plenty more wrangling between his current club and potential future employer.

‌



The club are aghast at the teenager's approach to forcing through a move elsewhere, given he has been nurtured at Carrington since joining in 2022.

Reports in Spain say that Gabriel has been tempted to Real by the offer of a three-year contract worth more than £850,000 (€1m) per season. He is being represented by agent Ali Bharat, who has helped facilitate his exit, along with his family.
