"There's palpable frustration [within] the party about how this has all played out," the person said, and much of it is directed at Trump. Anger with Trump "is extremely high".

The BBC spoke to a dozen party operatives, campaign officials, White House allies and others, many of whom spoke on background to offer a candid assessment of Trump's approach to the midterms.

Trump and Republicans had a lot riding on the outcome on Tuesday night. A stronger showing by the president's party - as happened in 2022, when Democrats under then-President Joe Biden lost just nine seats in the House, and gained one in the Senate - would have given Republicans some momentum heading into 2028.

But Trump will instead face a motivated Democratic majority in Congress that is eager to investigate the administration, block his judicial nominees and stymie the rest of his agenda.

The midterms have ushered in an uncertain new phase in Trump's second term and may force Republicans to start grappling with their post-Trump future.

World.title: US midterm results a 'victory' for Canadians hopeful of tariff relief
World.content:
There are currently several layers of tariffs on Canada, notably on sectors like autos, steel, aluminium and forestry.

After trade talks between Ottawa and Washington collapsed in August, the Trump administration imposed an additional 50% tariff on $20bn (Â£15bn) worth of various Canadian goods, from dairy to cosmetics and furniture.

The US also declared a total import ban on motorcycles, whey protein and alcohol.

Canada retaliated by slapping the US with its own 50% "dollar-for-dollar" tariffs. Most provinces have also banned the sale of US alcohol in retaliation.

Trump had also previously threatened to escalate the trade war with Canada further by â raising tariffs on sectors, including auto manufacturing, as of 1 January.

There were signs that his administration had become more sensitive to the optics of its tariffs on Canada in the run up to the election.

Just a few days before the vote, Trump told reporters that a trade deal is "very close" after speaking with Prime Minister Mark Carney.

Speaking to reporters on Tuesday evening, Carney said of US negotiators that "they're asking less and they're offering more" in recent discussions.

On Wednesday, US-Canada Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc said the midterm results won't change anything in the short term, and dismissed speculation over what the new Congress might do when they're seated in the new year as "an interesting discussion at a faculty club luncheon".

"Our approach will not change and we don't intend to speculate on the approach being taken by the Americans," he said.

Trump may feel more pressure to sign a deal with Canada now that American voters have clearly communicated their frustration, said Colin Robertson, a former Canadian diplomat and a fellow at the Canadian Global Affairs Institute.

"Will this change Trump's mind? It might, because he suffered such a beating at the polls."

But he added it remains to be seen how Trump will react from the bruising midterm loss.

Canada has an ideal window between now and January - when the new Democratic lawmakers are sworn in - to finalise a deal, Robertson noted.

After that, Trump is likely to be distracted by investigations launched by Democrats into Trump's family and finances and some members of his administration, Robertson said.

US trade representative Jamieson Greer also said earlier this year that he had ambitions to have interim deals in place with Canada and Mexico around the North American free trade deal, known as the USMCA in the US and CUSMA in Canada, before the end of the year.

And while Carney struck a more optimistic tone in recent days on the current state of Canada-US trade talks, he also told Politico last month that he was prepared to wait for a new American president if necessary to reach a deal with the US.

World.title: Ukraine says bodycam video shows deadly Russian double-tap bombing
World.content:
The bodycam footage was released by Ukraine's national police on Wednesday.

It shows huge devastation after the first bomb strike on the village in Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia region, as shocked local residents stare at the rubble.

Severely damaged buildings are also seen.

A voice of a military official is then heard on a two-way radio warning police on the ground of more glide bombs being launched towards Kamyshuvakha.

"Quickly [go] to the shelter!" one of the police officers tells local residents, who are seen walking into the shelter - at least two floors underground.

Seconds later the shelter is hit, and the recording stops.

Ukraine said the shelter was near a local school, which was being used to distribute humanitarian aid.

BBC Verify has confirmed the video was filmed in the same place as footage released by the Ukrainian state emergencies service DSNS showing the aftermath Monday's attack in Komyshuvakha.

In a post on social media on Wednesday, Zelensky said that "nine aerial bombs were dropped by the Russians.

"First, they hit people who came to receive humanitarian aid, and then rescuers and police officers who arrived at the scene."

The Ukrainian president added that "unfortunately, there has been very little reaction from the world to this insane attack", describing it as yet another of "thousands" of war crimes committed by Russia.

Ukraine's DSNS earlier posted another video showing a huge crater left after the attack on Kamyshuvakha.

The Russian military has not publicly commented.

Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

Additional reporting Paul Brown, BBC Verify

World.title: French blood storage impacted by freezer hacks as theories swirl about culprits
World.content:
French authorities say that fridges used in medical facilities to store blood for donations were impacted by recent cyber-attacks by unknown hackers.

The French Blood Establishment (EFS) said cold rooms storing blood were impacted by hackers, with temperatures set to rise - but staff intervened to protect blood supplies.

"No health impact has been identified and no loss of blood products is to be reported," the EFS said.

Up until now, only supermarkets were known to have been impacted by the hacks.

Meanwhile rumours have been circulating online about Russian hacktivist groups claiming they worked together to hack one of the systems that was used in the attacks which have affected European supermarkets.

Noname057(16) and Z-Pentest Alliance posted that they successfully hacked Danfoss which led to speculation that they were the culprits behind the freezer hacks.

But analysts now question whether or not that meant they were behind the supermarket cyber-attacks.

While Russian groups are not being ruled out, experts say Iranian hacktivists or nation state hackers - or even teenagers pulling pranks - could also be the culprits.

Cyber-security researchers at multiple firms are poring over evidence gathered from so-called "honeypots" to provide clues as to who is behind the waves of freezer hacks.

Three separate cyber-security firms have deployed fake freezer software traps to monitor how hackers attempt to use them for attacks.

In cyber-security, a "honeypot" is a digital decoy - such as a fake computer network or file - deliberately set up to look like a vulnerable target to lure and trap hackers.

By monitoring these traps, security experts can safely study an attacker's methods without putting real systems at risk.

According to activity gathered after the first wave of cyber-attacks, the second wave which hit several European countries was highly targeted.

"The fact that all these fridge freezers were hit simultaneously suggests planning and coordination," says Ryan Dewhurst from Spanish cyber-security company Previdian.

The entry point to the affected freezer software products was not difficult to exploit as they were poorly protected, with known attack methods already floating around online.

But experts like Dewhurst say the hacker or hackers had to gather the information about the devices' public IP addresses to create a target list then take time to plan which methods to use and when to execute them.

"Given the reported timing of when the devices had their temperatures increased, which seems to have been overnight for maximum damage - this is further evidence that the attack was planned and co-ordinated," he said.

Another cyber firm which has deployed similar honeypot tech to lure the hackers into revealing their tactics is Strathclyde-based Lupovis.

It had honeypots which appeared to be located around the world, and started seeing activity 10 days before the second wave of cyber-attacks.

Intriguingly, the team saw hackers scanning and probing their fake freezer sites only in Europe.

"We saw none of our honeypots in places like Africa or South America targeted at all," said Lupovis founder Dr Xavier Bellekens.

"Even pots in Ukraine were left alone."

World.title: 'Most difficult days of my life' for keeper Owono
World.content:
FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono says he is experiencing "the most difficult days of my life" after the death of Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel.

Tenerife player De Miguel, 30, died after suffering a serious injury in a collision with Owono during a Spanish second division match on Monday.

The world of football has paid tribute to De Miguel, a father-of-one who joined Tenerife in summer 2025, with a minute's silence being held at all games in European competition this week.

Owono's club issued a statement on the goalkeeper's behalf on Wednesday, explaining the 25-year-old "wishes to share a few words personally".

"These are the most difficult days of my life," Owono says in the statement.

"I struggle to find the words, and it is very hard for me to come to terms with what has happened.

"I feel enormous pain over the loss of Jesus. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him.

"I know there will be many issues to address, and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect. But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesus and the pain we are all experiencing.

"Rest in peace, Jesus."

Earlier on Wednesday, FC Andorra team-mate Lautaro Spatz defended Owono and said he "would never intentionally hurt anyone" and had been "deeply affected" by De Miguel's death.

Writing on social media, centre-back Spatz said Owono was devastated.

Spatz paid tribute to De Miguel, then said of Owono: "Those of us who know him know the kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone.

"In football, unfortunate incidents can happen but no-one could imagine that one of them might end with such tragic consequences."

Players from FC Andorra held a minute's silence before a voluntary training session on Wednesday. Owono was not at the session.

World.title: Israel's president begins consultations with parties after election deadlock
World.content:
In the election on 27 October, Netanyahu's right-wing Likud party and its far-right and ultra-Orthodox Jewish allies won 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. Eisenkot's centrist Yashar party and three other Jewish opposition parties in his bloc won 48.

Two Arab-led alliances, the United Arab List and the Joint List, together won an unprecedented 19 seats following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.

That makes them potential kingmakers. However, all but one of the Jewish parties pledged before the polls not to work with them to form a government.

The role of Israel's president is largely ceremonial, but after an election they have the role of inviting a Knesset member to form a government. That person will be given 28 days to do so, with a potential 14-day extension.

The president has wide discretion to pick someone they believe has the best chance of building a coalition. They do not have to choose the leader of the party with the most seats.

On Wednesday morning, Herzog was presented with the official results by Central Elections Committee chairman Justice Noam Sohlberg at a ceremony in Jerusalem.

"In recent days, we have heard voices trying to cast doubt on the election results and to undermine their legitimacy. This is a real danger," Sohlberg said.

"One of the foundations of democracy is the ability to have a peaceful transfer of power. This stems from the understanding that the will of the electorate obligates us all."

Herzog announced that he would begin the consultation process on Wednesday evening.

"In order to prevent another round of elections and to build a stable and good government here for the people of Israel, I expect the factions and their representatives to understand that, in the current reality, not every commitment and promise can be fulfilled," he said.

The president also expressed confidence in the Shin Bet's ability to investigate the allegations of foreign interference in the election and appealed for patience.

But he warned that Arab Israelis - who make up about one fifth of the population and often refer to themselves as Palestinian citizens of Israel - "must not be smeared".

"I condemn the coarseness and racist expressions that we have heard recently. There is no place for them toward any community in Israel," he said.

World.title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force
World.content:
Delhi is once again battling worsening air pollution as the onset of winter brings a familiar deterioration in air quality to India's capital.

The city's air quality index (AQI) - which measures PM2.5, fine particulate matter that can clog lungs - has crossed 300, entering the "very poor" category and raising health concerns for millions of residents.

Breathing such polluted air over prolonged periods can cause respiratory problems and worsen existing illnesses, with children and older people particularly vulnerable.

Authorities have responded by invoking Stage II of the Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP), introducing measures to curb dust, vehicle emissions and other sources of pollution.

GRAP is a set of emergency measures that become progressively stricter as pollution levels rise. The latest restrictions include more intensive road cleaning, higher parking charges to discourage private vehicle use and increased public transport services. Delhi Metro has introduced 20 additional weekday train trips, while authorities have been directed to stagger government office timings to ease traffic congestion.

Officials said the measures were introduced after forecasts suggested air quality would remain very poor over the coming days.

Delhi and neighbouring parts of northern India grapple with hazardous air every winter, particularly around Diwali, one of India's biggest festivals, which is just days away.

The festival is celebrated with lights, lamps and fireworks, which often worsen the city's already poor air quality by releasing fine particles and harmful gases into the atmosphere.

The annual pollution crisis is driven by a combination of factors, including vehicle exhaust, industrial emissions, falling temperatures, low wind speeds and the burning of crop stubble in neighbouring states.

The sharp rise in pollution follows an unusually clean October, when Delhi recorded its lowest average AQI for the month in eight years.

Experts have attributed the sudden deterioration to falling temperatures, slow winds and an increase in crop-residue burning in the neighbouring states of Punjab and Haryana.

A recent storm had brought rain and stronger winds, helping clear the air. But as the weather settled, northwesterly winds returned, carrying smoke from burning fields towards the capital.

India's pollution watchdog classifies AQI readings between 301 and 400 as "very poor", while anything above 400 is considered "severe". On Wednesday morning, Delhi's AQI stood at 377.

The index takes into account eight major pollutants, including PM2.5 - tiny particles about 30 times smaller than the width of a human hair that can penetrate deep into the lungs.

World.title: Secret police files released in Hungary, 37 years after fall of communism
World.content:
Hungary has opened communist-era secret police files to the public, in a controversial move the government says will help Hungarian society heal itself from the traumas of 45 years of communist rule.

Critics say the move comes too late, that the files themselves are incomplete, and that the move risks sowing division and causing unnecessary anguish to family members.

The date of the opening is symbolic - on 4 November 1956 Soviet tanks rolled through Budapest and other cities, to crush Hungary's short-lived revolution.

"I ask everyone to treat this long overdue publication of documents with dignity and humanity," Prime Minister PÃ©ter Magyar told reporters at the state archives in Budapest.

"Many families will now face difficult information, often related to a deceased relative," he added. "It is impossible to process a trauma without discussion and asking questions."

Magyar defended the move, which was a central promise of his election campaign ahead of his landslide victory in April elections, as the fulfilment of a promise made by those who toppled the Communist party in 1989 in Hungary.

World.title: Tinubu’s Education Reforms: FG disburses ₦372.62bn in student loans, trains 156,446 TVET beneficiaries
World.content:
The Federal Government has disbursed ₦372.62 billion in student loans and provided free technical and vocational training to more than 156,000 beneficiaries under President Bola Tinubu’s education reforms, according to the All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council.

The council said the reforms had expanded access to education, improved teachers’ welfare and strengthened academic stability in tertiary institutions.

In a press statement issued on Wednesday and signed by Dele Alake, spokesperson for the APC Presidential Campaign Council, the council cited the 2026 report of the Nigerian Education Sector Renewal Initiative (NESRI) of the Federal Ministry of Education.

According to the report, the reforms span basic, secondary, technical and tertiary education, with interventions targeting six priority areas: technical and vocational education, science and medical sciences, out-of-school children, girl-child education, digitalisation and education quality assurance.

The council said the Federal Government allocated ₦3.52 trillion to education in the 2026 budget and secured $552 million for the HOPE-EDU programme, which targets 29 million children, more than 500,000 teachers and 65,000 public schools.

It added that the Better Education Service Delivery for All (BESDA) programme had returned more than one million out-of-school children to learning, trained 1,400 Tsangaya teachers and established 200 bilingual centres across 17 northern states.

The Adolescent Girls Initiative for Learning and Empowerment (AGILE), it said, had reached 7.19 million girls, with 3.7 million enrolled in secondary schools. More than 10,000 schools had also benefited from improved facilities.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Student loans, TVET programmes

The council said the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND) had processed 1,659,853 student loan applications and disbursed ₦372.62 billion to beneficiaries across 319 tertiary institutions.

The disbursement comprises ₦192.89 billion for tuition and ₦179.73 billion for students’ upkeep allowances.

Under the Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) programme, the government reportedly received more than 2.8 million applications, with 156,446 verified trainees benefiting from free training, monthly stipends and start-up support.

The statement said more than ₦65.7 billion had been disbursed to trainees, while ₦30.2 billion had gone to training centres.

It added that 38 technical colleges had been rehabilitated, while free technical education covered tuition, boarding, textbooks and uniforms.

Teacher development, university reforms

The council said the government had introduced a revised national curriculum, reintroducing Nigerian History and strengthening Civic and Heritage Studies.

It also said the National Learning Assessment had been restored to monitor pupils’ performance and identify learning gaps.

Under the EduRevamp initiative, 53,553 teachers had registered, while 51,794 had joined the first cohort of the Accelerated Teacher Professionalisation Pathway, a six-month programme offering professional qualifications, certification and licensing.

The programme, backed by ₦2 billion, targets 250,000 teachers by 2027.

The council further claimed that the Tinubu administration had resolved the longstanding dispute between the Academic Staff Union of Universities (ASUU) and implemented an agreement providing a 40 per cent increase in academic staff remuneration and improved welfare benefits.

It said the Tertiary Institutions Staff Support Fund had disbursed ₦28 billion to 15,000 workers across 153 public institutions, offering eligible staff loans of up to ₦10 million for housing, healthcare, transportation and education.

Investment in medical, STEM education

According to the statement, the Federal Government is investing ₦110 billion to rehabilitate 18 federal medical schools across the six geopolitical zones.

Nursing enrolment reportedly increased from 81,480 in 2023 to 114,300 in 2025.

The government has also approved 20 STEM-focused tertiary institutions and plans to rehabilitate 12 engineering and technology faculties.

On research and innovation, the council said the government had provided ₦365 million annually for the National Laureate Prize.

It added that the Student Venture Capital Grant had disbursed more than ₦2.5 billion to 45 student entrepreneurs, with each beneficiary eligible for up to ₦50 million in equity-free funding.

Entrepreneurship certification is ongoing in 14 federal universities, while the Diaspora BRIDGE initiative has registered 1,141 Nigerian experts abroad and reached 16,675 students across 107 tertiary institutions.

Minister highlights impact

The Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, said the success of the reforms would be measured by their impact on students, teachers and institutions rather than the amount of money allocated or the number of programmes introduced.

“Our measure of success is not merely the amount of money allocated to education or the number of programmes introduced. It is the difference these interventions make in the lives of our children, students, teachers and institutions,” Mr Alausa was quoted as saying.

World.title: PSC dismisses three senior police officers, demotes 16 others
World.content:
The Police Service Commission (PSC) has approved the dismissal of three senior police officers and the demotion of 16 others over misconduct.

The commission’s spokesperson, Torty Kalu, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday, adding that the PSC also approved “severe reprimands” for 21 officers and “ordinary reprimands” for two others.

Three officers were exonerated, while some previously suspended officers were reinstated into the Nigeria Police Force, Mr Kalu stated.

He said the decisions were reached at the commission’s plenary meeting held at its headquarters in Abuja on Tuesday. The meeting was presided over by the commission’s chairman, Hashimu Argungu, a retired deputy inspector-general of police.

The commission did not disclose the identities of the dismissed and demoted officers or provide details of the specific misconduct established against them.

However, the commission’s spokesperson stated that Mr Argungu reaffirmed the PSC’s zero-tolerance stance on corruption, human rights abuses, interference in land and civil matters, and other forms of misconduct within the police.

Mr Argungu also “assured” the public that the commission would continue to ensure the speedy resolution of disciplinary cases before it.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

He commended members of the commission’s Standing Committee on Discipline and Legal Matters and other officials for their work in reviewing disciplinary cases and appeals.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that the PSC is the legal body saddled with the promotion and discipline of senior police officers across Nigeria.

World.title: Abuja Rent: Reps advance bill to protect tenants from exploitation
World.content:
The House of Representatives has advanced a proposed law to regulate tenancy arrangements in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), with lawmakers divided over how far the government should interfere in rental transactions between landlords and tenants.

The Federal Capital Territory Advance Rent Regulation and Tenants’ Protection Bill, 2026 (HB.2839), jointly sponsored by Paul Nnamchi (APC, Enugu) and Ahmed Doro (PDP, Katsina), passed second reading during Wednesday’s plenary.

The proposal seeks to address exploitative rental practices, particularly compulsory demands for multiple years’ rent in advance, excessive charges and unlawful eviction of tenants.

The bill had passed first reading on Thursday, 22 October, when it was formally introduced in the House.

Leading the debate, Mr Nnamchi said the increasing cost of accommodation and the requirement for tenants to pay large sums upfront had placed considerable financial pressure on residents, affecting household savings, businesses and employment opportunities.

He said the proposed legislation would establish a more transparent and accountable rental system through restrictions on advance rent, regulation of letting practices and the creation of a framework for protecting the interests of both landlords and tenants.

Mr Nnamchi maintained that the legislation was not designed to undermine property ownership or discourage investment in the real estate sector.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Rather, he said it sought to ensure that the commercial interests of landlords and estate agents did not come at the expense of tenants who were vulnerable to exploitative practices.

He said: “Mr Speaker, this legislation is not intended to undermine property rights or discourage investment. Rather, it recognises that legitimate commercial interests must coexist with public protection. Landlords deserve reasonable returns.

“Agents deserve professional recognition. And tenants deserve fairness and protection from exploitation.”

The lawmaker added that a regulated rental market would promote transparency, certainty and accountability while improving confidence in the housing sector.

He urged lawmakers to support the bill so it could proceed to committee consideration, where its provisions would receive further scrutiny, and stakeholders would have an opportunity to make contributions.

Lawmakers divided over proposed restrictions

Although several lawmakers supported the proposal, the debate exposed differences over whether the government should prohibit certain rental practices or simply regulate them.

Idris Zacharias (PDP, Kogi) described the bill as important but urged the House to consider wider land and housing issues in the FCT.

He also called for the House Committee on FCT and Area Councils to participate in the committee that would consider the proposal.

Chinedu Ogah (APC, Ebonyi) supported the bill, citing the financial difficulties businesses encounter when trying to secure office accommodation in Abuja.

He said, “Renting a three-bedroom office in Wuse could cost between ₦25 million and ₦30 million annually, excluding agency charges.”

Mr Ogah argued that clearer regulations would help address excessive charges and create a more predictable environment for investors.

Leko Gambo (APC, Bauchi) also supported the proposal but questioned the use of the word “prohibit” in its title.

He suggested replacing it with “regulate,” arguing that the legislation should focus on controlling rental practices rather than imposing an outright prohibition.

Mr Gambo also proposed extending the bill’s application beyond the FCT to other parts of the country. However, Deputy Speaker Benjamin Kalu, who presided over the plenary, clarified that the proposal, as presented, was specifically designed for the territory.

Ibe Osonwa (LP, Abia) expressed reservations about restricting multiple-year rent payments.

He argued that landlords should retain some flexibility in determining the terms of their transactions, describing the rental market as a free-market arrangement.

“This is a free market situation. By the free market economy, are we now going to, for every good or service that is sold outside, start to tell people how to trade in their own businesses?” he asked.

Mr Osonwa said landlords and tenants could mutually agree to multi-year payments in certain circumstances, urging lawmakers to avoid a blanket restriction that could interfere with legitimate commercial arrangements.

Joseph Bagudu (APC, Kaduna) also advocated regulation rather than prohibition, arguing that landlords needed to recover their investments, particularly amid increasing building material costs.

He further disputed claims that agency fees could reach 25 per cent of rent, saying the charges were generally around 10 per cent.

Ayodeji Alao-Akala (APC, Oyo) supported the bill, saying it would address compulsory demands for multiple years’ rent rather than prevent landlords from increasing rental charges.

He said requiring young couples and other prospective tenants to pay two years’ rent upfront placed an unreasonable financial burden on them.

The lawmaker argued that the proposed legislation could accommodate different payment arrangements, including monthly, six-monthly and annual payments, without allowing landlords to compel tenants to pay several years’ rent at once.

Patrick Umoh (APC, Akwa Ibom), however, raised concerns about possible constitutional implications, particularly regarding property rights and freedom of trade.

He urged lawmakers to step down the bill for further consultation and a review of existing tenancy laws in the FCT.

Wale Raji (APC, Lagos) said previous attempts to address rental difficulties had not sufficiently tackled the underlying problems.

He argued that the imbalance between housing demand and supply remained a major driver of increasing rents and called for greater investment in social housing and increased housing supply.

Sunday Umeh (APC, Enugu) disagreed with suggestions that the proposal violated the Constitution, urging the House to allow it to proceed to the next legislative stage, where lawmakers could scrutinise and amend its provisions.

He argued that the National Assembly’s responsibility was to make laws that promote the welfare and good governance of Nigerians.

“The bill is not anti-investment. The bill is not against landlords or those investing in the real estate environment or industry. This bill is of good use to both the landlords and the tenants,” he said.

Mr Umeh added that the legislative process provided further opportunities to address concerns and make necessary corrections before the bill received final passage.

The Minority Leader, Frederick Agbedi (PDP, Bayelsa), also urged members to support the proposal, saying high rental costs were forcing some Abuja residents into overcrowded and unsuitable accommodation in the suburbs.

He said the bill sought to address excesses in the rental market without discouraging investment in property development.

House Leader Julius Ihonvbere (PDP, Edo) also backed the proposal, citing the difficulties residents encounter when searching for accommodation and the activities of unregistered estate agents.

He said the proposed legislation would proceed to a public hearing, where Nigerians, housing professionals and other interested groups could contribute to its consideration.

“We are in a stage where we have a duty to protect Nigerians. It’s not against you to build your house. You can build as many houses as you want,” he said.

Deputy Speaker defends regulation of housing sector

In his closing remarks, Mr Kalu cited Section 16 of the 1999 Constitution, which outlines the economic objectives of the Nigerian state, including promoting citizens’ welfare and providing suitable and adequate shelter.

He argued that Nigeria operated a mixed economy in which government regulation remained necessary in certain sectors, particularly those connected to essential human needs.

“Not all sectors of the economy should be free and capitalist, especially when it has to do with shelter, which is fundamental. So, some sectors should be regulated as well as controlled,” he said.

The deputy speaker’s position reflected supporters’ argument that housing should not be treated solely as a commercial transaction without safeguards for people seeking accommodation.

The House subsequently passed the bill for second reading.

What the proposed law seeks to achieve

PREMIUM TIMES reported that the 17-page bill proposes a comprehensive regulatory framework covering advance rent payments, tenancy agreements, estate agents, complaints, refunds, eviction practices and dispute resolution.

Under Section 4, landlords, estate agents, and property managers would be prohibited from demanding, receiving, or compelling tenants to pay more than 12 months’ rent in advance as a condition for granting, renewing, or continuing a tenancy.

The restriction would apply to residential and commercial properties across the FCT.

However, the proposal does not completely prohibit tenants from paying more than one year’s rent. It allows voluntary payments exceeding 12 months when the tenant initiates the arrangement without coercion, discrimination, threats, or retaliation, provided the agreement is documented in writing.

World.title: Soldiers kill suspected kidnappers, recover AK-47 rifles in Kogi
World.content:
The Nigerian Army and the Kogi State Vigilance Service have killed three suspected kidnappers and recovered four AK-47 rifles during a joint operation in Kogi State.

The operation was conducted on Wednesday in Igalamela/Odolu Local Government Area as part of a sustained search for suspected kidnappers operating around Edimogbo and Obele forests.

In a statement on Wednesday, the Acting Assistant Director of Army Public Relations for 12 Composite Brigade, Hassan Abdullahi, said the joint security team extended its search from Edimogbo Forest towards Obele Forest in pursuit of fleeing suspects.

He said the suspected kidnappers attempted to escape after sighting the security team, leading to an encounter in which three of them were killed.

The subsequent search led to the recovery of four AK-47 rifles, 12 magazines, 336 rounds of 7.62mm special ammunition, three bandoliers and an identity card, Mr Abdullahi said.

The Commander of the 12 Composite Brigade, Kasim Sidi, a brigadier general, commended the soldiers and personnel of the vigilance service for their role in the operation.

He urged them to sustain the operations and prevent criminal groups from using the area as a haven.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that soldiers killed two suspected kidnappers and recovered two AK-47 rifles during a follow-up operation in Edimogbo Forest on 3 November.

The army had said the operation followed an earlier raid on a suspected kidnappers’ hideout in the forest on 2 November, during which soldiers recovered 1,000 rounds of ammunition, six motorcycles and other items.

In another report, PREMIUM TIMES reported that troops of the 21 Battalion Quick Reaction Force destroyed the suspected kidnappers’ camp after the occupants fled as soldiers approached.

The latest operation brings the number of suspected kidnappers the army has reported killing in the area over the three days to five.

The army urged residents to provide credible information to security agencies to support ongoing operations.

World.title: US Midterms: Why we lost woefully – JD Vance
World.content:
US Vice President JD Vance said on Wednesday that the reason his Republican Party performed woefully in Tuesday’s midterm elections was because of the Iran war.

Mr Vance, in a post on X, said, “The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night.”

The US and Israel’s war with Iran has led to higher petrol and diesel prices as well as a high cost of living in the US and across the world.

PREMIUM TIMES reports that the Democratic Party won in most of the elections held on Tuesday and took control of both chambers of Congress.

Details later…

Read the full post by Mr Vance below.

One of the things the data analysts on our side obsessed over was “composition” whether the electorate looked close enough to 2024 for Republicans to win. And despite polls that showed a Democrat blowout, the data kept on telling us the same story: in some states turnout was merely OK, in other states it was downright amazing, and in no state was it catastrophic. There was a genuine sense of optimism on our team: our people were showing up.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

So, I asked the smartest data guy I know, does that mean we’re going to shock the world? “No,” he told me. “We might do better than the polls suggest. But the data is telling us that a lot of Trump/Vance 2024 voters are pissed and planning to vote for the other guys. Our voters are turning out, but they may not vote for us.”

Well, that looks prophetic now. Our voters did show up. In Florida, for example, the electorate was 9 points more Republican than Democrat, just a couple points worse than 2024. Undoubtedly there were places we could have done better on turnout. But the main problem is not turnout. The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026.

There will be a lot of infighting and arguing over what happened and why that is. One of the pollsters I really respect told me that our economic messaging wasn’t sharp enough down the stretch. I’m sure that’s true.

But the real reason we lost is obvious to almost everyone.

Another pollster—one of the smartest people I know in politics, told me yesterday we’d lose the generic ballot by 13 points. I felt negative going into Tuesday, but even I was shocked by this. In his polling, he saw that a lot of Trump 2024 voters were angry and planning to vote for Democrats. He asked those voters who had abandoned us what would cause them to come back on our team. The top four answers, accounting for nearly all of the responses were:

1) End the war

2) Focus on cost of living/inflation

3) Put America First

4) Change our relationship to Israel

Our voters showed up. And the above four reasons are why many of them voted for Democrats. This is according to a pollster who nailed the results. While many spent Monday attacking Rachel Campos Duffy for calling for a diplomatic resolution to the conflict, it turns out her political advice was sound. (She’s also a great person.)

In the next few months, there’s going to be a lot of gaslighting. Expect to hear any number of establishment politicians say the solution to our woes is amnesty. I’m open to the idea that we should change enforcement—by focusing more on businesses that hire illegal labor, for instance. But anyone pushing amnesty is lying to you.

The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night.

If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that’s at least honest.

But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.

I remain hopeful about our country. To the people who are pissed off and want to say, “I told you so”: you’re right, you did tell us so. Take that energy into electing Republicans who share your worldview. To the people who are just pissed at the results, you should be. Let’s take that anger and get back to the work of saving our country.

World.title: 2027: Obuebite defends defection to APC, addresses past criticisms
World.content:
Jonathan Obuebite, the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate for Brass/Nembe Federal Constituency in the 2027 general elections, has defended his political realignment, saying his previous criticisms of the party were made while he was speaking on behalf of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP).

Mr Obuebite, a former member of the Bayelsa State House of Assembly and former PDP spokesperson in the state, spoke on Arise Television’s The Morning Show on Wednesday.

During the interview, presenter Rufai Oseni confronted him with his earlier comments describing the APC as a party associated with propaganda, violence, and electoral malpractice, asking whether the party he once criticised is now acceptable to him.

Responding, Mr Obuebite acknowledged making some of the statements but said he made them in his capacity as a party spokesperson.

“As a politician, I have served as spokesman for my party, and I was a very strong member of the PDP. I must tell you this: the former president, Goodluck Jonathan, is my father,” he said.

He added that his political position changed because of developments in the country and the situation within the PDP.

Mr Obuebite, however, rejected the suggestion that his previous criticisms were necessarily factual, insisting that most of the allegations raised by the interviewer did not happen.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“Most of those things you are saying never happened. But as a party person, I spoke and marketed my party. I know I’m a good product, and I marketed that product, and you can see the result,” he said

Past criticisms

Mr Obuebite’s comments contrast with some of his public statements during the 2015 Bayelsa governorship election, when he served as Director of Publicity of the PDP Restoration Campaign Organisation.

In November 2015, he accused the APC of plotting to rig the Bayelsa governorship election through alleged attempts to compromise officials of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) and security agencies.

He also alleged that the party was working with two northern governors and individuals in the Presidency to influence the election. The APC dismissed the allegations as false and unfounded.

In December 2015, Mr Obuebite again criticised the APC over claims surrounding Former Bayelsa State Governor Henry Dickson’s visit to the Presidential Villa in Abuja.

Describing the claims as “propaganda and recurring lies”, he said the APC had been rejected by the people of Bayelsa.

“The APC has lost, and they know it. No amount of propaganda and blackmail will return them as winners. They have been roundly rejected by the people, and we truly sympathise with them because the APC is finished in Bayelsa State,” Mr Obuebite declared.

Those statements formed part of the political exchanges between the PDP and APC during the 2015 governorship election in Bayelsa.

Support for APC

Speaking further on Arise, Mr Obuebite also defended the decision by Bayelsa Governor Douye Diri and his political allies to align with the APC, citing what he described as federal support for major development projects in the state.

He said the Nembe-Brass road project has long been a demand of the people in the two local government areas.

According to him, the first phase of the road, covering 21 kilometres, is progressing, while the second phase has been awarded under President Bola Tinubu’s administration.

He said previous efforts to secure federal government collaboration on the project during the administration of former President Muhammadu Buhari were unsuccessful.

Mr Obuebite also cited the state’s independent power project, saying the Tinubu administration granted waivers for the importation of turbines and other equipment for the facility.

He said the project was important to the state’s industrialisation and economic development.

Mr Obuebite further praised President Tinubu for his commitment to a free and fair electoral process during Governor Diri’s re-election.

He said the president allowed INEC to perform its duties without interference.

Political background

Mr Obuebite served two terms in the Bayelsa State House of Assembly, representing Nembe Constituency I, and held the position of Chief Whip.

He also served as Commissioner for Information, Strategy and Orientation under former Governor Seriake Dickson and held other political appointments in the state.

He is the APC’s candidate for Brass/Nembe Federal Constituency ahead of the 2027 general elections.

World.title: State Police: Senate sets deadline for state assemblies to transmit resolutions
World.content:
The Senate on Wednesday fixed 15 November as the deadline for state Houses of Assembly to transmit their resolutions on the proposed creation of state police to the National Assembly.

The Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, announced the deadline during plenary after senators endorsed the decision through a voice vote.

According to the Senate, the states yet to transmit their resolutions on the proposal are Kano, Oyo, Cross River, Abia, Niger and Benue. However, records show five states have passed the proposal in their respective states, except Niger State.

The Senate Leader, Opeyemi Bamidele, read out the names of the 30 states that have approved the proposal so far and transmitted their resolutions to the National Assembly.

The states are Adamawa, Akwa Ibom, Anambra, Bauchi, Bayelsa, Borno, Delta, Ebonyi, Edo, Ekiti, Enugu, Gombe, Imo, Jigawa, Kaduna, Katsina, Kebbi, Kogi, Kwara, Lagos, Nasarawa, Ogun, Ondo, Osun, Plateau, Rivers, Sokoto, Taraba, Yobe and Zamfara.

Mr Bamidele urged the remaining states to transmit their resolutions before the deadline, describing the development as a positive step for Nigeria’s democracy, the government and Nigerians.

Background

On Tuesday, the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, announced that 28 state Houses of Assembly had approved the establishment of state police and transmitted their resolutions to the National Assembly.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The announcement indicated that the proposal had met the constitutional requirement of approval by at least two-thirds of the 36 state assemblies, equivalent to 24 states.

However, Mr Bamidele’s announcement on Wednesday said 30 states had transmitted their resolutions.

The National Assembly can now proceed with the remaining stages of the constitutional amendment process, including harmonising the versions passed by both chambers before transmitting the bill to the president for assent.

The proposal was transmitted to the state assemblies in September for consideration as part of the ongoing amendment of the 1999 Constitution.

It seeks to establish state police services that would operate alongside the existing federal police system.

Under the proposed framework, state governors will appoint commissioners of police, subject to confirmation by their respective Houses of Assembly. Governors would also be empowered to issue directives to state police on matters relating to insecurity.

While the federal police would continue to be headed by the Inspector-General of Police, each state police service will be headed by a commissioner appointed by the governor and confirmed by the state assembly.

The proposal, however, prohibits the conversion of existing local security outfits into state police services or the exercise of police powers by such outfits under the new framework. It also bars them from bearing firearms.

Such outfits include Amotekun in the South-west, Ebube Agu in the South-east and Hisbah in parts of northern Nigeria.

World.title: Over 2m Northern children, 25,000 teachers benefit as UK-funded programme closes
World.content:
More than two million children in Northern Nigeria have benefited from the learning programmes initiated by the UK-funded Partnership for Learning for All in Nigeria (PLANE) since its launch in 2019.

The programme has also supported the training of over 25,000 teachers and facilitators across northern Nigeria within the same period.

The programme’s achievements were highlighted on Wednesday at its close-out event in Kaduna, where education stakeholders called on state governments to sustain the gains and ensure more children have access to quality education after the programme ends.

Implemented by DAI, UNICEF, Save the Children and consortium partners, PLANE supported education reforms, foundational literacy and numeracy, child protection and learning opportunities for vulnerable children, including those affected by emergencies.

Speaking at the event, the British High Commissioner to Nigeria, Pete Vowles, said the programme had demonstrated the value of collaboration among governments, teachers, communities and development partners.

“While we are celebrating the achievements of the programme today, the most important question is what happens next,” he said.

Mr Vowles said the UK was encouraged that Nigerian institutions were adopting and expanding the approaches under PLANE to sustain improvements in learning beyond its lifespan.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“PLANE is closing. The UK’s education partnership with Nigeria is not,” he added.

State governments must sustain the programmes – Gov Uba

In his keynote address, Kaduna State Governor Uba Sani said state governments must take responsibility for sustaining the programme’s achievements.

“PLANE has done its part. It is now up to us, the state governments, to keep the progress going and to make sure that every child in our respective states has the opportunity to go to school and learn,” he said.

The governor, represented by his deputy, said Kaduna had increased basic school enrolment from 2.17 million in 2022 to more than 2.57 million in 2025.

He added that recent household mapping across the state’s 23 local government areas put the number of out-of-school children at 187,719, compared with an estimated 535,000 when he assumed office.

Mr Sani said education received 25 per cent of the state’s N985.9 billion 2026 budget, describing investment in education as essential to the state’s development, security and economic prosperity.

He also called for stronger cooperation among states, saying shared challenges could be addressed more quickly through the exchange of evidence and lessons from successful interventions.

The Acting Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Education, Folake Olatunji-David, said partnerships, reliable data and innovation were crucial to improving access to education and learning outcomes.

She said education stakeholders must go beyond increasing school enrolment and focus on attendance, retention, completion, and foundational literacy and numeracy, particularly among girls, children with disabilities, displaced learners, and other vulnerable groups.

Mrs Olatunji-David urged governments to incorporate effective interventions into education policies, institutional processes and budgets to ensure that gains achieved through development programmes are sustained.

She also emphasised the importance of using reliable education data to identify learning gaps, guide resource allocation and assess the impact of interventions.

The Kaduna State Commissioner for Education, Abubakar Sani Sambo, said the programme had contributed to efforts to improve access to education and strengthen teaching and learning.

He said more than 25,000 out-of-school children had returned to learning across the state’s 23 local government areas, while calling for continued commitment to keeping children in school.

“The seeds sown under PLANE are already bearing fruit,” Mr Sambo said, urging stakeholders to build on the progress recorded.

Education commissioners from participating states, including Kano, Jigawa, Borno and Yobe, also commended the programme and stressed the need for governments to sustain its achievements.

The Borno State Commissioner for Education, Abba Lawan Wakilbe, said the programme’s legacy would depend on what governments and other stakeholders achieved after its closure.

“The legacy of PLANE will not be measured by what it has done, but by what we achieve from it afterwards,” he said.

About the PLANE Programme

The programme operated through interventions focused on foundational skills, education in emergencies and community-centred initiatives, working with government institutions and communities to improve learning opportunities for children.

World.title: Yusuf urges Nigerians to be patient with Tinubu’s policies
World.content:
By Hadiza Yusuf

KANO — Kano State Governor, Abba Kabir Yusuf, has urged Nigerians to be patient with President Bola Tinubu’s economic policies, saying the difficult decisions taken by the administration are aimed at rescuing the economy and stabilising its macroeconomic environment.

The governor said the policies had helped stabilise the economy, expressing optimism that the benefits would eventually translate into improved living conditions for Nigerians.

Yusuf, who was represented by Muhammad Yusuf Jamu, spoke on Wednesday at the inauguration of campaign coordinators for the presidential, governorship, senatorial, House of Representatives and State House of Assembly elections in Tarauni Local Government Area of Kano State.

He said the President had taken difficult decisions to address the country’s economic challenges, adding that economic stability would create a conducive environment for businesses to thrive.

“The President’s economic policies have helped rescue the country’s economy and stabilise the macroeconomy. With a stable economy, businesses can go to the markets and carry out their transactions.

“We are now at a stage where the economy is growing, and the microeconomy will soon begin to flourish, so that Nigerians can also feel the benefits.

“We are in a period where tough decisions have been taken to rescue the country. We urge Nigerians to be patient with the President and his government’s policies. At the end of the day, we will all celebrate,” he said.

The governor also urged members of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Kano to sustain efforts towards reconciliation and unity within the party ahead of the 2027 general elections.

He called on party members to abide by established rules and work collectively towards the success of the APC.

“I urge you to continue on this path of reconciliation and strictly adhere to the rules of the game. We have the best candidates to present to the people of Kano,” he said.

He further urged party supporters to vote for the APC across all elective positions in the 2027 elections.

“On election day, everyone should vote for the APC from top to bottom and from bottom to top,” he added.

Also speaking, the APC candidate for Tarauni Federal Constituency, Hon. Nasir Bala Aminu Ja’oji, pledged to expand empowerment programmes and educational support for residents if elected in 2027.

Ja’oji said education would remain his priority, alongside youth and women development, healthcare and economic empowerment.

He disclosed that he had supported 2,500 beneficiaries across the 10 wards of Tarauni with N125 million in cash grants and distributed 100 motorcycles to constituents.

He also said he had paid registration fees for students sitting the West African Senior School Certificate Examination (WASSCE), Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) and National Examinations Council (NECO) examinations, as well as provided financial assistance to hundreds of students in tertiary institutions.

“If elected, I will redouble my efforts in all these areas. My first, second and third priorities will be education, while healthcare, empowerment and youth and women development will also receive attention,” he said.

Similarly, the APC senatorial candidate for Kano Central, Senator Ibrahim Shekarau, urged members of the campaign council to intensify grassroots mobilisation and educate voters on how to identify the party on the ballot.

He said voters needed to familiarise themselves with the party’s logo and symbol ahead of the elections.

“We must educate voters that on election day, they will see the APC logo on the ballot paper, not the faces of President Bola Tinubu, Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf or other APC candidates. They must therefore be familiar with the party’s logo and symbol,” he said.

World.title: 5 facts to know about Keisha Lance Bottoms, America’s first black female governor
World.content:
By Morenike Taire, Woman Editor

Her historic victory in Georgia breaks a century-old political barrier for Black women in the United States.

The United States has recorded another milestone in its political history following the election of Keisha Lance Bottoms as Georgia’s governor, making her the first Black woman elected governor of a US state.

Bottoms, a former mayor of Atlanta, defeated Republican candidate Rick Jackson in the November 3, 2026 gubernatorial election. Her victory is particularly significant in a country where women and Black Americans have historically faced considerable barriers to political representation.

Here are five things to know about the woman making history.

She is the first Black woman elected governor of a US state

Bottoms has broken a significant racial and gender barrier in American politics. Although several women have previously served as governors, no Black woman had ever been elected to lead a US state before her victory in Georgia.

Her election represents a landmark moment for Black women in American public life and expands the history of women’s political representation in the country.

She will assume office in January 2027.

She is also Georgia’s first female governor

Beyond making national history as the first Black woman elected governor, Bottoms will also become the first woman to occupy Georgia’s governorship.

Her election marks a departure from the state’s political history, in which men have held the office since Georgia became a state.

Interestingly, the United States elected its first female governor more than a century ago. Nellie Tayloe Ross of Wyoming became the first woman to take the oath of office as a state governor on January 5, 1925.

Ross was elected in November 1924 following the death of her husband, Governor William B. Ross. She subsequently served until January 1927.

The distinction is important: Ross made history as the first woman governor, while Bottoms has now made history as the first Black woman elected to the governorship of a US state.

She was previously the Mayor of Atlanta

Before her historic gubernatorial victory, Bottoms served as Mayor of Atlanta, Georgia’s capital and one of the most prominent cities in the United States.

She held the position from 2018 to 2022, becoming a nationally recognised political figure during her tenure.

Her mayoral administration coincided with major national developments, including the COVID-19 pandemic and the protests following the killing of George Floyd in 2020.

Her experience in municipal leadership provided a platform for her subsequent return to national politics.

She has experience in the White House

Bottoms’ political experience extends beyond local government.

Following her tenure as Atlanta’s mayor, she joined the administration of former President Joe Biden as a senior adviser and Director of the White House Office of Public Engagement.

The position placed her at the centre of the administration’s engagement with communities, advocacy groups and other stakeholders.

Her White House experience further strengthened her national political profile before her successful gubernatorial campaign.

Her victory follows years of struggle for greater political representation

Bottoms’ achievement comes against the background of decades of efforts by women and minority communities to gain greater representation in American political leadership.

Her victory also follows the unsuccessful gubernatorial campaigns of Stacey Abrams, another prominent Black woman politician who sought to become Georgia’s first Black female governor in 2018 and 2022.

Bottoms’ victory has therefore opened a new chapter in Georgia’s political history and provides another milestone in the broader struggle for women’s political representation.

A HISTORIC MILESTONE

From Nellie Tayloe Ross, who became America’s first female governor in 1925, to Keisha Lance Bottoms, who has broken the racial barrier for Black women in 2026, the history of women in American gubernatorial politics reflects a gradual expansion of political representation.

Nearly 102 years after Ross took office, Bottoms’ election demonstrates how far the country’s political landscape has evolved, while highlighting the barriers that took generations to overcome.

World.title: Oborevwori assures residents of peaceful elections
World.content:
Governor Oborevwori

Gov. Sheriff Oborevwori of Delta has assured residents of the state of peaceful, free and fair elections.

He also warned political parties against violence and urged all to respect the rule of law.

Oborevwori gave the assurance at a stakeholders’ meeting on electoral security on Wednesday in Asaba.

The News Agency of Nigeria reports that the meeting is organised by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC).

Represented by his Senior Political Adviser, Sen. Emmanuel Aguariavwodo, Oborevwori reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to providing a conducive political environment for all parties.

According to him, all political parties are free to campaign and canvass for votes without intimidation or harassment.

The governor also urged political parties to sell their programmes and ideas to the electorate through peaceful campaigns and other lawful engagements.

He however, warned that anyone who violated the law would face the consequences, irrespective of political affiliation.

Oborevwori while pledging the state government’s support for INEC and its Resident Electoral Commissioner in the state, noted that achieving credible elections required collective commitment from all.

According to him, this include from the INEC, security agencies, political parties, civil society organisations and the electorate,” he said.

He added that no single institution could deliver credible elections independently, urging all stakeholders to collaborate in preventing electoral violence.

Also speaking, the state Commissioner of Police, Mr Samuel Erale, warned political parties and their supporters against violence, declaring that security agencies were fully prepared to enforce electoral laws.

Erale said that the police would monitor political activities and maintain peace before, during and after the elections.

“We want to be peaceful. We will be on ground. We will monitor all the activities of everyone,” he said.

The CP said security agencies would provide a level playing field for all political parties to exercise their democratic rights within the provisions of the law.

He warned that anyone who resorted to violence or breached electoral regulations would face the full weight of the law.

“The moment violence is involved, you leave us with no choice than to come and do our duties,” he said.

He stressed that maintaining peace, providing a level playing field and ensuring compliance with electoral laws were key priorities of security agencies.

He added that no individual, political party or contestant would be exempted from enforcement of electoral laws.

Erale also assured stakeholders that security agencies would not compromise their responsibilities, stressing their commitment to credible and transparent elections.

He urged political stakeholders to cooperate with security agencies to ensure peaceful campaigns and a violence-free electoral process.

World.title: Afenifere, Igbo forum seek stronger Yoruba-Igbo ties, back Tinubu, Hamzat
World.content:
The Afenifere and Ndi Igbo Unity Forum have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening Yoruba-Igbo relations and promoting peaceful coexistence in Lagos State.

Chief ​‌‍‍‍‍Deji Wellington, State Chairman of Afenifere, a Yoruba socio-cultural organisation, disclosed this in a statement on Wednesday, after a meeting with leaders of the Igbo community aimed at rebuilding cordial relationships between the two ethnic groups.

Wellington said the initiative was designed to change the existing narrative and restore the cordial relationship that previously existed between the Yoruba and Igbo communities.

He said it was important for Igbo residents to regard Lagos as their home and maintain peaceful relationships with their host community.

“It is our desire that the Ndi Igbo (Igbo people) see Lagos as home, where they are expected to work peacefully with the host community.

“They should establish good relationships with the Lagos State Government and subsequently protect their businesses, investments and properties,” he said.

Wellington said stronger relationships between the Igbo community, the host community and the state government would promote mutual understanding, security and peaceful coexistence.

He said the initiative was also aimed at creating an atmosphere where residents from both ethnic groups could pursue their economic interests without fear or hostility.

Wellington said Igbo leaders had pledged their support for President Bola Tinubu’s second-term ambition and the 2027 governorship aspiration of Lagos State Deputy Governor and APC candidate Dr Obafemi Hamzat.

He said the forum also promised to collaborate in mobilising support for Tinubu and Hamzat across the state.

Wellington said the forum pledged to take the campaign to local government areas, wards and Igbo communities across the state.

“The Igbo leaders have promised to join Afenifere in its determination to rally support for the President’s second term and Dr Hamzat as Lagos State Governor in the 2027 election,” Wellington said.

He expressed optimism that the partnership would strengthen inter-ethnic relations, deepen political cooperation and promote a more peaceful and inclusive environment in the state.

World.title: ₦70,000 Transport Allowance: Labour veterans wade into crisis between NLC, TUC
World.content:
File: TUC President Festus Osifo (left) and NLC President Joe Ajaero.

By Johnbosco Agbakwuru

ABUJA — Labour veterans from the Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC) have intervened in the face-off between the President of the NLC, Comrade Joe Ajaero, and the TUC President, Comrade Festus Osifo.

The two labour leaders have recently traded words over the recent approval of ₦70,000 by the Federal Government to cushion the effect of high transportation costs occasioned by the removal of fuel subsidy.

The rift between the two leaders degenerated into personal attacks on national television, a situation that has affected unity within the labour sector.



Worried by the development, labour veterans met to bring the situation under control.

Speaking on Wednesday in Abuja at the 52nd session of the National Executive Council (NEC) of the Medical and Health Workers Union of Nigeria (MHWUN), Comrade Wabba said the labour veterans had been able to arrest any form of hostility between the two leaders.

The former NLC President told journalists that veterans from the two labour centres had met to resolve what he described as a family misunderstanding between the two centres.

He said the veterans emphasised that workers’ organisations must remain united because they share a single objective and aim.

The former President of the International Trade Union Confederation (ITUC) said all hostilities had been ordered to stop, explaining that the goal is to prevent future occurrences through formal dialogue.

He said: “It’s a family misunderstanding between the two centres, and we have made it clear that workers’ organisations are supposed to be one because the objective is one and the aim is one.

“So, that seeming misunderstanding has escalated, and we have said all hostilities should stop. We will actually try to meet with them to see what happened and how future occurrences can also be prevented.

“So, basically, I can tell you for sure that veterans from both sides—TUC and NLC—namely Peter Esele, Bobboi Kaigama, Hassan Sunmonu, Abdulwaheed Omar, and my humble self, actually met and tried to look at the issue. We said we would meet formally when all of them are available because we just communicated among ourselves, the veterans, and we communicated with them, and they mutually accepted.

“The TUC General Secretary was here; I was here; the NLC President was here. All of us embraced ourselves and said,

‘Well, it’s a family issue.’ Therefore, we have also said members of the press should not actually try to advance issues that are not there because, even in your immediate family, you can have some internal issues.

“But that internal issue is certainly meant to be resolved, and we are working towards that very effectively because that is the hallmark of trade unionism: to resolve issues, even with our employers, through dialogue and social dialogue. So, basically, it is an issue we have practised, and therefore we will try to now put it into action.”

The former NLC President said some of the protagonists in the matter had travelled, adding that once they returned, “we will be able to have that platform to address the issue.”

“But for the meantime, we said we don’t see the necessity of further talking to the press because that, in itself, does not bring any solution.”

Speaking earlier, the NLC President, Comrade Ajaero, said the agreed ₦70,000 transport intervention had become secured for workers and that, when discussions for a new minimum wage begin, the money would form part of what would be added.

World.title: NNPC posts N3.49trn profit in nine months
World.content:
By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja

ABUJA — The Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited (NNPC) recorded a cumulative Profit After Tax (PAT) of N3.494 trillion between January and September 2026, following an 18.1 per cent increase in its September profit to N509 billion.

The September profit rose from N431 billion recorded in August, according to the company’s September 2026 Monthly Operations and Financial Report.

The latest figures bring NNPC’s cumulative profit for the first nine months of 2026 to N3.494 trillion.

A breakdown of the performance showed that the company recorded profits of N385 billion in January, N136 billion in February, N276 billion in March, N481 billion in April, N462 billion in May, N535 billion in June, N279 billion in July, N431 billion in August and N509 billion in September.

The report also showed that NNPC generated N33.152 trillion in revenue during the nine-month period.

Its September revenue stood at N4.608 trillion, representing a 23.3 per cent increase from the N3.737 trillion recorded in August.

Monthly revenue figures showed that the company generated N2.571 trillion in January, N2.680 trillion in February, N2.774 trillion in March, N4.971 trillion in April, N4.335 trillion in May, N4.389 trillion in June and N3.087 trillion in July.

On its statutory obligations, NNPC disclosed that payments to the Federation Account and other statutory remittances rose to N11.14 trillion between January and September.

The amount represents an increase of 17.4 per cent, or N1.65 trillion, over the N9.49 trillion recorded between January and August.

On the operational front, average crude oil and condensate production stood at 1.70 million barrels per day in September.

Natural gas production also increased to 7,789 million standard cubic feet per day, compared with 7,680 million standard cubic feet per day recorded in August.

Total hydrocarbon production, comprising crude oil, condensate and natural gas equivalent, averaged 3.04 million barrels of oil equivalent per day during the period.

The company further reported 100 per cent availability of its upstream pipeline infrastructure in September.

On gas infrastructure projects, NNPC said the Obiafu-Obrikom-Oben (OB3) Gas Pipeline had achieved 100 per cent completion, while the Ajaokuta-Kaduna-Kano (AKK) Gas Pipeline was 95 per cent complete.

It added that the OB3 River Niger Crossing pipeline had been commissioned and operationalised.

According to the company, collaboration with relevant stakeholders was ongoing to accelerate construction and pre-commissioning activities on the AKK project, with a target of delivering early gas supply to Abuja before the end of 2026.

World.title: Police arrest suspect over attack on Obi’s convoy in Calabar
World.content:
By Ike Uchechukwu, CALABAR

The Cross River State Police Command on Wednesday arrested a 27-year-old man, Victor Edet Yellow Duke, in connection with an attack on the convoy of the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr Peter Obi, in Calabar, the state capital.

The attack left the windshields of some vehicles smashed.

The incident occurred at about 2:20 p.m. at the Watt Market Roundabout as the convoy was returning from the palace of the Obong of Calabar to Metropolitan Hotel, the venue of the party’s presidential town hall meeting.

According to the police, a group of suspected hoodlums, reportedly armed with machetes and sticks, emerged from the Calabar Road and Clerks Alley axis and attacked vehicles in the convoy.

The number of vehicles affected had not been ascertained.

Police personnel deployed in the area moved in swiftly to contain the situation. Their intervention, which included the use of tear gas, led to the arrest of the suspect, while the other attackers fled.

The suspect was later taken to the State Police Headquarters by operatives of the Violent Crime Response Unit, VCRU, for what the command described as a discreet investigation, to prevent reprisals or a further breakdown of law and order. Normalcy has since returned to the area.

In a statement by its Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Sunday Eitokpah, the command said the Commissioner of Police, CP Ajo Geoffrey Ordue, had ordered a thorough investigation to identify and arrest other participants and establish the full circumstances of the incident.

Cautioning against presuming the suspect’s guilt, the police said: “The arrest of a suspect does not amount to a determination of guilt, as the suspect remains entitled to the presumption of innocence pending the conclusion of investigation and any subsequent judicial proceedings.”

The command assured residents, political stakeholders and visitors that adequate security measures remained in place across the state.

It reiterated its commitment to “providing equal security protection to all political parties, candidates and their supporters, irrespective of political affiliation.”

It also urged the public to stay calm, avoid spreading unverified information and report suspicious activities through established police channels.

Eitokpah added: “The Cross River State Police Command remains committed to maintaining public safety, protecting democratic participation and ensuring that all lawful political activities are conducted in a peaceful and secure environment.”

World.title: Atiku vows to restore fuel subsidy, reopen borders, reduce pilgrimage costs
World.content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

SOKOTO — Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar has pledged to restore petroleum subsidy, tackle insecurity, reopen Nigeria’s land borders with neighbouring countries and reduce pilgrimage fares for Muslim and Christian faithful if elected president in 2027.

Atiku, the presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), made the pledges on Wednesday during the party’s presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto, where he outlined his proposed measures to address the country’s economic challenges, insecurity and declining standard of living.

He said his administration would prioritise the welfare of Nigerians, adding that restoring petroleum subsidy would be among the measures considered to ease the burden of rising fuel prices and reduce transportation costs and the prices of essential commodities.

The former vice-president also promised to take decisive steps to address insecurity across the country, protect lives and property and restore confidence in the nation’s security architecture.

He said Nigerians deserved to live and conduct their businesses without fear of attacks, kidnapping and other criminal activities.

On the economy, Atiku pledged to reopen Nigeria’s land borders with neighbouring countries to revive economic activities, strengthen regional trade and improve the livelihoods of communities dependent on cross-border commerce.

He said the move would create opportunities for traders, farmers and other economic operators while strengthening Nigeria’s commercial relations with neighbouring countries.

The ADC candidate also promised to reduce pilgrimage fares for Muslim and Christian faithful, arguing that the cost of religious journeys should not constitute an overwhelming burden for ordinary Nigerians.

He said his proposed administration would introduce policies to improve citizens’ welfare, expand economic opportunities and address the hardship confronting households.

Atiku urged Nigerians to support the ADC in the 2027 presidential election, saying the party would provide an alternative direction for the country.

Senator David Mark speaks

Speaking at the rally, the ADC National Chairman, Senator David Mark, said the reception he witnessed from the Sultan Abubakar III International Airport to Sokoto metropolis indicated widespread support for the party in the state.

He expressed confidence that the people of Sokoto would vote for Atiku and other ADC candidates in the 2027 elections.

Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal speaks

Also addressing the gathering, former Sokoto State Governor, Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC)-led administration, accusing it of worsening poverty, hunger and insecurity across the country.

Tambuwal said the ruling party had failed to provide the leadership required to address Nigeria’s economic and security challenges.

He argued that Nigerians were facing severe economic difficulties, widespread hunger and persistent insecurity, insisting that the situation underscored the need for a change in leadership.

The former governor urged Nigerians to embrace the ADC as a political alternative, calling on them to support Atiku in the forthcoming election.

In his remarks, the ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto State assured Atiku of massive electoral support from the state, declaring that the party would mobilise its grassroots structures to secure votes for him in 2027.

“Your Excellency, Atiku Abubakar, Sokoto is your home, and we will prove that in 2027,” he said, amid cheers from party supporters.

The governorship candidate said the party would work to translate the enthusiasm surrounding Atiku’s candidacy into votes, urging members and supporters to remain united and committed to the ADC’s electoral campaign.

He described the campaign flag-off as an important step in the party’s preparations for the 2027 general elections.

World.title: Three-Hour Journey Through Massive Crowd as Atiku Flags Off Campaign in Sokoto
World.content:
Onuminya Innocent in Sokoto

The presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress (ADC), Alhaji Atiku Abubakar, has promised to restore fuel subsidy, reopen the nation’s borders for legitimate business and end insecurity if elected president.

Atiku made the pledge while addressing a mammoth crowd of party supporters that gathered at Ilorin Road, venue of the ADC presidential campaign flag-off in Sokoto.
