He said Nigerians have never had it so bad, stressing that the APC-led government has destroyed the country with anti-people policies.

The former Vice President said he meant every word of his promises, urging the people to come out en masse to vote for the ADC and protect their votes on election day.

He described Sokoto as significant in Nigeria’s politics because of its strategic position as the seat of the Caliphate, not only in Nigeria but in West Africa as a whole.

Atiku said if it had been left to the ruling party, the rally would not have held, as everything was done to stop the flag-off, but for the resilience of party members in Sokoto.

On his part, the vice presidential candidate, Rt. Hon. Rotimi Amaechi, said the government of President Bola Tinubu has impoverished the country.

Amaechi said corruption under the present government is second to none, alleging that the government borrows money and at the same time loots it.

In his remarks, the National Chairman of the party, Senator David Mark, urged the people of Sokoto to vote for the ADC from top to bottom.

Mark said the combination of Atiku and Amaechi will solve Nigeria’s problems.

Also speaking, the leader of the party in the state, Senator Aminu Waziri Tambuwal, took a swipe at the ruling party in the state for denying them venue and hotel accommodation.

Tambuwal said the APC-led government in the state did everything to frustrate the rally, but for the resilience of party members, imploring the people of Sokoto, as enlightened people and home of scholarship, to vote out Governor Ahmed Aliyu for what he described as crude methods of politics.

The journey of seven kilometres from the airport to the venue of the rally took Atiku and his entourage three hours because of the mammoth crowd that lined the route.

World.title: 40 More Artefacts Are Expected from Sweden, Says Benin Monarch
World.content:
* As Marwa visits Oba

Felix Omoh-Asun in Benin City

Oba of Benin, Omo N’ Oba N’ Edo, Uku Akpolokpolo, Oba Ewuare II, on Wednesday disclosed that 40 more artefacts looted from the Oba’s palace during the British invasion in 1897 were expected in Benin City within the week.

The monarch, who spoke during the visit to the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of the National Drugs and Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA), Brig. Gen. Mohamed Buba Marwa (rtd), in Benin, said the artefacts were coming in from Sweden.

According to him, a delegation will be going to Lagos, to receive more artefacts. “More and more artefacts are coming, the delegation will be handed over 40 artifacts from the Swedish Museum.”

Oba Ewuare scolded those he said wanted to reloot the artefacts. He said: “We battled prospective relooters of our artefacts, we battled them.”

He noted that: “The palace relentlessly battled the re-looting of our artifacts by the people who tried to re-loot what was looted.

“They wanted to re-loot it again, and I vowed that by the will of God, by the strength of God, the power of God Almighty himself, and our ancestors to give me the wisdom to always carry on the responsibility on my shoulders, because I vowed that it can never happen while I’m on the throne. By the grace of God, we prayed and it worked.”

Responding to Marwa’s request to be a drug abuse ambassador, Oba Ewuare II, who acknowledged the importance of collective efforts in addressing societal challenges, commended the NDLEA chairman for his efforts against drug abuse and other social problems.

The traditional ruler said he had a suggestion for improving the agency’s work and would communicate it privately to Marwa.

“I have a suggestion I will make in writing that I will not want to say here in public to NDLEA, as my own thinking on how to improve the work of NDLEA,” he said.

Earlier, Marwa, who with was with Edo State NDLEA Commander, Mitchell Ofoyeju, and other officers, disclosed that the agency has introduced a new pillar in drug control – Alternative Development – targeted at communities cultivating cannabis.

According to the NDLEA boss, of the 16 million kilogrammes of illicit substances seized in the last six years, 75 per cent was cannabis, which is cultivated in Nigeria, with Edo State being one of the cultivating states.

“We have introduced alternative development as a strategic pillar in which we are appealing and persuading the growers of cannabis to desist from illicit cropping and plant cassava, yam, corn, legitimate crops,” Marwa said.

He said the growers themselves have confided in the agency that they are grateful for the initiative.

“Even though there is more money in cannabis than these illicit crops, at least they will have peace of mind when they cultivate. The other one gives them money but they are perpetually ill at ease in their homes with their families for fear of NDLEA. If a cockroach moves or rats in their house, they all jump out and start looking for a way to escape,” he said.

Marwa said Nigeria is the first country in Africa to adopt the strategy, adding that the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC) has welcomed it, and the Federal Government has adopted it as part of the Renewed Hope Agenda – to move illicit croppers from crime to legitimate businesses.

Under the programme, Marwa said the Federal Government, NDLEA and state governments will support the communities with inputs and other interventions to make their livelihoods more sustainable – fixing roads, schools, clinics and water supply.

He disclosed that the pilot project has already started in Ondo State in three communities, supported by the Federal Government, with the governor of Ondo State personally part of the launch.

“We feel that the second state that we should try this alternative development is Edo State. I’ve presented it early this morning to His Excellency the governor and he welcomed it. Anything legitimate that can control drug use and trafficking is something to be welcomed,” Marwa said.

He also recalled the Oba’s historic curse against human trafficking and other crimes in the Kingdom, noting that it had helped to reduce the menace.

He appealed to the monarch to extend the same moral authority to the fight against drug trafficking, kidnapping and other vices in society.

“From here we seek your royal blessings and support throughout this kingdom for the communities to stay away from drug trafficking and drug trading,” he said.

He therefore appealed to the Oba of Benin to continue to lend the weight of the throne to the campaign against drug abuse, to protect the youths of the kingdom and secure the future of the state.

“We seek your Royal Majesty’s blessing on this alternative development. Once again we are very grateful to have been given this audience on this special day,” he added.

Meanwhile, the Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, described drug abuse as a driver of cultism, kidnapping and other violent crimes.

He spoke on Wednesday at Government House, Benin City, when he received a delegation of the agency led by Marwa.

Okpebholo said the war on drug trafficking and substance abuse could not be won by government alone.

According to him, security agencies and members of the public must play their part.

He said drug abuse remained a major concern for his administration because of its link to crime across the state.

“Drugs are totally our enemies, and we have to fight them,” the governor said.

World.title: Navy Deploys Newly Trained Special Forces to North-East to Combat Terrorism
World.content:
Linus Aleke in Abuja

The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS), General Olufemi Oluyede, said the Nigerian Navy had deployed the newly trained special forces, code-named the Marines, to the North-East Operational Theatre to tackle terrorism.

General Oluyede made this disclosure during an interview with journalists on the sidelines of the ongoing Chief of Naval Staff’s Retreat at the Naval Headquarters, Abuja.

Stressing that no single Service could do the job alone, the CDS said, “It is a collective effort, and that is why we always emphasise the issue of jointness.”

He said, “Talking about the Marines, these are specialised regiments that were brought together this particular year. They were well-trained and supported by the Americans.

“They have already been inducted and deployed to the North-East, where they are doing very well, especially along the Baga axis.

“They are working in conjunction with other Services, particularly the Army and the Air Force, integrating their activities to counter terrorist operations in that general area. They are doing very well, and we are very proud of their performance.”

Fielding questions on the fight against insurgency and what Nigerians should expect, the CDS said, “It is important for us to assure Nigerians that things are getting better. We are doing our very best collectively to make Nigeria safer.

“What we require from Nigerians is their support and prayers. If, for any reason, they notice anything suspicious, they should report it to us because everything we do relies on intelligence.

“We need community support and the support of all Nigerians to move the country forward.”

World.title: Tinubu Departs Jeddah For Abuja After Performing Umrah in Makkah
World.content:
Deji Elumoye in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu on Wednesday departed King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, for Nigeria’s capital, Abuja, after the successful completion of his Umrah (Lesser Hajj) in the Holy city of Makkah.

The president’s plane, according to a release issued by presidential spokesperson, Bayo Onanuga, took off at the Royal Terminal of the King Abdulaziz International Airport, Jeddah at exactly 5:13.pm Saudi time.

Deputy Governor of the Makkah Region, Prince Saud bin MISHAL bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Nigerian Ambassador to Saudi Arabia, Ambassador Yakubu Gambo, and Consul-General, Ambassador Muazam Ibrahim Nayaya, accompanied the president to the airport.

Before departure, Tinubu had a brief meeting with the Deputy Governor of Makkah at the Royal Guest Palace in the Airport.

On arrival in Saudi Arabia last Thursday, the president led members of the Nigerian delegation to perform the Umrah rites, including the circumambulation of the Holy Ka’abah.

Last Sunday, Tinubu was granted the rare privilege of entering the sacred structure, where he and members of his delegation performed the two raka’at prayers.

Inside the Holy Ka’abah, the president offered special supplications to Almighty Allah for lasting peace, security, unity and prosperity in Nigeria, while seeking divine guidance, wisdom and strength to continue serving the Nigerian people.

Tinubu also prayed for Allah’s continued blessings upon Nigeria, its leaders and citizens, expressing hope that the country’s diversity would be transformed into a source of strength, national cohesion and shared prosperity.

The president’s visit to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia provided an opportunity for spiritual reflection, thanksgiving and prayers for Nigeria, as well as renewed commitment to the national task of building a peaceful, united and prosperous nation.

Tinubu expressed profound appreciation to the Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, and Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, for the special courtesies and hospitality extended to him and the Nigerian delegation, particularly the privilege of accessing the Holy Ka’abah to offer prayers.

The president left the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia with renewed faith, gratitude to Almighty Allah and an unwavering commitment to the Renewed Hope Agenda and the aspiration of building a better Nigeria for all.

In his entourage were the National Security Adviser, Mallam Nuhu Ribadu, Governors of Sokoto, Jigawa, Kaduna, Borno and Yobe States, among others.

World.title: Shettima, Yilwatda, Yari, Abbas Rally Nasarawa For Tinubu’s Victory
World.content:
Igbawase Ukumba in Lafia

Vice-President Kashim Shettima on Wednesday led a high-powered All Progressives Congress (APC) delegation to Lafia for the party’s presidential campaign rally, urging voters in Nasarawa State to deliver a straight-ticket victory for the party in the 2027 general election.

Shettima, who represented President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, was joined at Lafia Square by APC National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, and the Speaker of the House of Representatives, Hon. Tajudeen Abbas.

The rally, which forms part of early mobilization activities for the 2027 polls in the North-central, drew party leaders, members of the National Assembly, APC governors and thousands of supporters from across Nasarawa State.

Addressing the crowd, Shettima said voting for Tinubu and other APC candidates will translate into more dividends of democracy for the people of the state and the country.

He said Nasarawa has benefited immensely from reforms at the centre, which had led to massive infrastructure development not just in the state but across the North-central zone and the country at large.

He cited examples of such projects, including the Lafia bypass linking the state to Benue and the Nasarawa-Plateau-Bauchi-Gombe highway project, whose groundbreaking took place recently.

He said the Tinubu administration has placed Nasarawa at the centre of its Renewed Hope Agenda through investments in road infrastructure, education and solid minerals development, and would sustain the momentum if given another mandate.

He called for uniform voting for the party across all levels.

“APC from top to bottom, APC from bottom to top. We do not want a situation where they say vote for the president and not the governor, or vote for the governor and not the president, or the senator, or the House of Assembly. We want APC straight!” Shettima declared.

In his remarks, APC National Chairman Prof. Yilwatda, said Nasarawa remains strategic to the party’s electoral calculations in the North-central and commended party stakeholders in the state for their unity and organization.

Also speaking, Speaker Abbas said the relationship between the National Assembly and the Executive has never been better, noting that the synergy has resulted in the passage of 78 bills in three years in support of the Renewed Hope Agenda.

The rally was also attended by Senator Ahmed Wadada, whose supporters chanted his name during the event, alongside other federal and state lawmakers, members of the Progressive Governors Forum, and APC stakeholders from across the 13 local government areas of the state.

World.title: Radda: We’ve Restored Dignity, Strengthened Traditional Institutions in Katsina
World.content:
Governor Dikko Umaru Radda has reaffirmed his administration’s commitment to restoring the dignity and strengthening the authority of traditional institutions across Katsina State.

He also described traditional rulers as indispensable partners in maintaining peace and driving grassroots development.

The governor stated this during a courtesy visit to the District Head of Kankara, Justice Alhaji Adamu Bello (rtd), the Sarkin Pauwan Katsina, other traditional rulers, Islamic scholars and community leaders ahead of the Tinubu-Dikko 2027 campaign rally in Kankara.

Governor Radda explained that seeking the prayers, blessings and counsel of traditional rulers before major political engagements has remained a consistent practice throughout his administration.

“We have come to pay our respects to our traditional rulers, district heads, Islamic scholars, elders and the entire community. We have also come to seek your prayers and blessings as we proceed to the campaign rally,” he said.

He stressed that his administration recognises the strategic role of traditional institutions in promoting peace, strengthening community relations and supporting development, noting that deliberate measures have been introduced to restore their dignity and reinforce their positions.

Highlighting his administration’s achievements, Governor Radda disclosed that gratuity payments had been approved and released to 14,560 beneficiaries across the 34 local government areas and Local Education Authorities, as part of efforts to settle inherited retirement and death-benefit liabilities.

He further maintained that the state government owes no contractor whose project has been satisfactorily completed, explaining that outstanding payments are limited to contractors with incomplete projects.

The governor attributed the improved financial capacity of state governments to fulfil their obligations to the economic reforms introduced by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu.

On grassroots development, Radda highlighted the Community Development Programme (CDP), explaining that the initiative was designed to bring governance closer to the people by actively involving district heads, Islamic scholars and community leaders in development planning and implementation across the wards.

“We introduced these initiatives deliberately to strengthen grassroots participation and ensure that development reaches our communities,” he added.

Responding on behalf of the traditional rulers, the District Head of Kankara, Justice Bello, commended the Radda administration for restoring peace and stability in the area.

He particularly acknowledged government’s intervention in resolving disputes over access to clean water through dialogue and engagement with Fulani leaders.

The district head also applauded the ongoing remodelling of General Hospital, Kankara, and the approval of a secondary school for Mabai community, while appealing for the speedy implementation of the project.

He further called for improved security around schools and sustained investment in major and feeder roads to connect farming communities with markets and other economic opportunities.

Earlier, the Chairman of Kankara Local Government Area, Hon. Alhaji Kasimu Dantsoho Katoge, described the governor’s visit as an important opportunity to strengthen the partnership between government, traditional institutions and the wider community.

World.title: Nigeria to Expand Eye Care to 25m People, Accelerate Universal Health Coverage
World.content:
The Federal Government of Nigeria, alongside its partners, has announced a major commitment to strengthening eye health services and advancing progress towards Universal Health Coverage (UHC). By 2030 the initiative aims to reach more than 25 million vulnerable Nigerians through expanded access to equitable, high-quality eye care, enabling more people to fully participate in education, work and community life.

The commitment was announced on Tuesday at the Global Summit for Eye Health, hosted by the Government of Antigua and Barbuda, co-hosted by the Governments of Bangladesh, Guyana, Ireland and Nigeria, in technical collaboration with the World Health Organisation. It was convened by the International Agency for the Prevention of Blindness (IAPB).

According to a statement from the summit, Nigeria is advancing efforts to reduce avoidable vision loss by integrating Primary Eye Care (PEC) into Primary Health Care (PHC), building the capacity of frontline health workers, and expanding access to essential services for women, older people and underserved communities including those in rural and hard to reach areas, where access to eyecare services can be limited.

Under the commitment, Nigeria will fully integrate Primary Eye Care into Primary Health Care services nationwide, train 10,000 primary health care workers in eye care, distribute 5 million pairs of ready-made reading spectacles, provide 25,000 fully subsidised cataract surgeries, increase the active eye care workforce by 20%, and Increase Nigeria’s Effective Cataract Surgical Coverage (eCSC) by 30 percentage points by 2030.

Senator George Akume, Secretary to the Government of the Federation (SGF), addressing delegates during the inaugural Global Summit on Eye Health, held on Tuesday at St John’s, Antigua and Barbuda.

The commitment, jointly submitted by multiple partners including Sightsavers and Christian Blind Mission, builds on Nigeria’s existing eye health strategy and recognises that avoidable vision loss remains a significant health, social and economic challenge. In 2020, an estimated 24 million Nigerians were living with vision loss, while approximately 1.3 million people were blind.

According to the “Value of Vision: The case for investing in eye health report on Vision Atlas”, investing in eye health in Nigeria could deliver US$2.45 billion in economic benefits by 2030 from an investment of US$110 million, while improving educational outcomes, productivity, road safety and mental health. The analysis estimates that such investments could avert 13,590 cases of depression, prevent 56 traffic deaths, avoid 1,479 traffic injuries, and generate the equivalent of 70,641 additional years of learning, the summit stated.



Speaking at the summit, George Akume, Secretary to the Government of the Federation, said: “For too long eye health has been treated as a footnote in the global development conversation. We must alter that paradigm because vision care is an economic accelerator… We cannot eradicate poverty, we cannot ensure inclusive education, and we cannot foster sustainable economic growth if a billion people are left in the dark, and the Value of Vision report shows what a modest investment can do. $71 billion over five years spent on six critical priorities would unlock $199 billion in economic benefits by 2030.”

An example of this collaborative approach is the Focus on Clear Vision project, supported by Sightsavers, government and other partners in Kebbi, Jigawa and Bauchi states. The initiative is helping school-aged children access essential eye care through vision screening and the provision of spectacles to those who need them. To date, the project has screened more than 1.5 million children and teachers and distributed over 33,000 pairs of glasses.



Also speaking on the project, Abimbola Ogundirahun, Country Manager, Vision Spring, said it is supporting the Federal Ministry of Health’s Jigi Bola initiative, which aims to integrate access to reading glasses into primary healthcare. Through training, technical assistance and the supply of affordable, fit-for-purpose eyeglasses, VisionSpring is helping strengthen the capacity of frontline health workers to deliver vision services.



Peter Holland, CEO, IAPB, said: “The Global Summit for Eye Health marks a defining moment for global eye health. Never before have so many governments, organisations, and private sector leaders come together around a shared commitment to expand access to sight-saving care. The package of commitments announced this week will improve the lives of hundreds of millions of people and help them go to school, stay in work, care for their families, and participate fully in society. It demonstrates growing recognition that investing in eye health is an investment in human potential, economic growth, and sustainable development.”

World.title: Tinubu Slashes External Borrowing Request to $7.7bn, Seeks Senate Approval
World.content:
* New proposal replaces earlier $20.52bn and €1.045bn borrowing plan, says Akpabio

* Funds to finance 2026 budget deficit, support reserves, stabilise naira

Sunday Aborisade in Abuja

President Bola Tinubu has revised the Federal Government’s external borrowing plan for 2026, seeking Senate approval for a fresh $7.707 billion (N10.79 trillion) loan to finance part of the budget deficit, replacing an earlier request for $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion.

The Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, disclosed this Wednesday while reading a fresh letter from Tinubu during plenary, explaining that the new request effectively superseded the previous borrowing proposal submitted to the National Assembly.

The revised request, dated October 26, 2026, seeks legislative authorisation for the Federal Government to raise the equivalent of N10.79 trillion in external financing as part of the funding arrangements for the 2026 Appropriation Act.

The president explained that the proposed external borrowing formed part of the N29.2 trillion new borrowing provision in the 2026 budget, designed to finance the country’s estimated N31.4 trillion budget deficit.

Under the revised financing arrangement, the Federal Government plans to raise N10.79 trillion externally, while N18.4 trillion would be sourced from the domestic debt market.

Tinubu said the external financing would be mobilised through several channels, including Eurobond issuance, concessional and commercial loans from multilateral and bilateral institutions, International Monetary Fund (IMF) facilities and bridge financing arrangements.

However, he indicated that the government would place greater emphasis on Eurobond issuance because of its relatively faster processing time and capacity to generate substantial funds at comparatively lower costs.

The president said: “All the options will be pursued simultaneously, considering the costs and related benefits to the country and the time required to access the funds.

“In view of this, emphasis will be on the issuance of Eurobonds, which is typically faster to conclude. Additionally, a large amount can be raised through Eurobonds at a relatively lower cost.”

He explained that the final terms and conditions of the proposed facilities would be determined by prevailing market conditions when the loans were being priced.

According to him, the Federal Ministry of Finance and the Debt Management Office (DMO) would work together to ensure that the country secured the most favourable borrowing terms.

Tinubu said the proposed funds would finance projects and programmes captured in the 2026 Appropriation Act, particularly in critical sectors considered essential to economic growth and national development.

He identified defence and security, transportation, agriculture, power, education and healthcare as priority areas expected to benefit from the proposed external financing.

The president explained that the borrowing was necessary to sustain the implementation of the administration’s economic reform agenda and consolidate the gains recorded over the past few years.

“The new external borrowings are required to implement the items, programmes and projects in the 2026 Appropriation Act, which are designed to consolidate and strengthen the macroeconomic reforms and gains recorded by this administration in the past few years,” he said.

Beyond financing budgetary obligations, Tinubu said the proposed borrowing would also strengthen Nigeria’s external reserves and provide additional support for exchange-rate stability.

He explained that the foreign currency proceeds would be received by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) on behalf of the Federal Government, thereby increasing the country’s foreign reserves.

“It is also important to add that the process will increase the accretion to the external reserves, since the funds will be received by the Central Bank of Nigeria on behalf of the Federal Government, thereby supporting the naira exchange rate,” he stated.

The president anchored his request on Sections 21(1) and 27(1) of the Debt Management Office (Establishment, etc.) Act, 2003, which provide for legislative approval of external borrowing and empower the National Assembly to approve the terms and conditions of such facilities.

He specifically asked the Senate to approve the proposed N10.79 trillion borrowing, equivalent to $7.707 billion, based on the 2026 budget exchange rate of N1,400 to the dollar.

Tinubu also sought the Senate’s authorisation for the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, in collaboration with the DMO, to take the necessary steps to implement the borrowing arrangement.

New Request Cancels Earlier Proposal

Explaining the significance of the revised communication, Akpabio said the fresh request effectively cancelled the earlier proposal read by him from Tinubu on October 27, seeking approval for $20.52 billion and €1.045 billion in external borrowing.

He said the latest letter was more explicit about the government’s financing requirements and provided greater flexibility in sourcing funds from different international markets and institutions.

Akpabio said: “I believe this letter effectively cancels the earlier request that was sent for $20-something billion. But this is much more explicit.”

The Senate President explained that the revised arrangement recognised that the Federal Government would not necessarily obtain all the required funds from a single source, but would explore different financing opportunities to secure competitive terms.

According to him, “This also takes cognisance of the fact that the borrowing is not going to take effect from only one location. So we have to go out there and search for the best terms, what we may call a willing-seller, willing-buyer approach.”

Following the presentation of the presidential communication, Akpabio referred the request to the Senate Committee on Local and Foreign Debts for further legislative scrutiny.

He asked the committee to examine the proposed borrowing arrangements and report back to the Senate for consideration, “as soon as practicable”.

The revised borrowing request comes amid continuing concerns over Nigeria’s rising public debt obligations, the growing cost of debt servicing and the government’s dependence on borrowing to finance budgetary commitments.

With the 2026 budget providing for substantial new borrowing, the Senate’s consideration of Tinubu’s request is expected to focus not only on the proposed financing arrangements but also on the country’s capacity to manage additional external debt and ensure that borrowed funds are deployed for the purposes stated by the government.

World.title: The Gentleman: Ford Ranger Wildtrak 2.3 EcoBoost review
World.content:
At R899 000, the Ford Ranger Wildtrak 2.3 EcoBoost give the impression it is a more expensive double cab then it really is. Spend enough time around Rangers, like any South African motoring journalist, and the diesel clatter and judder become ubiquitous. Press the starter on an EcoBoost and instead you get near-silence.

The Ford Ranger Wildtrak 2.3 EcoBoost is R59 400 more than the Sport 4×2 (R839 600) we drove earlier this year. And genuinely, it’s pretty hard to tell them apart. Both run the Blue Oval’s 2.3-litre turbo-petrol four-cylinder with 222 kW and 452 Nm, through a 10-speed automatic and two-wheel-drive only. I’m reliably told the Wildtrak gets matrix LED headlamps over the Sport, and some Wildtrak badging and stitching inside and out, that’s about it …

FORD RANGER WILDTRAK 2.3 ECOBOOST

A tried-and-tested interior now from the Ford stable with the portrait-style touchscreen much copied by competitors. Image: Ray Leathern

So, where do we start? How about refinement. Like the Sport, the Wildtrak is smooth, quiet and refined beyond measure. Throttle response builds smoothly from the first squeeze, with none of a turbodiesel’s lag-and-shove. And the 10-speeder shuffles through gears decisively without you noticing it in the background. You might hear a subtle turbo flutter when overtaking, that’s about it.



Performance wise, the Ford Ranger Wildtrak 2.3 EcoBoost is quick rather than Raptor fast. Both petrol, both revvy, but the EcoBoost delivers its oomph largely without theatre. And the zero to 100 km/h sprint is an 8.0 second affair.

As ever, interior tech is the second pro. The Ranger has the kind of semi-autonomous driving aids you used to expect only in an S-Class. We’ve said for ages that the cabin is a step above what other bakkies offer you. And as mentioned, the Wildtrak adds a couple of nice plush trim pieces and interior touches.

PETROL VERSUS DIESEL DOUBLE CAB

A splash of colour on the black rims matches the eye-catching Ignite Orange paint job. Image: Ray Leathern

Then there’s the fuel you put into the Ford Ranger Wildtrak 2.3 EcoBoost itself. 2026 has delivered the worst diesel price increases this century. Diesel sat at R33 a litre most of last month (October 2026), before a fuel levy reprieve brought it down a touch in November 2026. Sadly, with the price of diesel so volatile right around, the unlikely petrol Ranger is starting to look smarter by the week.



However, a turbo petrol double cab is always going to count thirst in its debit column. Ford claims 9.3 l/100 km on a claimed/combined cycle. Unfortunately, on this test, we got 12.5 l/100 km. And truthfully, this was on a pretty leisurely week, mostly urban driving, but hardly racing around either. And there’s the missing drivetrain hardware. This is a 4×2 only, which for a bakkie wearing a Wildtrak badge, does create somewhat of an identity crisis.

We can report, however, that the Ford Ranger Wildtrak 2.3 EcoBoost is an accomplished city slicker. Bar perhaps its size when threading through tight carparks. Nevertheless, it’s for the urban or highway driver who wants some Wildtrak gloss without the diesel 4×4 baggage, and doesn’t plan to go too far off the tar.

THE VERDICT

Rear roller shutter and sports hoop included in the Wildtrak price. Image: Ray Leathern

Disagree with the concept all you want, but the Ford Ranger Wildtrak 2.3 EcoBoost shows very few compromises. It’s refined, quick, quiet (perhaps too quiet) and brilliantly equipped. It’s exactly what you’d expect from the firm that brings you South Africa’s best-selling double cab. And we’d argue the R899 000 price is pretty enticing considering the Wildtrak halo status. If your life stays largely on tar, it’s arguably the best Ranger to get. Time will tell whether South African buyers vote with their wallets on this one …

World.title: ‘Pension and veterans grant should be R 3 000’: Pensioner’s plea as grant runs dry
World.content:
Close-up of elderly hands clasped together, showing texture and detail in black and white. Image: Pexels

A Western Cape pensioner says her SASSA Older Person’s Grant runs out completely before each new payment lands, even though she owns her home and has no one else to support.

The retired grant recipient, who is over 65 and asked to remain anonymous, has received the grant for more than five years. She told The South African in its SASSA grant survey that she spends the money mainly on food and groceries. By the end of each month, nothing is left.

The Older Person’s Grant pays R2 400 a month to recipients aged 60 and older, following the April 2026 increase announced in the February Budget.



No rent, but still not enough

Asked whether the grant covers her basic needs, the pensioner said it helps but is not enough. She named the cost of living and rising food prices as her biggest financial worry.

She has not gone without food in the past month. However, her experience shows how quickly a fixed grant shrinks at the till, even for a recipient with no rent or bond to pay and no dependants at home.

For pensioners who rent, the strain is heavier still, as the same grant must stretch across housing, transport and medicine as well as food.



The payments themselves have caused her no trouble. She said receiving the grant has been straightforward, with the money deposited directly into her bank account each month.

Pensioner backs union’s R3 000 call

Where SASSA falls short, she said, is communication. She rated the agency’s communication with recipients as poor and admitted she has never applied for additional government support because she did not know what else was available.

If she could change one thing about SASSA, it would be the size of the grant. She pointed to the position taken by Cosatu.



“Cosatu states that the minimum pension and veterans’ grant should be R 3 000,” she said.

That figure would mean about R600 more each month for pensioners aged 60 and older. For a recipient whose grant is already gone by month-end, she believes that increase could make the difference between scraping by and having something left over.

Win R2 000 in the South African SASSA grant survey

If you receive a SASSA grant and want to share your story, we want to hear from you.



Take part in our survey and stand a chance to win R2 000. Your responses help us tell the stories that matter.

World.title: 100 metres from the beach, there’s property on the West Coast for R699 000
World.content:
The West Coast isn’t known for being affordable.

But tucked away, just north of Paternoster, buyers can get inexpensive property.

Beachfront property perfect for a dream retirement or holiday home

The West Coast has expanded so much that finding property minutes from the beach is rare. That’s not the case in one town where you can get a seaside property closer to R500 000 than R1 million.



In Steenbergs Cove, Saint Helena Bay, buyers can purchase a 299-square-metre property 100 metres from the beach.

Rates and taxes are estimated at R800 and levies at R400.

The asking price? R699 000. The same as the average sale price in St Helena Bay, according to data from the Western Cape Deeds Registry.



In other coastal towns across South Africa, buyers can get oceanfront properties for less than R700 000.

But along the West Coast, these prices are rare because of demand.

Property prices have nearly tripled since 2017, when the average sale price was R250 000.



So, this could be the last chance for buyers to purchase prime real estate within a 2-minute walk from the water’s edge.

The town is 19 kilometres from Paternoster, where the average sale price is R2.6 million.

In St Helena Bay, buyers can still get vacant land within a development for R350 000.



That price is possible because of how many homes are on the market.

According to data from Private Property, there are 1 637 listings in St Helena Bay.

There have also been 547 sales since the start of the year.



This particular property is within an estate. Yet there aren’t any building deadlines or penalties.

Building plans, however, will need approval to maintain the Cape’s classic coastal architecture.

Life in St Helena Bay

The price tag is reasonable when you consider the lifestyle offered in this quiet coastal town.



St Helena Bay is the perfect place to spend life after retirement.

The town is close to amenities.

Vredenburg is only 20 minutes away, where there’s a growing shopping and commercial district and a hospital.



Every West Coast attraction is within an hour’s drive, and it offers a gateway to wildflower blooms.

Buyers who love the beach will relish the crisp ocean air that is distinctive of fishing communities.

Sunsets from St Helena Bay are majestic, and so is the community; residents will love joining Shelley Point Golf Club or participating in community events.

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs transfer news: Full list of new signings this season
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs have completed the signing of Bafana Bafana international Elias Mokwana.

The 27-year-old winger becomes Amakhosi’s seventh signing of the season after spending the past two years in North Africa and the Middle East.

Following his departure from Esperance, reports emerged that Mokwana was closing in on a move to the Soweto giants. On Wednesday, Chiefs officially announced the signing of the Bafana Bafana winger.



Which Other Players Have Kaizer Chiefs Signed?

During pre-season, Kaizer Chiefs signed Thabo Moloisane as a free agent after the defender parted ways with Stellenbosch FC. Goalkeeper Renaldo Leaners was the next player to join the Glamour Boys, also on a free transfer.

Amakhosi then strengthened their squad with the signing of Adolf Mtasingwa from Tanzania before completing another major acquisition in Langelihle Phili from Stellenbosch FC.

As part of the same deal, Chiefs also secured the services of Faiz Abrahams on loan.



Khanyisa Mayo, who initially joined Amakhosi on a season-long loan last campaign, was also signed permanently.

With Mokwana’s arrival now confirmed, here is a list of Kaizer Chiefs’ seven new signings:

Thabo Moloisane

Renaldo Leaners

Adolf Mtasingwa

Khanyisa Mayo

Faiz Abrahams

Langelihle Phili

Elias Mokwana

Amakhosi will be back in action this weekend when they take on Siwelele in the Carling Knockout Cup. If Kaizer Chiefs manage to win the match, it will be their first semi-final in four attempts. The Glamour Boys have only won one trophy in 11 years.



Which of the new signings have impressed you the most?

World.title: Kaizer Chiefs’ best starting XI with Elias Mokwana
World.content:
Kaizer Chiefs will soon confirm the arrival of 27-year-old Bafana winger Elias Mokwana. Where does the ex-Sekhukhune man fit into the system?

Potential Kaizer Chiefs XI with Mokwana

Petersen; Moloisane, Miguel, Dortley; Monyane, Maboe, Ndlovu, Mokwana; Shabalala, Vilakazi; Mayo.

The stats don’t paint the best picture

Mokwana moved to Saudi Pro League side Al Hazem on loan from Espérance in August 2025. The ex-Sekhukhune man played 24 times in the 2025-26 Saudi Pro League season, scoring once and supplying three assists. That’s a poor direct output of goal contributions. In those 24 appearances, Mokwana picked up six yellow cards, an average of a booking every four games. Perhaps that’s an even more worrying stat. If the Glamour Boys want to coax the best out of Mokwana, this is an issue they’ll need to sort out. In 2023-24, Mokwana’s performances caught the eye, and he bagged four goals and four assists in 25 league outings for Babina Noko.



Kaizer Chiefs’ season is in limbo

Kaizer Chiefs are already 12 points adrift of leaders Sundowns, and their season is only nine matches old. What conclusions can we draw here? Are the players at Da Cruz’s disposal simply not good enough, or is he not getting the most out of a talented young group? The Glamour Boys lost in the MTN8 quarters to Golden Arrows so there’s a lot hinging on their upcoming Carling Knockout clash with Siwelele.

Will Mokwana find his feet in SA again and produce his 2024 form that caught South Africa’s eye? Add your thoughts by clicking the red comments banner below!

World.title: Heavy rain puts rural voters to the test in Eastern Cape
World.content:
People queue outside a polling station under cloudy skies as voting gets underway. Image: File

Heavy rain is making it difficult for some voters in the Eastern Cape to reach polling stations.

Muddy rural roads and limited transport options make it difficult for residents to reach polling stations and cast their ballots.

In parts of Alfred Nzo East, the wet conditions have forced election officials to use specialised trucks to transport ballot papers along muddy roads.



Despite the difficult conditions, the Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) says voting stations in the area remain fully operational.

How heavy rain is affecting rural voters

According to SABC News, the rain has added another obstacle to an already difficult journey for residents who live far from polling stations.

Some voters rely on public transport or have to travel long distances to reach their nearest voting station.

When heavy rain makes rural roads difficult to use, getting there can become even harder.

The situation highlights how severe weather can affect access to essential services, particularly in communities where transport options are limited.

Will the rain keep voters away?

Although the IEC has confirmed that voting stations in Alfred Nzo East remain operational, the difficult travelling conditions raise questions about how many residents will manage to reach them.



The number of voters prevented or delayed by the rain has not been established.

World.title: The affordable holiday properties bordering Kruger National Park
World.content:
The properties for sale around Kruger National Park. Image: Pexels

Kruger National Park is the highlight of the South African lowveld.

Developers and investors flock to the region to benefit from tourism.

But you can also retire there or get holiday accommodation within driving distance of the most popular gates.



These are your options.

Homes start from R300 000 close to Kruger National Park

You can buy an acre for as little as R250 000 in Hazyview or a hectare in Baberton for R300 000.

But some of the most affordable plots are in developments that demand fees and enforce strict building requirements.



For example, in one development, land sells for R250 000, but buyers must pay an additional R80 000 in fees and build a R1.8 million home.

This list shows what your options are if you want to buy affordable property where your only expenses are rates and taxes.

Hazyview

Hazyview in Mpumalanga is the main town bordering Kruger National Park. From most locations in the town, you can get to the park in less than 45 minutes.



The closest gate to Hazyview is Phabeni Gate.

If you’re coming from Gauteng, the Phabeni

Property in Hazyview starts from R240 000 for 550 square metres.



In Numbipark, a part of Hazyview that’s closer to Kruger National Park, property starts at R249 000 for 800 square metres.

A 2-bedroom, 2-bathroom house in Numbipark is listed for R899 000 on Private Property.

Then there’s a 3-bedroom, 3-bathroom home with a carport and pool, listed for R1.2 million.



Hazyview Rural

Hazyview Rural offers buyers value for money.

According to one Private Property listing, buyers can get a 3-bedroom, 2-bathroom home in Ximhungwe for R300 000.

Hazyview Rural is on the outskirts of Hazyview and adds about 15 minutes to the drive to Kruger National Park.



Sabie

In Sabie, buyers can get a half-acre level plot for R350 000. A vacant plot with a slight slope starts at R250 000.

Homes in Sabie start at R550 000.

According to one Pam Golding listing, buyers can get a 2-bedroom townhouse for R580 000.



The drive to Kruger National Park from Sabie is just under an hour without traffic.

But residents don’t need to drive to the park to indulge in nature and wildlife. Several nature reserves border Sabie.

There’s Mount Sheba, a private nature reserve with buck and several trails.



Graskop

It’s a one-hour drive from Graskop to Phabeni Gate.

But buyers who move to the area benefit from the area’s amenities.

For this reason, property in Graskop is limited.

Currently, only 26 listings are on the market.

Land starts at R430 000, while homes start at R795 000.



White River Central

White River Central possibly has the best access to Kruger National Park.

It’s under an hour’s drive to the Paul Kruger Gate and about a 40-minute drive to Phabeni Gate and Numbi Gate.

Buyers who want to move to a developed area will love White River Central.



An 87-square-metre flat is on sale for R535 000. The unit has a garage, and the complex has a pool.

Rates, taxes, and levies on these properties are below R1 600 a month, and buyers could get an income from short- or long-term lets.

World.title: Gauteng tops voter turnout as 12 million South Africans cast ballots by 5pm
World.content:
MIDRAND - The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) says it has made significant progress across the country despite isolated incidents.

According to the Commission's preliminary estimates, approximately 12 million voters have cast their votes by 5pm on Wednesday.

In its latest media briefing, IEC Chief Electoral Officer Sy Mamabolo said Gauteng recorded the highest number of voters of about 3 million.

World.title: IEC puts backup power measures in place ahead of vote counting
World.content:
MIDRAND - The Electoral Commission of South Africa (IEC) has assured that contingency measures are in place to ensure that voting and the subsequent counting process are not disrupted by electricity outages.

Briefing the media on Wednesday, just a few hours before voting stations close at 9pm, IEC Chief Electoral Officer Sy Mamabolo said generators and alternative lighting facilities have been made available to voting stations in areas that have experienced power outages.

But even so, with voting scheduled to close at 9pm, Mamabolo has urged eligible voters who have not yet cast their ballots to make their way to their registered voting stations.

World.title: Presidency condemns political murders
World.content:
MIDRAND - The Director-General in the Presidency, Phindile Baleni, has condemned political killings.

She warned that police will deal with those responsible for these violent crimes.

“It is quite sad that certain people believe that their best way to express their political opinions is by killing others. “The democracy in the country enables us to choose our leaders at different points, and there are ways to allow for democratic principal transition between the different administrations or when people step down from positions,” she said.

Baleni's remarks come amid growing concerns about political killings. Natjoints Co-Chairperson Tebello Mosikili said they recorded 20 murders involving political representatives, party members and supporters, with seven arrests having been effected.

Mosikili indicated that SAPS has prioritised these investigations.

Baleni called on South Africans to be responsible, and if one wants to express an opinion, this must be done through established mechanisms and public participation.

World.title: CheckPoint Podcast | Is South Africa's Foreign Policy Failing Its Economy? Thembisa Fakude | 4 November 2026
World.content:
The Strategy Meeting Is Not The Strategy

Organisations often mistake activity for progress. Meetings are held, partnerships announced and influential relationships cultivated. The calendar fills up, but the fundamental question remains unanswered: what has actually changed?

This problem extends beyond business. It also affects governments, public institutions and international diplomacy.

During a CheckPoint: The Podcast conversation with Nkepile Mabuse, international relations analyst Thembisa Fakude questioned South Africa's clarity about its national interests.

“We don't know what we want.”

It is a provocative assessment, but it exposes a leadership problem that exists in organisations of every size.

The Missing Link Between Ambition And Execution

Strategy should establish what an institution intends to achieve, which resources it will commit and how success will be measured.

Yet organisations frequently separate those responsibilities.

Leadership teams establish ambitious objectives. Relationship managers secure partnerships. Operational departments are then expected to produce results without always having the necessary resources, authority or shared understanding of the intended outcome.

The result is an execution gap.

Everyone can demonstrate activity, but nobody can confidently establish whether the institution has moved closer to its objectives.

Every Partnership Needs An Owner

International relationships provide a useful illustration.

A diplomatic agreement may create an opportunity for investment or trade. But unless someone is responsible for converting that opportunity into a practical outcome, its value may remain unrealised.

Businesses face the same challenge when they announce strategic alliances without defining commercial responsibilities.

A credible partnership requires more than goodwill. It needs measurable objectives, clear ownership, delivery milestones and a process for evaluating performance.

These requirements should be established before success is announced, not after disappointment becomes obvious.

Accountability Begins Before The Announcement

The strongest organisations do not measure success by the number of initiatives they launch.

They examine whether those initiatives produce the intended results.

That means asking difficult questions before committing resources. What problem are we solving? Who benefits? What must change operationally? Who is accountable if nothing happens?

Fakude's criticism of South African foreign policy provides a useful reminder that external influence cannot compensate for internal uncertainty.

The lesson for leaders is straightforward.

If an organisation cannot explain what it wants from a relationship, it is unlikely to recognise whether that relationship is delivering.

Strategy is not demonstrated by access to important people or participation in important conversations.

It is demonstrated by the decisions, capabilities and measurable outcomes that follow.

Reference

World.title: Death rumours made me stronger, says ODM leader Oburu
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi when they paid a visit to ODM leader Oburu Oginga at his Nairobi residence on November 4, 2026. [Speaker’s Press Unit]

ODM leader and Siaya Senator Oburu Oginga has said rumours about his death while he was admitted to hospital only strengthened his determination to overcome his illness.

Dr Oburu who is recovering after being discharged from hospital, assured his supporters that he was making remarkable improvement and would return to active politics soon.

Speaking at his Nairobi residence on Wednesday when Speakers Moses Wetang’ula and Amason Kingi paid him a visit, the ODM leader said the rumours only strengthened his resolve to come out of the hospital bed.

“Those who wrote me off while I was in hospital by declaring me dead only made me stronger and more determined to fight my sickness. Here I am, recovering and growing stronger by the day,” he said.

He said that his recovery was a testimony to God's protection, saying those who had spread the false reports had been put to shame.

Oburu admitted that the illness had slowed down him down but he was looking forward to returning to the political arena.

“The sickness slowed my political activities. Very soon, I will be back roaring in the best way I know how,” he said.

The senator thanked the National Assembly Speaker Wetang’ula, his Senate counterpart Kingi and other legislators for taking time to visit him following his discharge from hospital.

He said the visit had lifted his spirit and revealed that he missed participating in parliamentary debates and engaging in national political affairs.

“I have no words to explain my feelings after the Speakers of both Houses and fellow legislators created time to come and check on me,” he said.

“I miss being on the floor of the House debating and roaring in the political arena. I urge my supporters to pray for me and be patient because soon I will be back,” he added.

Despite his recent health challenges, Oburu kept his visitors entertained with his trademark humour while expressing confidence that he would soon resume his political duties.

The two Speakers condemned the spread of false information on social media, particularly rumours that the senator had died while undergoing treatment.

Wetang’ula said they were encouraged by the senator's recovery and wished him a full and speedy return to good health.

He, however, cautioned Oburu against rushing back into politics before fully recovering, urging him to give his health priority.

“Prioritise your health and avoid rushing back into political engagements before making a full recovery,” he said.

The National Assembly Speaker also praised the senator for his courage and determination in facing his health challenges.

Kingi said the Senate missed Dr Oburu's contribution to debates, parliamentary proceedings and national politics.

“As the Senate, we miss your contributions to proceedings and debates as well as your guidance in national politics. We pray that you get better and resume your political duties as soon as possible,” he said.

Those who accompanied the two Speakers included Senate Chief Whip David Wakoli, Senate Minority Leader Stewart Madzayo, Senators William Kisang and Daniel Maanzo.

Others were National Assembly Minority Whip Millie Odhiambo, Parliamentary Commissioner Mishi Mboko and MP Eve Obara.

World.title: Kenyans stranded after Saudi Arabia blocks entry over Ebola concerns
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

More than 300 Kenyans who travelled to Saudi Arabia in search of employment have been forced to return home after authorities blocked their entry over Ebola-related restrictions, leaving them stranded at the airport for two days.

The group, which departed Kenya on October 30, had travelled to the Gulf country on valid work visas but was denied entry upon arrival and subsequently repatriated, arriving back in the country on Monday.

The return follows a warning by Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale on Saturday, October 31, over restrictions imposed by Saudi Arabia on travellers from countries flagged over Ebola concerns.

Speaking to the media at Jomo Kenyatta International Airport (JKIA) on Monday, the affected workers recounted their ordeal, accusing authorities at the airport of subjecting them to harsh conditions as they waited to be repatriated.

“We were treated so harshly as though we had leprosy. We only took one meal per day and slept on the cold floors at the airport in Saudi Arabia,” said Kanyi Njau, one of the affected workers, claiming that some have even lost their luggage.

Beyond the difficult experience at the airport, the workers said their biggest concern was the financial loss incurred while preparing for the promised jobs.

Some said they had sold land, household belongings and other property, while others borrowed money to pay recruitment agents, process visas and secure travel documents in preparation for their departure.

Njau said the abrupt disruption had shattered the hopes of many who had invested heavily in securing employment abroad.

“Some of us sold things in our houses, even land. Some even took loans from shylocks just so that we could travel over there for the jobs, but now we are back with no hope,” she said.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

The workers are now appealing to the Kenyan Government to intervene and resolve the standoff with Saudi authorities before their visas expire, allowing them to return and take up the jobs they had secured.

Meanwhile, recruitment agencies have called on the Government to urgently clarify the restrictions, warning that uncertainty over a 21-day provision could disrupt the country's labour mobility programme.

Monika Mwema, the Secretary General of the Association of Skilled Migrant Agencies of Kenya (ASMAK), said recruiters had been caught off guard, with some workers already repatriated while others had confirmed tickets and were scheduled to travel.

“We are caught off guard. We have people who are coming back because they could not be allowed to enter Saudi Arabia, while others have confirmed tickets and are even supposed to leave tonight and tomorrow,” she said.

Mwema said the association was seeking clarification on what the 21-day provision meant for workers holding stamped Saudi work visas, including whether they would be required to undergo quarantine in Kenya or in a third country before being allowed into the Kingdom.

“Does it mean we have to quarantine our people here for the 21 days, then they are allowed to enter the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia? Or does it mean that we need to seek an alternative quarantine area where there is no case of Ebola?” she asked.

Kenyan jobseekers arrive at JKIA on November 2, 2026, after being denied entry into Saudi Arabia over Ebola-related restrictions. [Stafford Ondego, Standard]

She said recruiters were also concerned about the 90-day period within which migrant workers are required to travel after their visas are stamped, warning that delays could result in significant losses for agencies and prospective employees.

Mwema added that some workers had already undergone training and completed examinations in preparation for their deployment, while recruitment partners in Saudi Arabia were demanding to know when the workers would arrive.

“The losses are just too many. We have people who have already gone to school for training; others have done their examinations and are waiting to go. Our partners are calling us, asking when these people are coming, but we are all in the dark,” she said.

ASMAK is now seeking urgent engagement with the Kenyan Government and Saudi authorities to establish a clear way forward.

Mwema said the association was ready to engage the Government, including through a meeting with President William Ruto, to discuss the future of labour mobility between the two countries.

Saudi Arabia remains Kenya's biggest market for labour mobility, with recruiters warning that continued uncertainty could affect workers awaiting deployment and agencies with visas already processed.

World.title: Gachagua dismisses Uhuru reconciliation calls, says 'we are one team'
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua received at PCEA Kamangu in Kikuyu constituency by former Kiambu governor James Nyoro on November 1, 2026. [George Njunge, Standard]

Former Deputy President Rigathi Gachagua has dismissed calls for mediation between him and former President Uhuru Kenyatta, insisting that the two leaders remain in contact and have no differences requiring reconciliation.

Gachagua said attempts by Mount Kenya elders to broker peace between them were unnecessary, maintaining that he and the former Head of State continue to communicate, meet and share meals despite perceptions of a political fallout.

He challenged elders calling for reconciliation to instead focus on uniting the Mount Kenya community, warning that internal divisions could weaken the region's political voice and influence.

“On unity, as a community we have to remain united. Our unity is strength. Nimeona some elders in the newspaper wakisema tunataka to reconcile Rigathi Gachagua and Uhuru Kenyatta. How do you reconcile two brothers, who love one another and work together?” he posed.

The former Deputy President maintained that he and Uhuru were still on the same team, dismissing claims that their relationship had deteriorated to a point requiring third-party intervention.

“President Uhuru Kenyatta and I are one team. We work together. Please elders don’t reconcile us because there is no need for reconciliation. We are working together. There is no work there, we are one. We talk the same language, we meet, talk, we agree,” he said.

Gachagua further urged Mount Kenya elders to resist attempts to divide the community along political lines and instead promote dialogue and cohesion among its leaders.

“Our unity is our strength as a community. Please help me to unite Mount Kenya elders and tell people not to accept to be divided,” he added.

His remarks come amid growing calls by sections of Mount Kenya elders for reconciliation among influential political figures from the region following political differences that have emerged since the 2022 General Election.

Uhuru, who served as Kenya's fourth president from 2013 to 2022, remains an influential political figure in the region, while Gachagua has continued to position himself as a key voice in Mount Kenya politics.

World.title: Sifuna rallies opposition leaders to unite against Ruto in 2027
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Linda Mwananchi leader Edwin Sifuna adresses a rally at Ukunda in Kwale County on 31st October, 2026. [Omondi Onyango, Standard]

Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna’s Linda Mwananchi movement took its grassroots mobilisation tour to Kwale County, a day after unveiling its secretariat and leadership, with leaders urging the opposition to unite behind one candidate to face President William Ruto in 2027.

The unveiling had been marred by disagreement, with Wiper leader Kalonzo Musyoka jeered. Addressing a rally at Masai Grounds in Ukunda town, Sifuna said Kenyans were yearning for a single, strong opposition candidate and asked other leaders not to let them down.

“To send Ruto home, we need a strong team and a strong presidential candidate. I will ask other leaders to listen to the voices of the people politely because this is the voice of God,” he said.

The team made stopovers in Samburu, Kinango, Kwale town and Kombani during the day-long tour. Unlike earlier rallies in Mombasa, the Kwale events drew modest crowds, amid claims that local organisers had failed to mobilise supporters.

The mobilisation tour covered Samburu Town, Kinango Town, Kombani Junction, Lunga Lunga Town, and culminated in a major public rally at the Ukunda Showground.

The movement officially opened its new Kwale County office as part of a push to build county-level structures ahead of the 2027 General Election.

Addressing supporters in the rain, Sifuna declared that he will continue to build consensus among the opposition to ensure that they are united to send Ruto home in 2027. he said that divisions of the opposition leaders will guarantee Ruto a second term.

He warned against schemes to elbow local leaders out of the front lines, stressing that Kwale residents and local aspirants must drive the agenda on regional issues like water shortages and mineral exploitation. The Kwale tour marks the first public rallies after weeks without a large-scale county mobilisation exercise.

It has previously held gatherings in Mombasa and Taita Taveta as part of its plan to reach all 47 counties. The tour took place the same day the Orange Democratic Movement (ODM) was holding a rally at Jacaranda Grounds in Nairobi's Embakasi East constituency.

Embakasi East MP Babu Owino urged Sifuna, Musyoka, DCP leader Rigathi Gachagua and Jubilee leader Fred Matiang’i to agree on one presidential candidate, warning that time was running out.

“We are urging all opposition leaders to sit down and talk. We only have nine months to the General Election, and you should agree on one presidential challenger to President Ruto,” he said. “Sifuna, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i should come together now. United we stand, divided we fall.”

isii Senator Richard Onyonka said it was time for opposition leaders to lock themselves in a room and emerge with a single candidate to face Mr Ruto. The call was backed by Linda Mwananchi chairman Godfrey Osotsi and Secretary General Caroli Omondi.

Trans Nzoia Governor George Natembeya, however, said Sifuna was best placed to challenge the President and asked Mr Gachagua and Mr Musyoka to back him.

“I want to urge Gachagua and Kalonzo to back Sifuna for the opposition to secure an easy win against Ruto. I want to assure you that there will be no rigging of the election,” he said.

Meru Governor Kawira Mwangaza said Kenyans would reject Ruto at the ballot for failing to honour pledges, including those on women’s empowerment.

Sifuna accused the President of failing to protect the Constitution and the rights of Kenyans. “He has focused more on building houses and markets and failed to protect lives,” he said.

He also claimed the government had issued title deeds for smaller parcels than residents used to own, while land was stolen. He further alleged that the government was plotting to plunder mineral resources at Mrima Hill in Kwale and demanded that an agreement with American investors be made public.

World.title: Musonye to lead AFCON 2027 preparations
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya with Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee chairperson Nicholas Musonye on October 29, 2026. [Jonah Onyango, Standard]

Sports Cabinet Secretary Salim Mvurya has unveiled the Local Organising Committee (LOC) Standing Committee for the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON PAMOJA 2027), with Nicholas Musonye appointed chairman to oversee Kenya’s preparations for the continental football tournament.

Musonye will be deputised by Hussein Mohammed, while Anthony Lung’aho Inzihuli, also known as Antony Emmanuel Inzahuli Lung’aho, will serve as head of the secretariat and chief executive officer.

The committee is tasked with coordinating Kenya’s preparations, including stadium renovations, infrastructure development, operational planning and logistical arrangements ahead of the tournament, which Kenya will co-host with Uganda and Tanzania.

Mvurya said the committee brings together individuals with experience, professional expertise and leadership to help deliver a successful competition that meets the expectations of football fans, participating teams and the Confederation of African Football (CAF).

“I have unveiled the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) PAMOJA 2027 LOC Standing Committee, entrusting its members with the national responsibility of coordinating and overseeing Kenya’s preparations towards delivering a world-class, memorable and successful continental football tournament,” Mvurya said.

He challenged members to move from planning to implementation, emphasising operational readiness, coordination, strategic partnerships, financial accountability and adherence to delivery timelines.

“With less than eight months to kick-off, I challenged the committee to move decisively from planning to execution,” he said.

Besides Musonye, Mohammed and Lung’aho Inzihuli, the listed committee members include Football Kenya Federation (FKF) Vice-President McDonald Mariga and FKF National Executive Committee representative Robert Macharia.

Other members named in the roster are Timothy Nabea, a former FKF NEC member; Gabriel Mghendi; Peter Kamau; Kerubo Momanyi; Benard Lagat; Collins Kalee; Caleb Amwayi; Ken Rungu; and Dan Shikanda, the former AFC Leopards chairperson.

The list also includes Charles Njagi, Thomas Karugu, Evelyn Cheluget, Miriam Chepkoech, Rodgers Chimega, Diana Injendi Manyengo and Collins Were.

The 38 committee members also comprises representation across functional areas, including finance, technical matters, refereeing, legal affairs and youth development.

The committee is expected to coordinate the different aspects of tournament preparation and ensure that the relevant agencies and stakeholders work towards agreed targets.

Kenya’s preparations also include the development of Talanta Sports City, officially known as the Raila Odinga International Stadium, which is expected to strengthen the country's capacity to host major international football matches.

Mvurya said the planned high-profile encounter between German giants FC Bayern München and Dutch powerhouse AFC Ajax, scheduled for January 5, 2027, would provide an opportunity to assess the country’s readiness.

The event is expected to test security arrangements, transport and logistics, crowd management, operational systems and the overall fan experience.

The CS also disclosed that representatives of the two European clubs had visited Kenya to assess its capacity to host the proposed fixture.

He said the government was adopting a whole-of-government approach, involving relevant agencies responsible for security, immigration, tourism, travel and hospitality.

AFCON 2027 is expected to attract thousands of supporters, officials and international visitors, creating opportunities for hotels, airlines, tour operators, transport businesses and other service providers.

The government is also positioning the tournament as an opportunity to promote tourism, attract investment, develop sporting infrastructure and inspire young footballers.

Mvurya said the committee carries the responsibility of delivering an event that would bring national pride while creating a lasting legacy for the country.

“I reaffirmed their mandate and reminded them that they carry the hopes and aspirations of over 55 million Kenyans to deliver a tournament that brings pride and joy to the country while securing a lasting legacy in sports development, tourism, investment and economic opportunities,” he said.
