World.title: SC rejects woman's plea to terminate six-month pregnancy over marital discord
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Wednesday refused to allow a woman's plea for medical termination of her pregnancy which was over six months along citing marital discord with her husband.

The case came before a bench of Justices B V Nagarathna and R Mahadevan, which had expressed concern over the request during an earlier hearing on Monday.

The woman's husband opposed the termination, arguing that he too had a right over the unborn child and was willing to take care of the baby after birth.

The bench said the case was different from those involving rape, sexual assault or foetal abnormalities, where termination may be permitted under the law.



It questioned whether marital discord or alleged mistreatment by a husband and in-laws could, by itself, be grounds for ending an advanced pregnancy.

âIt is normal that wife talks against husband and husband talks against wife but it does not mean that you have to terminate the pregnancy on that ground. It is not a case of sexual assault or single woman becoming pregnant. Where are we heading as a society if the wife says that she wants termination of pregnancy because of her fight with the husband and in-laws...

What about the right of the father,â the bench had said on Monday.

World.title: 'Dialled wrong number, season of dharna': CJI's quip at man seeking rotation of SC-ST reserved seats
World.content:
CJI Surya Kant

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant on Wednesday quipped at a petitioner to organise public protests and demonstrations while rejecting his plea seeking mandatory rotation of seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in Parliament and state assemblies.A bench of CJI Surya Kant and justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana upheld the Allahabad high court order validating Section 9(1)(c) of the Delimitation Act, 2002, which provides for the identification of reserved constituencies in areas where the proportion of SC/ST residents is comparatively high.The Supreme Court, however, said the petitioner was free to approach public representatives and persuade them to adopt the principle of rotation."You are dialling the wrong number. This is a season of dharna, protest etc. You should also do the same," Bar and Bench quoted CJI Surya Kant as saying in a lighter vein."This is also a good ground for protest," he added.During the hearing, Justice Bagchi said that in a multiparty democracy, voters are expected to make electoral choices based on political ideologies rather than caste or religious considerations."In a political democracy, there are multiple political parties having different ideologies.The voters are expected to vote for the party, not for the religion. You may like or dislike a particular political ideology. Who is representing that ideology becomes irrelevant. You vote for that ideology. So that also defeats your argument," Justice Bagchi said.The bench also distinguished between the right to vote and any claimed right to contest an election from a particular constituency. It observed that candidates belonging to the general category remain eligible to contest from constituencies that are not reserved.The petitioner, Jagdish Singh, had challenged the continued reservation of his constituency for Scheduled Castes, claiming that it had remained reserved for nearly seven decades since its creation.He argued that the absence of a rotation mechanism violated Articles 14, 15 and 19 of the Constitution and restricted voters' electoral choices by limiting the candidates they could elect to members of the SC community.He further claimed that the existing arrangement benefited a handful of political families rather than advancing the interests of the wider community.Seeking a mechanism similar to the rotational reservation provided for panchayats and municipalities under Articles 243D and 243T of the Constitution, the petitioner urged the bench to direct periodic rotation of SC/ST-reserved constituencies.Justice Bagchi, however, disagreed with the argument that candidates from the majority community would anyway get elected in constituencies with a high SC population, making reservation unnecessary."That proceeds on the idea that a majority community will vote on community or caste lines. They may not vote on community and caste lines. The High Court cannot judicially pronounce on a democratic choice. That is for the voters to decide," Justice Bagchi said.The bench clarified that it could not rewrite the Constitution or the statute by introducing a rotation requirement that finds no mention in Articles 330 and 332 or the Delimitation Act.The Allahabad high court had held that Articles 330 and 332 merely prescribe the number of reserved seats in proportion to the population and leave the methodology for identifying reserved constituencies to Parliament under Article 327.It had found Section 9(1)(c) neither ultra vires nor violative of fundamental rights, ruling that courts cannot issue a mandamus directing the legislature to introduce a rotation provision.While acknowledging that rotation could better advance social and political justice by allowing SC/ST candidates to contest even from constituencies with smaller reserved-category populations, the high court had emphasised that the policy decision rests exclusively with Parliament.

World.title: Court grants bail to driver of bus in Bhandup accident case
World.content:
The Bombay High Court has granted bail to Santosh Sawant, driver of a bus of BEST, in the Bhandup station accident case in which four persons died and 12 persons suffered injuries.

The court said the defence argument had substance at the stage of bail: Sawant may not have received training that BEST requires to operate a bus that runs on electricity. Justice Shyam Chandak made the observation while granting bail.

The court took note of a letter that a depot manager of BEST sent to the police on January 7. The letter stated that the undertaking did not have a certificate that confirmed whether Sawant had received training to drive a bus that runs on electricity. The name of Sawant was not on the list of drivers who had training. BEST assigned Sawant to operate a bus on Route 606 from December 1, 2025, even though the name of Sawant was not on the list.

The prosecution alleged that Sawant drove the bus at speed and without care when the bus went out of control near Bhandup railway station (West). The bus hit pedestrians who stood near a bus stop.

Devendra Patil, lawyer for Sawant, argued that BEST assigned Sawant to drive a bus that runs on electricity although Sawant had not undergone training. The defence submitted that refusal of the assignment could have led to action under discipline rules and to loss of job. It was brought to the notice of the court that there was no evidence that Sawant drove the bus at speed on purpose or that Sawant was under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

The court considered that Sawant had worked with BEST since 2011 and had no record of an accident. The court also noted that the trial may not conclude soon and that the case lists 56 witnesses.

Sawant had approached the High Court after the Sessions Court rejected the bail plea of Sawant. Sawant has been in jail for 11 months since the arrest of Sawant. The court accepted the argument of Sawant and granted bail to him.

World.title: 24 hours after High Court rap, BMC fails to restore Dia Mirza’s video on pollution-free Diwali
World.content:
Over 24 hours after the Bombay High Court directed the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) to restore the video message of actor Dia Mirza’s appeal for a noise-free and pollution-free Diwali, the BMC has failed to do so. Sources in the BMC say they will study the court order and take an appropriate call on it. They refused to give a timeline for the restoration of the video. Meanwhile, the opposition and civil rights organisations hit out at the government for the lapse. Shiv Sena UBT demanded that the civic body should restore the video immediately.

“The BJP regime is now blatantly disrespecting the Honourable Court. Firstly, it criticised Dia’s video because of her surname. The video was made for an appeal of the High Court order itself. Then the BJP calls her anti-national. For what? Raising environmental issues? Making a video appeal for a court order? The regime can’t handle the administration – be it the city or the country,” Shiv Sena UBT leader Aditya Thackeray told The Hindu on Wednesday (November 4, 2026).

Civil rights activist Sumaira Abdulali, who has been working for the cause of noise pollution, demanded that the BMC should give an explanation about why it had pulled down a video which was recorded as per the directives of the Bombay High Court.

“The reason they took it down was not explainable. They were only following the court order. How can a politician interfere in a court order? The second question is to ignore the order 24 hours later. The government is not respecting the court of law. The noise rules were made in the year 2000. The first orders started coming around in the year 2003. We have still not been following those court orders. The intention seems to be not to follow the court order in this aspect (noise pollution). Whether we are going to follow them or not is the real question. The record shows that we don’t,” she told The Hindu.

She said that she was similarly targeted for raising voice against noise pollution. “Instead of following the court order, we are tarnishing people for other reasons, which is subverting the law. This is very brazen. But it has been happening for a long time. I have been targeted for years in the same way,” she said.

Last week, the BMC had uploaded the videos of celebrities appealing to people to celebrate noise-free and air pollution-free Diwali. This was done as per the directions of the Bombay High Court. The celebrities who participated in the voluntary campaign included Madhuri Dixit, cricketer Ajinkya Rahane, actor Nishigandha Wad and UN Goodwill ambassador Dia Mirza.

Soon thereafter, BJP Mumbai president Ameet Satam had publicly posted against Ms. Mirza, telling the BMC that they do not need her advice to celebrate their festival. This had led to the BMC pulling down the tweet. The Bombay High Court took note of this and expressed displeasure at the move. It directed the BMC to restore the video message of Ms. Mirza. The orders were issued on October 3 (Tuesday).

BMC sources said that the law and judiciary department officials were busy on Wednesday (November 4) with the urgent demolition drive, which was held in Borivali. That drive was held after the Supreme Court had ordered the withholding of BMC Commissioner’s salary for the failure to raze illegal structures. “We will study the order and take a decision on it,” a BMC official said.

In the order issued on November 3, the Bombay High Court has also asked the Maharashtra government if it can designate regulated timings for the bursting of firecrackers during Diwali to prevent health hazards and environmental damage.

World.title: After milk and curd, prices of ghee, butter and paneer too up
World.content:
After the prices of milk and curd were increased by the Karnataka Milk Federation (KMF) upwards of ₹8 per litre, Bangalore Urban, Rural & Ramanagara District Co-Operative Milk Producers Societies Union Limited (BAMUL) has increased the prices of ghee, butter and paneer too.

The revised prices, released on November 4, will come into effect across the State from November 5. The prices were last hiked in July 2026, by 10%.

While earlier a one-litre ghee sachet was priced at ₹715, it will now be ₹850 per litre. Ghee pet jar, which was earlier ₹735, will now cost ₹870 per litre. For five litres, the price has increased from ₹3,575 to ₹4,250. Ghee tin of one litre has been increased by ₹120, from ₹750 to ₹870. For a 15-litre tin, the price is up from ₹11,625 to ₹14,000.

A 100 gm butter blister pack has been increased from ₹600 to ₹900, while a 500 gm butter salted pack is up from ₹310 to ₹380 and unsalted butter from ₹330 to ₹390. Paneer pack of 200 gm has been increased from ₹96 to ₹115 and one kg paneer pack from ₹480 to ₹485.

Criticising the move, P.C. Rao, honorary president of Bangalore Hotels Association, said, “This was expected, but it is a huge financial burden on the hotel industry. An additional 25% burden including milk, curd, paneer, ghee, and butter prices hike.”

World.title: HC summons Madurai Commissioner of Police
World.content:
The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court on Wednesday summoned Madurai City Commissioner of Police after a petitioner complained that a police officer in uniform was smoking a cigarette while on duty at a police check post near Sri Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple.

A Division Bench of Justices P. Velmurugan and K.K. Ramakrishnan was hearing a public interest litigation petition filed by A. Radhakrishnan of Salem, who said he was a devotee of the temple. The petitioner said on October 16 at around 7 a.m., he noticed a Special Sub-Inspector of Police smoking a cigarette while on duty at the police check post near the temple.

He said despite him questioning this, the police officer continued to smoke. The incident had caused him mental anguish and raised concerns regarding discipline among police personnel in public and religious places.

He said he had lodged a complaint in this regard. However, the action taken appeared to be confined to an internal warning and temporary duty assignment, without adequately demonstrating consideration of the applicable statutory provisions, the relevant service rules and the wider issues raised in the complaint.

He sought a direction to the authorities to take appropriate preventive measures across the State to ensure discipline and effective enforcement of relevant statutory proceedings and service rules. The court posted the matter for hearing to November 12.

World.title: Mukka Sravani set to become new Mayor of Vizag; YSRCP begins internal post-mortem
World.content:
The NDA Mayor candidate Mukka Sravani has registered a landslide victory in the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) elections, defeating her YSRCP rival, Varudu Kalyani, by a massive margin of 2,44,644 votes to emerge as the new Mayor of Visakhapatnam.

According to Returning Officer B. Dayanidhi, Ms. Sravani secured 5,85,454 votes, while Ms. Kalyani polled 3,40,810 votes. The massive margin reflected the overwhelming mandate in favour of the NDA candidate in the mayoral election. The Returning Officer handed over the declaration certificate to Ms. Sravani late on Tuesday night, formally confirming her victory.

With this victory, Ms. Sravani is set to become the second Telugu Desam Party (TDP) leader to be elected Mayor of Visakhapatnam through a direct election, after D.V. Subba Rao, who won the mayoral election in 1987. Her victory also marks the continuation of TDP leadership in the Mayor’s office, following Peela Srinivasa Rao, who served as Mayor from 2025 to 2026.

Of the 120 wards in the municipal corporation, the NDA has emerged victorious in 98, with the Telugu Desam Party (TDP) winning 64 wards. The Jana Sena Party (JSP) has secured 26 wards, while the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has won eight wards, taking the alliance’s combined tally to 98.

In contrast, the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) managed to win only 13 wards, a significant setback for the party. Independent candidates have also made their presence felt by winning eight wards, while the CPI(M) secured one ward.

Meanwhile, the YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) has initiated an internal post-mortem of its electoral defeat, with senior leaders discussing the reasons behind the party’s performance and the lapses that may have contributed to the outcome.

Sources from the party said that several senior leaders reportedly raised concerns over alleged irregularities at certain polling stations, including issues relating to polling booths, ballot boxes and the sudden rise in the voting percentage. Some leaders alleged that polling staff had been misused at a few booths, potentially affecting the electoral process. They also felt that the party leadership and its cadre should have been more vigilant and alert during polling and counting, and that certain lapses could have been prevented had they monitored the process more closely.

The leaders discussed the party’s future course of action, including the need to examine the alleged irregularities, identify organisational shortcomings and take corrective measures to strengthen the party. The discussions also focused on the steps to be taken to rebuild the organisation and prepare for future political challenges.

World.title: U.S. judge temporarily blocks deportation of detained Afghans to Afghanistan or Pakistan
World.content:
A federal judge in New York temporarily blocked the Trump administration’s plans to deport Afghans detained in the United States to Afghanistan or Pakistan on Tuesday (November 3, 2026), after advocates and dozens of members of Congress warned that their lives would be at risk.

The government told the court on Tuesday (November 3, 2026) that Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) had no chartered or commercial flights to deport Afghan nationals to Afghanistan or Pakistan at least until the end of the week. Judge Valerie Caproni’s order, which expires on Saturday (November 7, 2026), directs officials to adhere to that statement. ICE books deportation flights weeks in advance.

A letter led by California Democratic Representative Scott Peters and signed by 65 other members of the House and Senate said they were “extremely concerned that sending vulnerable people” would expose them to “persecution, torture, or even death”. The letter was sent on Monday (November 2, 2026) to Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin.

Immigrant rights organisations have also warned that those deported could face retaliation from the Taliban.

Thousands of Afghans fled persecution and feared for their lives after helping the U.S. military and aid groups in Afghanistan.

According to court documents obtained by the Associated Press, the U.S. planned to deport Afghan immigrants on Monday on flights from Louisiana, where ICE has detention and processing facilities, to Pakistan.

President Donald Trump’s administration has deported thousands of immigrants to countries other than their own. In some cases, it has used third-country deportations when removal to a person’s country of origin was not possible, including when formal diplomatic relations were absent, as is the case with Afghanistan’s Taliban government. In other instances, third-country deportations have been used as a deterrent.

Advocates and attorneys said more than 80 detained Afghans had contacted them after ICE notified them that they could be deported this week via Pakistan. They include women, a police officer, members of religious minorities and people whose family members served in the U.S. military. Most fled Afghanistan because of persecution and do not have legal representation, according to Human Rights First and AfghanEvac, a nonprofit organisation that advocates for immigrants.

Before the judge signed her order, Zia Ahmad Takal, deputy spokesman for Afghanistan’s foreign ministry, said “the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan expresses its serious concern” about reports that the U.S. planned to transfer Afghans to Pakistan.

Mr. Takal called on the U.S. to ensure that decisions or actions were based on the rights and “legitimate demands” of those involved. He said “third-party countries should not engage in dealings concerning the fate of another nation’s citizens”.

“Today is a good day,” Shawn VanDiver, president of AfghanEvac, said at a news conference. “But I want to be honest with you, this is a reprieve, not a resolution. We haven’t stopped this fight forever. This is just a pause.”

Savitri Arvey, director of policy, refugee and immigrant rights for Human Rights First, said people returned to Afghanistan “face grave, systematic dangers”, including arbitrary detention, executions, public flogging and retaliatory violence.

“The stakes were very, very high,” she said, noting that women and girls faced severe restrictions in Afghanistan, including systematic denials of education, employment and public speech.

Advocates expressed concern about the role of the Pakistani government in facilitating returns to Afghanistan and the lack of information about arrangements made between the U.S. and Pakistan.

“We celebrate today, but we’re getting right back to work tomorrow, continuing to make sure through our flight tracking that none of these flights are taking off,” Ms. Arvey said.

Abdul Qahar Afghan contributed from Jalalabad, Afghanistan.

World.title: NVS-03 reaches geosynchronous orbit; satellite in good health
World.content:
The NVS-03 satellite launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) on October 30, 2026, has reached the intended Geo Synchronous Orbit.

See The Hindu’s visual story on India’s space journey.

ISRO said in an update on Wednesday (November 4, 2026) that following four successful orbit manoeuvres, the satellite has reached Geo Synchronous Orbit (35765 km x 36196 km) at an inclination of 29.980.

“Four orbit manoeuvres have been successfully completed with a cumulative LAM engine burn of 6164 seconds. With this the satellite has reached Geo Synchronous Orbit [35765 km x 36196 km] at an inclination of 29.980,” ISRO said.

The NVS-03 satellite was successfully injected into 170.3 km x 38080 km orbit by GSLV on October 30.

The NVS-03 is the third satellite in the next generation navigation satellite system envisaged for providing continuity of navigation services for the IRNSS series.

The satellite carries indigenous atomic clock along with the procured clocks. It also includes L1 signal in addition to L5 and S band signals with coverage over Indian land mass and a region extending 1500 km around Indian geopolitical boundary.

The space agency also said that the satellite’s health is normal.

The development is significant as ISRO in 2025 was unable to perform the intended orbit raising operations for the NVS-02 satellite due to a valve malfunction. The NVS-02, the second satellite in the NVS series, was launched by the ISRO on January 29, 2025.

World.title: Political activities have no place in educational institutions: Keralam HC
World.content:
A Division Bench of the Kerala High Court observed that political activities such as dharna, hunger strikes and Satyagraha have “no place in a constitutional democracy, much less in academic institutions”, as it quashed a Single Bench order that had permitted 16 Students’ Federation of India (SFI) activists to appear for semester examinations at the Sree Sankaracharya University of Sanskrit, Kalady.

The Court cited another Division Bench ruling from 2017, observing that educational institutions are meant to impart education, not politics. It also said anyone indulging in such activities in an educational institution would be liable to be expelled or rusticated.

The Division Bench of Justices Anil K. Narendran and S. Muralee Krishna recalled that the 2017 decision had also quoted B.R. Ambedkar’s words in 1949. Ambedkar had stated that “to maintain democracy, we must abandon the bloody methods of revolution”, that “we must abandon the method of civil disobedience, non-cooperation and Satyagraha”, and that where constitutional methods were open, there could be no justification for these unconstitutional methods.

On this premise, the Court held that a suspended student would have to suffer the consequences of a suspension, such as an attendance shortage.

In the absence of statements from the students indicating that they were qualified to appear for the examinations, the Single Bench erred in granting permission, the Division Bench observed. It further said the students had not brought forward any evidence of the required internal assessment marks or attendance before the Single Bench.

The students were under suspension pending an inquiry, for allegedly staging a mock cremation of the Vice-Chancellor, Ciza Thomas, manhandling her and attempting to damage property. The University Syndicate had constituted an inquiry committee to look into the alleged incident and take disciplinary action. The committee had found the students guilty and recommended action.

The SFI activists have denied the allegations, claiming that their protest was meant to highlight their 18-point charter of demands, including the appointment of required faculty and the provision of basic facilities for students across various departments.

World.title: US Vice President JD Vance says Iran war is 'the reason we lost' midterms
World.content:
US Vice President JD Vance said on Wednesday that the Iran war had doomed Republicans in the midterm elections, moving to distance himself from the unpopular conflict ahead of a possible 2028 White House run.

“The reason we lost is the war. The president himself said so last night,” Vance said in a lengthy post on X — apparently referring to President Donald Trump’s remarks that the Iran war was “part of it” but that it was still justified.

“If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so. Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that’s at least honest,” added Vance.

“But everyone knows why we lost. And any honest conversation about where we go from here must start there.”

The Democratic wave in Tuesday’s midterms has raised major questions over Vance’s previous status as the frontrunner for the Republican nomination in the 2028 presidential election. He has not yet formally declared that he will run.

Vance, a longtime vocal critic of US foreign interventionism, had reportedly been sceptical behind the scenes about the war on Iran that Trump and Israel launched in late February.

Vance also acknowledged that Republican voters who backed Trump and himself two years ago had switched sides due to the war and its effects on the US economy.

“The main problem is that many people who voted for Trump/Vance in 2024 voted for Democrats in 2026,” the vice president said.

He said a pollster that he respected showed that the Iran war and the economy were key factors in voters abandoning Republicans.

“In his polling, he saw that a lot of Trump 2024 voters were angry and planning to vote for Democrats,” Vance wrote. “He asked those voters who had abandoned us what would cause them to come back on our team. The top four answers, accounting for nearly all of the responses, were:

End the war Focus on cost of living/inflation Put America First Change our relationship to Israel.”

Top Senate Democrat says Iran war ‘must end’

Meanwhile, Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer said that the Iran war “must end” and suggested his party’s incoming majority in Congress could use their control over government funding to press for that goal.

“The American people don’t know what the heck we’re fighting for in Iran,” Schumer tells journalists, adding that Trump has never made it clear and “changes his mind day to day, minute to minute”.

“This war must end. It must end,” Schumer added.

He later noted that the “power of the purse” is “one of the ways of deterring a president who does war without the consent of the American people”.

“Make no mistake: whenever Trump defies the will of the American people or the law, we will launch investigations, take him to court and entangle him in legislative razor wire,” Schumer warns. “The days of Trump’s supplicant Senate are over.”

World.title: Petrol price dropped by Rs7.06 per litre, high-speed diesel by Rs3.71
World.content:
The government on Wednesday cut the price of petrol by Rs7.06 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.71.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs362.00 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs387.81. This is the third consecutive reduction in fuel prices.

The prices are applicable for Nov 5 (Thursday), according to a notification by the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra).

The latest price cut came after international oil prices fell under $100 in volatile trade on Wednesday, as investors awaited Washington’s next move in the US-Israeli war with Iran after President Donald Trump’s Republican Party lost control of Congress in midterm elections.

Brent futures were down $4.50, or 4.3 per cent, to $99.07 a barrel at 1619pm GMT (9:19pm, PKT), while US West Texas Intermediate crude futures are down $4.13, or 4.3pc, to $92.02.

The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

Under an arrangement announced on Monday for 30 days, oil refineries will contribute to the petroleum levy by bearing a cumulative impact of Rs15 billion, according to the government. This would allow a Rs14.71 reduction in the petrol price at the consumer end.

Addressing a press conference on Tuesday, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik said efforts were being made to introduce a similar system for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

He also hinted at the latest reduction in fuel prices, saying “even better news will come before us”.

Meanwhile, the Jamaat-i-Islami and the government are set to follow up on their recent discussions on possible relief in petroleum prices and hold another round of talks on Thursday, the party said.

Rise in fuel prices

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on Feb 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm, and fuel allocations for official vehicles have been cut by 50pc for three months.

On Sept 13, PM Shehbaz also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, the petroleum minister announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give Ogra the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and HSD are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

Additional input by Reuters

World.title: Opposition leaders gather at JUI-F chief Fazl's Islamabad residence to discuss KP emergency
World.content:
Opposition leaders on Wednesday arrived at the residence of Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman in Islamabad to discuss the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, among other matters.

A statement by the JUI-F on social media said that opposition leaders in the National Assembly (NA) and Senate, Mahmood Khan Achakzai and Allama Raja Nasir Abbas, respectively, along with key PTI leaders, were attending a meeting to discuss “the situation of emergency and governor’s rule” in KP.

The meeting was also expected to discuss plans to hold a multi-party conference (MPC).

Meanwhile, according to a statement by the opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) — headed by Achakzai — the meeting was also “discussing unity and solidarity among opposition parties, the supremacy of the Constitution and law, the protection of democratic rights, a joint strategy to address the current political situation, and a future course of action”.

TTAP termed it a meeting of a “united opposition”. On Aug 20, following a meeting between Fazl and Achakzai, the alliance and JUI-F had announced plans to form a “united opposition”.

MNA Asad Qaiser, PTI Secretary General Salman Akram Raja, NA Chief Whip Amir Dogar and Senator Noorul Haq Qadri were present from PTI in Wednesday’s huddle, while TTAP spokesperson Akhundzada Hussain Ahmad Yousafzai was attending as well.

TTAP said that PTI core committee member and Imran Khan’s legal counsel, Khalid Yousaf Chaudhry, as well as Agha Nasir Shirazi, were also participating in the meeting.

JUI-F was represented by its vice-president and KP chapter president Senator Maulana Attaur Rehman, senators Kamran Murtaza and Maulana Attaul Haq Darwish, alongside party members Akram Khan Durrani, Aslam Ghauri, Maulana Salahuddin Ayubi, Hafiz Hamdullah and Zahid Durrani, the party said.

The gathering comes a day after PTI said it would welcome support from Fazl in its struggle against the government, with Raja telling the media that the party would welcome anyone who stood by it and supported its struggle.

“It is possible that some may walk with us for one mile, some for 10 miles, and some may go with us till the end. But why should we reject them?” the PTI secretary general said.

Fazl has been critical of the federal government over the imposition of governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. He accused the Centre of reneging on its commitments amid his efforts to mediate between the federal and KP governments.

Since mid-October , the veteran politician and key federal ministers have also made harsh remarks against each other, after Fazl accused the Centre of depriving the provinces of their rights.

Last week, Fazl accused the government of misusing the Constitution and resorting to unconstitutional measures in imposing the emergency.

In September, TTAP and PTI leaders said they intended to hold consultations to call an MPC to discuss several issues, including the creation of new provinces, law and order, and the economy. This was prior to the government’s declaration of emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11.

In the days preceding the emergency, political tensions between the Centre and the opposition — including the PTI, which was in power in KP — had remained high since Imran’s party announced a protest march to Islamabad to demand his release.

World.title: Govt says Islamabad's One Constitution Avenue to be turned into a five-star hotel
World.content:
The federal government on Wednesday said that a joint investigation team had revealed that Islamabad’s One Constitution Avenue was built on “irregularities and rigging” and announced that the residential building will soon be turned into a five-star hotel.

The building, a skyscraper in the federal capital that houses residential apartments, had its lease cancelled by the Capital Development Authority (CDA) due to the company behind the project defaulting on payments. The decision was upheld by the Islamabad High Court (IHC) in April.

The building was initially supposed to be a five-star hotel project; however, instead of functioning as a five-star hotel, it was converted into residential apartments and commercial areas. The IHC’s order led to the mass evictions of residents in May, following which Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif formed a joint investigation team (JIT) to probe the matter.

Addressing a press conference on Wednesday alongside Information Minister Attaullah Tarar and State Minister for Interior Tallal Chaudhry, Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal said the JIT presented its report to the federal cabinet today, noting that the project was fraudulent.

He said that the report had input from the National Accountability Bureau (NAB), the Federal Investigation Agency, the Federal Board of Revenue, the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan, the Intelligence Bureau and Inter-Services Intelligence.

“They carefully assessed this project and presented the report, and it was approved,” Iqbal said. “The JIT has clearly identified that the project was created based on irregularity and rigging and that the bidding process was manipulated.”

Iqbal added that, according to the report, rules were ignored to provide benefits and the company which was given the lease had no rightful claim.

“In this whole matter, the CDA was found complicit, and similarly, the conditions of the bank guarantee were removed to provide benefits to the developers,” he stated. “The work which was carried out was conducted in a very suspicious manner and the apartments were sold illegally.”

He noted that the project was initially approved as a five-star hotel two decades ago, but later it was turned into apartments.

“The JIT has identified Abdul Hafeez Sheikh, who has been called the mastermind and was found to be in connivance with CDA officials,” the planning minister added.

“CDA officers such as Kamran Lashari, who was chairman at the time, Dr Faisal Awan, Azhar Ali Chaudhry, Brigadier (retired) Nasrullah and Marhoom Rai Nawaz Kharal were found to be colluding in fraud,” he said.

Iqbal said that as a result of the scheme, the national exchequer suffered losses, while the aforementioned people “gained financially and defrauded the Pakistani people of their invested capital”.

“The JIT recommended that Sheikh and his company be blacklisted from future public projects and that proceedings be launched against him,” the minister added.

It was further recommended that the project be reviewed and work undertaken to achieve its original purpose as a hotel. Additionally, the report recommended that the project be started anew and auctioned in a transparent manner, he said.

“Security clearance and clearance from other institutions should also be sought so that future projects have a steady framework to prevent this type of fraud from happening again,” Iqbal said, adding that fire safety and other protocols must also be ensured.

He added that according to the JIT, the project should be renamed, as the name ‘One Constitution Avenue’ was the same address as the finance ministry.

“They used this address for marketing purposes only,” the minister asserted.

“There will be action taken against those found involved in fraud. The government has a responsibility to protect those who were robbed or swindled.”

Iqbal said it was decided that those defrauded would receive compensation, their principal investments would be refunded and payments would be adjusted against their Kibor interest “so they do not suffer losses”.

“It was also recommended that the CDA and its ordinance be overhauled and that an independent master plan commission be formed to shut the door on such fraud in the future,” he announced.

Iqbal added that all of the records must be digitised and officers should be rotated between the state planning, enforcement and building control departments every two years.

“People have held offices for 20 years and opened offices of fraud. With this constant rotation, it will close the door on these corrupt projects,” he explained.

“In the same way, pre-audit auctions and contracts from third parties will be consulted, and in light of this JIT report, NAB has been ordered to take action against anyone involved in this project, and those who facilitated it,” Iqbal said.

Meanwhile, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi also addressed a press conference on Wednesday and said that the government had now regained possession of the skyscraper, vowing to turn the building into a five-star hotel within months.

“In official documents, we always had possession of this building, and after the cabinet’s approval, it is now legally in our possession,” Naqvi maintained.

He regretted that the government’s decision to regain control of the building earlier this year had been portrayed as a “crime”, decrying how Islamabad’s land had been infringed upon.

“We will try our best to convert this building into a five-star hotel in months,” the interior minister announced, reaffirming that this had been the project’s primary objective.

“There is a severe shortage of hotels in Islamabad. We will soon try to make an agreement with a large chain of hotels and convert this building into a five-star hotel,” he stated.

He commended the CDA chairman and legal team for pursuing this case; however, Naqvi also reproached the CDA for being at fault.

“NAB will tell who is responsible,” he said.

“As per JIT recommendations, we will try to make rightful payments to the occupants,” Naqvi said. “This is binding for us after the report.”

The interior minister said he was grateful to PM Shehbaz, recalling that the prime minister had assured him that the right decision would be taken.

Naqvi further said that a residents’ committee, which was overseeing the building’s affairs, had been abolished.

“A CDA member will look after the building’s matters from now on,” he said, reiterating that the hotel would be operational soon and be a “gift to the people of Islamabad”.

World.title: Asif says Chaudhry Salik's remarks about corruption in Punjab 'beyond my understanding'
World.content:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif said on Wednesday that Minister for Overseas Pakistanis Chaudhry Salik Hussain’s remarks regarding corruption in Punjab were “beyond my understanding”.

During a talk show on a private television channel on Monday, the Pakistan Muslim League-Quaid (PML-Q) leader had lavished praise on former Punjab chief minister Chaudhry Pervez Elahi. However, he had also criticised the present provincial administration, headed by Chief Minister Maryam Nawaz, alleging that he regularly heard complaints of corruption.

On Tuesday, CM Maryam had sent a Rs5 billion defamation notice to the minister, demanding that he retract his remarks.

In a post on the social media platform X on Wednesday, Asif said, “Chaudhry Salik Sahib is very respected in my eyes; I respect his elders just as I respect my own.

“His statement regarding corruption in Punjab is beyond my limited political understanding. Corruption is the biggest issue in our society and it is the collective responsibility of the political leadership, both at the central and provincial levels, to rid the country of this curse,” he said.

He went on to say that Salik was a part of “both the federal and provincial governments and the leadership of both these governments lies with the PML-N”.

“If this statement is part of some future political agenda — to target Maryam Nawaz’s government and carve out space for himself in Punjab and at the Centre to secure his political future — then it starts to make sense,” Asif said.

He also praised Maryam’s performance, saying her work across Punjab’s cities and villages and the service standards being set by her government would pose a “very difficult challenge” for its opponents.

Meanwhile, Punjab Senior Minister Marriyum Aurangzeb sought an apology from Salik over his comments, saying that the PML-Q leader was “himself admitting that he has no evidence to support the allegations he made regarding corruption in the Punjab government”.

“After this, what dignity, justice, and principles demand is clear: an apology should be sought for the lack of evidence and for making baseless allegations, rather than turning the transfer of a single DC into an issue of personal ego,” she wrote.

The Punjab minister called on Salik to either fulfil his responsibilities as a minister or step down from his role “instead of engaging in empty rhetoric about eradicating corruption from society and promoting good governance”.

“We will not tolerate false and baseless allegations against the chief minister who has set an example of serving the people in Pakistan through hard work and transparency in two and a half years,” Aurangzeb asserted.

Acknowledging that corruption existed as a “disease in every society in the world”, she contended that Punjab was the only province where the chief minister herself was “leading the campaign to eliminate corruption”.

What did Salik say?

During his interview, Salik had also questioned lavish government spending , particularly the use of official aircraft , arguing that public representatives should remain mindful of the country’s economic difficulties. Officials using government aircraft, he said, should be required to demonstrate the tangible outcomes and public benefits of their trips.

He further called for greater ministerial accountability, proposing that the federal as well as provincial ministers should be empowered to perform their duties, but also be held answerable for their performance.

The remarks carry particular political significance given the fractured relationship between the Chaudhry family and the PTI leadership. Salik, the younger son of PML-Q president Chaudhry Shujaat Hussain, belongs to a family whose political loyalties have diverged sharply since the ouster of Imran Khan’s government in 2022 through a no-confidence vote.

While Elahi and his son, former federal minister Moonis Elahi, aligned themselves with the PTI, the Shujaat family chose to stand with the Sharifs. Salik’s elder brother, Shafay Hussain, is also part of CM Maryam’s cabinet in Punjab.

On Tuesday, CM Maryam said the PML-Q leader’s anger stemmed from neither corruption nor progress. She said the issue was that she had changed the deputy commissioner of Gujrat a few days earlier, whereas Salik wanted a DC of his choice to be appointed.

The defamation notice — sent to Salik, ARY News host Naeem Ashraf Butt and the channel’s chairman — said the minister’s remarks were not just an expression of disagreement with policy or “ordinary political criticism”, but conveyed “serious imputations” of widespread corruption in the province.

The notice called on them to retract the remarks, publish an “unconditional and unequivocal apology and clarification” and “remove or suitably correct” the portions of the interview in question. It also demanded a sum of Rs5bn in damages.

Meanwhile, responding to Maryam’s remarks, Salik said he stood by his statement and had responded honestly to a question during the interview.

The minister’s remarks had also drawn a sharp rebuttal from Punjab Information Minister Azma Bokhari, who advised Salik not to “bite the hand that feeds him”. Bokhari also alleged that his displeasure stemmed from a request to appoint a deputy commissioner of his choice being turned down.

World.title: ECP objects to retired SC judge's remarks about 2023 ruling on polls in Punjab and KP, reserved seats case
World.content:
The Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Wednesday objected to remarks made by former senior puisne judge of the Supreme Court of Pakistan, Mansoor Ali Shah, regarding polls in KP and Punjab and the reserved seats case pertaining to the PTI.

Shah made the remarks at an event organised by the US-based Community Alliance for Peace and Justice on October 29, where he was asked about his dissenting opinion in the 2023 SC ruling on provincial elections in Punjab and KP and whether it was a “turning point” and the beginning of a “division” within the SC.

In its 3-2 verdict, the SC, after taking a suo motu notice, directed that elections should be held within 90 days in both provinces. Two judges, including Shah, had dissented from the ruling, saying that the suo motu proceedings initiated by then-chief justice of Pakistan Umar Ata Bandial, were “wholly unjustified”, besides being initiated with “undue haste”.

In their detailed reasoning , they explained that the SC by a majority of 4-3 and not 3-2 had dismissed the suo motu hearing on polls delay in Punjab and KP and therefore the same should be considered as the “Order of the Court”.

It had resulted in a controversy, with the government igniting a raging debate claiming that the ruling was a 4-3 majority decision in its favour and not a 3-2 verdict against.

In response to the question, Shah said that this was the time when the ex-chief justice was forming “like-minded benches”, adding that three or four judges were attending to the majority of the cases.

He said that initially the matter was taken by the high courts. He said that the SC judges had gathered in the ante-room and discussed with the chief justice at the time that suo motu notice should not be taken at this point. He said that it was “agreed” to wait but days later a SC bench took up the matter under suo motu powers as he denounced the “one-man show” going on at the time.

He said that at the time, two SC judges — Justice Yahya Afridi and Justice Athar Minallah — had dismissed the petitions in the case. He said that the SC bench was later reconstituted, adding that since two judges had decided the matter, the verdict could not be dismissed. He said that this sparked the 4-3, 2-3 debate.

Shah also defended the 2024 verdict in the reserved seats case, wherein PTI was declared eligible for seats reserved for women and minorities, in a setback to the ruling coalition.

“We said that the PTI was a political party and it was wrong to deprive [them of their symbol] … and illegal,” he said, recalling that this was a decision “that nobody liked”.

In a statement on Wednesday, the ECP referred to the remarks made by Shah, saying that they ignored “basic constitutional and legal facts related to the election matters and judicial decisions”.

“It is highly inappropriate to present the judicial record for specific purposes through selective quotations, incomplete perspectives and one-sided interpretations,” the statement said.

The electoral watchdog said that Shah had claimed that the SC’s majority decision about the elections in 2023 was a 4-3 verdict and that the suo motu notice and relevant petitions were dismissed.

The ECP also stated that according to Shah’s claims, the election ruling was a “minority decision” and the commission could not have held polls.

Regarding the PTI case, it said that Shah had declared the order for withdrawal of the party’s electoral symbol during the 2024 elections as “illegal”.

The commission said that the election symbol was subject to transparent intra-party elections as per Sections 208 and 209 of the Election Act 2017. It added that “till date, PTI has not been able to fulfil the requirement”.

The ECP said PTI was supposed to hold intra-party elections by June 30, 2021, and the commission had given the party three chances; however, the party failed to hold intra-party elections.

As a result, the commission said that the party’s election symbol was withdrawn, which, the ECP added, was also upheld by the SC in 2025, along with rejecting review petitions filed by the PTI.

The ECP further stated that PTI held intra-party elections after five years and its proceedings remained pending before the commission as the “PTI itself has taken a stay order from a high court”. It further stated that as per the commission’s records, the PTI was still enlisted as a political party.

The ECP added that only political parties which contested the elections had a right to the reserved seats.

“These political parties are required to submit a preferred list of candidates before the elections, while PTI has not submitted any preferred list,” it stated.

It further stated that it was mandatory for a political party to win at least one seat and that independent members were not entitled to reserved seats and therefore, the ECP gave the seats to the eligible parties.

It said that if the PTI was entitled to the reserved seats, then “Articles 51 and 106 of the Constitution and Section 104 of the Elections Act 2917 become ineffective”.

The ECP said that it was “unfortunate” that a retired judge was taking a position against the Constitution and the law.

In November 2025, Shah had resigned as an SC judge alongside Minallah, hours after the 27th Constitutional Amendment — which made significant changes to the country’s judicial system and established the Federal Constitutional Court — was signed into law by President Asif Ali Zardari.

“By fracturing the unity of the nation’s apex court, it has crippled judicial independence and integrity, pushing the country back by decades,” he wrote in the letter sent to the president.

“Staying on would not only amount to silent acquiescence in a constitutional wrong, but would also mean continuing to sit in a court whose constitutional voice has been muted,” he said.

World.title: 38 briefly detained in Karachi as police baton-charge protesters headed towards CM House
World.content:
KARACHI: Thirty-eight people were released after brief detention on Wednesday as police used tear gas and batons against protesting teachers headed towards Chief Minister House from Karachi Press Club (KPC).

Hundreds of teachers had gathered outside the press club at the call of the All Sindh Primary Teachers Association (ASPTA). They were headed towards CM House to present their demands that pertained to the service structure and called for delegating powers for transfers and postings to district officers.

The protesters chanted slogans and attempted to move towards the CM House. However, when they arrived near Fawara Chowk, police baton-charged them and used tear gas shells to push them back toward the press club.

Adjoining roads near the KPC were closed to traffic, according to a traffic police spokesperson.

South Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Syed Asad Raza told Dawn that all detained teachers “have been released at night”, after he confirmed in earlier comments that 38 people were taken into custody.

Speaking to Dawn earlier in the day, the DIG noted that a teachers’ organisation had announced a protest at the KPC, with a march planned toward the CM House.

He said prior to the protest, the administration made concerted efforts to resolve the matter through negotiations and engaged officials from the education department to facilitate meaningful dialogue.

The official said the protest leadership was categorically told that entry into the Red Zone — a term used to denote the area surrounding Governor House and Chief Minister House — would not be permitted. Nevertheless, the administration was directed to exhaust all available resources and make every effort to ensure a peaceful resolution through dialogue, he said.

Raza alleged that around 3:15pm, the protesters turned “violent, abandoned the course of negotiations and forcibly started advancing towards the CM House.”

He claimed that the protesting teachers “breached police barricades and resorted to pelting police personnel with stones, causing injuries to one official.”

“Upon reaching and crossing Kabir Masjid on Governor House Road, the situation escalated, compelling police to resort to shelling to disperse the violent mob and restore order,” said the South police chief.

He said during the operation, 38 protesters, including ASPTA President Ghulam Rasool Mahar and General Secretary Aijaz Ali Chandio, were taken into custody.

Raza insisted that police took drastic action as the teachers tried to enter the Red Zone.

Meanwhile, Rafiq Nizamani, the vice president of the teachers’ association, told Dawn that in 2021, the Sindh government had chalked out an “education policy” under which it was decided that teachers would not be promoted and they would remain in the same pay scale.

He said they launched a protest against this “arbitrary” decision as others were being promoted, but not them. He said that at the time, the government had assured them that their demands would be addressed, but this did not happen.

He said apart from the service structure, their other demands pertained to delegating the powers of posting primary teachers to district government officials. He said that they wanted recruitment and the transfer/posting of teachers to be delegated to district officials.

According to Nizamani, as the protesters moved from KPC towards CM House, police resorted to tear gas and a baton charge.

He claimed that two teachers were also injured. Nizamani said that they had decided to set up a protest camp outside the KPC for the fulfilment of their demands.

He admitted that the education officials had approached them for talks, but said they considered it “delaying tactics” in view of their past unfulfilled promises and decided to hold a protest march.

World.title: Democrats win US Congress in midterm rout of Trump
World.content:
Democrats seized control of the US Congress on Wednesday, capturing the Senate and House of Representatives in a stunning, nationwide rejection of Donald Trump set to put the brakes on the final two years of his presidency.

The Democratic landslide will give the opposition power to block legislation, launch broad investigations into Trump’s administration and thwart his judicial and senior government appointments.

The vote reflected deep anger over living costs, tariffs and Trump’s war against Iran, which has sent fuel prices soaring and compounded dissatisfaction with an already deeply unpopular president.

Trump struck a conciliatory note despite his history of questioning election results, telling The New York Times: “I am absolutely willing to accept those results” and promising to “work with the Democrats”.

“I think the Democrats did a good job, I really do,” the 80-year-old told Fox News, in rare praise for his political opponents. “They fought hard.”

But he sought to distance himself from his own party’s poor showing, adding: “I don’t view it as a hit on me.”

He acknowledged that the Iran conflict had contributed to the defeat but defended the military campaign, and he suggested the rival parties could find common ground on immigration, long one of the most divisive issues of his presidency.

But minutes later on social media the 80-year-old signalled how he intends to deal with Democratic attempts to pass laws, posting a picture of a red baseball cap emblazoned: “VETO.”

The Democrats’ decisive Senate breakthroughs came in Kansas and Iowa, the fifth and sixth Republican-held seats to fall in the extraordinary “blue wave” election night.

In Kansas, Methodist minister Adam Hamilton defeated Republican incumbent Roger Marshall, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from the reliably conservative state since 1932.

Iowa had not elected a Democratic senator since 2008, again illustrating the scale of party’s inroads into Republican strongholds.

Democratic gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton speaks following her victory in the US midterm elections at a Democratic Election Night rally, in Columbus, Ohio, US, November 3, 2026. — Reuters

The upsets followed victories in Texas, South Carolina, North Carolina and Ohio, where voters rejected Republican candidates despite Trump’s intensive efforts to rally his supporters.

Democrat James Talarico ousted a Trump-backed Senate candidate, while Gina Hinojosa unseated Republican governor Greg Abbott, ending decades of Republican control of the state’s top office.

Talarico said that “we defeated Goliath” after winning a US Senate seat over Texas attorney General Ken Paxton, a close ally of President Donald Trump who was heavily backed by tech billionaire Elon Musk.

“In this race, we went up against our own Goliaths. The richest man in the world, the most powerful man in the world, and the entire Washington, DC establishment,” Talarico told a victory rally in the Texas capital, Austin.

Democrats also protected key Senate seats of their own, including Jon Ossoff’s in Georgia and an open seat in New Hampshire.

In California, Democrat Xavier Becerra handily defeated Donald Trump-backed Republican Steve Hilton in the race to become the governor, US networks said.

Partial results showed Becerra, a career politician who served in the cabinet of former president Joe Biden, had a nearly two-to-one advantage over Hilton, with about half of the ballots counted.

Becerra had run a low-key campaign in a state where Democrats heavily outnumber Republicans and where the Trump brand is almost toxic.

The son of Mexican immigrants, he will be the first elected Latino governor of California, a state that would be the world’s fourth-largest economy if it were a country.

“Ladies and gentlemen, you have now entered the Becerra era,” the former US Health and Human Services secretary told his supporters at a victory party in Sacramento.

“I didn’t run to make history,” he said. “I ran to make a difference for anyone and everyone who calls California home, whether you voted for me or not.”

Becerra will replace term-limited Governor Gavin Newsom, a Democratic Party big-hitter who is believed to have his eyes on a tilt at the White House in 2028.

California Democratic gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra speaks at an election night event on November 3, 2026 in Sacramento, California. —AFP

Hilton, a British-born conservative former pundit who was once an adviser to former UK prime minister David Cameron, had always been a long shot.

He conceded he had lost a difficult race.

“Maybe this isn’t the best year to be running for office as a Republican when we see what’s going on around the country,” he said.

Republicans had held a 53-47 Senate majority.

The six-seat Democratic gain proved sufficient for networks to project a takeover despite some races remaining unresolved.

Republican heartland

Democrats also captured the House after flipping Republican-held districts in states stretching from Pennsylvania and New Jersey to Kentucky, Arizona and North Carolina.

Some victories came in territory Trump had carried comfortably in 2024, despite Republican attempts to shore up House seats by redrawing electoral boundaries.

One bellwether was Indiana, where Democrat J.D. Ford defeated Republican congresswoman Victoria Spartz in a district Trump won by 17 points. Analysts had identified an upset there as a warning of a much wider Democratic advance.

Supporters react to early election results in favor of US Senator Jon Ossoff at an election night watch party hosted by the Democratic Party of Georgia after the midterms election in Atlanta, Georgia on November 3, 2026. — AFP

In Georgia, former Atlanta mayor Keisha Lance Bottoms became the first Black woman elected governor in US history, while other Democratic gains extended to statehouses across the country.

Republicans had some bright spots in Florida, where Trump-backed Byron Donalds won the governorship, becoming the state’s first Black governor, and Ashley Moody kept a Senate seat.

George Washington University professor Todd Belt called the Democratic advance “a big wipeout and a strong repudiation of Donald Trump and his policies,” citing voters’ concerns about the economy, corruption and the Iran conflict.

Trump on defensive

Democrats will now be able to block Trump’s legislation, investigate his administration over corruption allegations, the Iran war and immigration enforcement, and use Senate control to thwart judicial appointments and senior nominations.

Robert Garcia, a Democrat expected to lead the powerful House Oversight Committee, warned Republicans on social media: “LAWYER UP.”

House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries declared Trump’s MAGA movement “on the run from sea to shining sea.”

House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-NY) speaks during a press conference with the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) at the AC Hotel Washington DC Capitol Hill Navy Yard on November 03, 2026 in Washington, DC.

Jeffries is also positioned to become the first Black speaker of the House when the new Congress convenes in January, if elected by his colleagues.

As speaker, Jeffries, representing a New York City congressional district, would preside over a majority that will be sworn in the first week of January, taking the reins from Republicans who controlled the House for the past four years.

“Today begins the great American comeback,” Jeffries proclaimed in a victory speech late on Tuesday after media outlets projected the likelihood of Democratic majorities in the House and Senate.

For many voters, the central concern was Trump’s stewardship of the economy.

“Rent, groceries, utility bills, and property taxes keep climbing,” 24-year-old Los Angeles voter Taylor Cook told AFP.

A rebuke to Trump, winner says

“In sweeping and decisive victories, the American people have rebuked the depravity, corruption and incompetence of the man named President Donald J. Trump,” incumbent Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff, the projected winner in Georgia, told supporters at a victory party.

In Florida, Republican Senator Ashley Moody fended off Democrat Angie Nixon but was ahead by only about three percentage points in a state Trump carried by 13 points in 2024, according to a vote count compiled by Reuters and USA Today, further evidence that even solidly Republican states were shifting dramatically toward Democrats.

Democrats held onto three House districts in Florida that Republican lawmakers had redrawn earlier this year, all of which backed Trump by at least nine percentage points, according to media projections.

Cait Conley, Democratic candidate for the US House of Representatives in New York’s 17th Congressional District, reacts following her victory in the US midterm elections, in Pleasantville, New York, US, November 3, 2026. — Reuters

Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms, a former mayor of Atlanta, on Tuesday was elected governor of the state of Georgia, becoming the first Black woman elected to that office in the US, media projections showed.

CNN and NBC News called the race in her favour.

Bottoms defeated billionaire health care executive Rick Jackson, who ran as a Republican. Current Governor Brian Kemp is term-limited and could not run again.

Midterm elections are typically viewed as a referendum on the president, and that is especially true for Trump, who dominates attention like no other politician. Trump himself told his supporters to “pretend I’m on the ballot” and held dozens of rallies in the closing weeks.

According to exit polls conducted by SSRS on behalf of a consortium of US media outlets, including major television networks and the Associated Press, half of voters nationwide said they saw the 2026 midterm elections as an opportunity to rebuke the president, and three-quarters said they are “angry” or “dissatisfied” with the way the country is headed.

In addition, 70 per cent of voters surveyed said they want Congress to provide more checks and balances on the president.

History is against Republicans: the sitting president’s party has lost ground in Congress in all but two midterms since World War Two. Trump’s approval rating is hovering near his career lows, with voters frustrated by war on Iran, higher fuel prices and wider affordability concerns.

Led by Trump, Republicans have portrayed Democratic candidates as radical, un-American and even communist, labels Democrats flatly reject.

Opinion polls show voters are most concerned about affordability and disapprove of Trump’s handling of the issue. His tariffs on imports, many of which the courts threw out, and his decision to attack Iran in February raised prices for consumers.

Trump deploys election monitors

The US Justice Department said it had deployed 1,000 election monitors and observers to all 50 states in what it called the largest Election Day monitoring effort in history.

Democrats criticised the plan as potential voter intimidation. In roughly two-thirds of the jurisdictions the department listed, voters supported Democrat Kamala Harris over Trump in the 2024 presidential election, a Reuters analysis found.

Election officials in several states reported no issues with the monitoring effort. New Mexico’s secretary of state’s office said it had received reports of federal monitors asking “unusual questions” in one county and that the Justice Department offered assurances that the conduct would be addressed.

World.title: Ramisa rape and murder: Sohel Rana mentions new name as charges framed
World.content:
A new name has surfaced in the Ramisa rape and murder case, with prime accused Sohel Rana telling reporters today that a man called "Dollar" was responsible for the rape and murder of the eight-year-old girl.

However, no further details about the person were immediately available.

Sohel made the claim while being escorted to the courtroom of the Dhaka Metropolitan Children Violence Suppression Tribunal.

"I am at fault, and Dollar is also at fault. I am not the only culprit," he told reporters.

Standing in the courtroom's dock, he shouted at the lawyers present in the courtroom after the hearing, and said, “I did not commit the rape; I only dismembered the body. A man named Dollar committed the rape. I have sinned, so punish me for that sin.”

At that time, Sohel further claimed that Dollar had promised to pay him Tk 2 lakh if he could bring the girl to him.

However, police officers present immediately stopped him from speaking further.

Sohel also claimed that his wife, Swapna Khatun, was innocent.

Earlier in the day, Sohel and Swapna were brought to the lock-up of the Metropolitan Sessions Judge's Court in Dhaka.

Later, Judge Masrur Salekin of the tribunal framed charges against the couple in the case over the rape and murder of Ramisa in Dhaka's Pallabi area.

Both accused pleaded not guilty after the charges were read out, said Bench Assistant Pankoj Peter Gomes.

The judge also fixed tomorrow for the start of the trial, with the victim's father, Abdul Hannan Mollah, scheduled to testify first, he added.

On May 24, Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station submitted the charge sheet before the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate's Court in Dhaka, accusing Sohel of rape, murder and destruction of evidence, and Swapna of destruction of evidence and providing false information.

Several hours later, the CMM Court transferred the case to the Children Violence Suppression Tribunal for trial.

Ramisa, a second-grade student of Popular Model High School, was found beheaded on May 19 in the house of her neighbour, Sohel.

The following day, Ramisa's father filed a case with Pallabi Police Station, accusing the couple and an unidentified person.

According to the case statement, Sohel lured Ramisa into his room and raped her. Investigators said he later slit her throat and attempted to dismember the body to conceal the crime.

On May 20, police produced Sohel and Swapna before a Dhaka court, and court sources said Sohel agreed to give a confessional statement before a magistrate. The third and unidentified accused was on the run. Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Aminul Islam Junaid recorded Sohel's confessional statement after police brought him to the magistrate’s chamber, said a court staff member.

Sub-Inspector Ohiduzzaman of Pallabi Police Station told The Daily Star that day, the prime accused had already admitted to the crime during primary interrogation.

On May 22, the Dhaka Bar Association decided not to provide legal assistance to the accused following an emergency virtual meeting of its executive committee, citing the gravity of the allegations.

The next day, the government appointed Supreme Court lawyer Musa Kalimullah as a state defence counsel to represent the accused to ensure a fair trial.

This report has been corrected at 4:43pm. In the earlier version, Sohel Rana’s comment was misreported. We regret the error.

World.title: Why Bangladesh must pivot to renewable energy now
World.content:
There are moments in a nation’s history when a crisis does more than create hardship. It reveals the weakness of an old system and opens the door to a better one. Bangladesh is now standing at such a moment.

The country is facing an energy crisis that no longer centres on power cuts. It is affecting factories, farms, schools, offices, exports, foreign currency reserves, and the daily life of ordinary people. What we are seeing today is not just a temporary shortage of gas or fuel. It is a signal that our energy system has become too dependent on imported fossil fuels.

More than 60 percent of Bangladesh’s energy demand is met through imports. LNG, coal, oil, and other fossil fuels have kept the country running for years, but this dependence has become risky and expensive. Global fuel markets are unstable because of geopolitical tension, supply chain disruption, and price volatility. For a country like Bangladesh, this creates double pressure: fuel supply becomes uncertain while fuel costs keep rising.

The government is now spending more than BDT 200 crore per day in energy subsidies. Annual energy import expenditure remains around USD 12 billion, putting serious pressure on foreign currency reserves. Nearly 70 percent of Bangladesh’s LNG imports come from Qatar. If supply is disrupted, Bangladesh can quickly face a severe shortage. In the power sector, daily gas demand exceeds 2,500 mmcfd, but supply sometimes falls to 850–900 mmcfd. This can create a power generation shortfall of 1,500–1,800 MW. Overall, the daily gas shortage exceeds 1,100 mmcfd, and peak-time electricity shortages may reach nearly 2,000 MW.

Bangladesh also has a weak Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The current reserve capacity is sufficient for only about 35–40 days, well below that of countries such as China and Japan. This makes the national energy system even more vulnerable.

Visual: Teeni and Tuni

The impact is already visible. In the readymade garments sector, gas shortages and load shedding are reducing productivity by 25–30 percent in many cases. This threatens export earnings, foreign currency reserves, and economic stability. The crisis has also reached ordinary households. Although Bangladesh declared 100 percent electrification in 2022, many rural areas still experience 10 to 20 hours of load shedding every day during summer. This affects education, small businesses, agriculture, and people’s dignity.

We have also seen long lines at fuel stations, schools moving online, and offices shortening working hours because of fuel shortages. These are not isolated events. They show how deeply energy insecurity can disturb national life.

Over the last 15 years, electricity tariffs in Bangladesh have been increased on many occasions, including more than 10 rounds of increases at both bulk and retail levels. This path is not sustainable. Fossil-fuel-based electricity depends on imported fuel, global prices, the availability of the dollar, subsidies, and repeated tariff adjustments. Solar power offers a different path. With a one-time investment, solar can provide stable energy for 15–20 years. Once installed, its fuel cost is almost zero.

The economic comparison is clear. A 1 MW HFO-based power plant produces electricity per year at a cost of nearly BDT 190 crore, with much of the cost paid in foreign currency. In contrast, a 5 MW solar project requires a one-time investment of around BDT 25 crore, after which fuel costs are practically zero. Each 1 MW of solar power can save around USD 325,000 per year in foreign currency.

This is why renewable energy should not be discussed solely in technical terms like decarbonisation, emissions, and sustainability. For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Despite Bangladesh’s potential, renewable energy contributes less than 5 percent to power generation, far below the global 30 percent target by 2030. Clear, measurable goals and timelines are essential for effective policy planning and investment decisions.

Renewable energy equipment imports face around 50–60 percent in duties and taxes, hindering local manufacturing growth. Policy reforms that reduce import duties and support local industry can accelerate renewable deployment and reduce dependency on imports.

For Bangladesh, renewable energy means jobs, fuel independence, savings in foreign currency, industrial competitiveness, agricultural protection, and economic strength. Policymakers and stakeholders can lead this transformation, inspiring confidence in a sustainable future.

Import duty is usually imposed to protect the local industry. But where local production is not yet significant, a high duty only increases project costs, reduces investment returns, and slows renewable energy expansion. Policy reforms can unlock this potential, making stakeholders feel their efforts directly contribute to progress.

India, Pakistan, Vietnam, and China have expanded solar and wind power by offering low or zero import duties, tax exemptions, and low-interest financing. Many countries have also reduced duties on lithium-ion batteries and energy storage systems. Bangladesh should learn from these examples.

The barriers are clear: high duties and VAT, high financing costs of 10–12 percent or more, limited access to easy loans, slow approval processes, net metering delays, high LC margin, weak Merchant Power Policy, lack of clear policies for rooftop solar, utility-scale solar, floating solar, agrivoltaics, solar irrigation, and hybrid solar-storage, weak local manufacturing, and insufficient grid digitalisation. Addressing these collectively can accelerate Bangladesh's renewable journey, uniting stakeholders in a common goal.

One urgent reform is customs assessment. The current weight-based assessment system does not reflect the actual value of solar equipment. It can create artificial overvaluation and raise duties by three to four times. Bangladesh should shift to transaction-value-based assessment using pro forma or commercial invoice values, in line with international practice and WTO customs valuation principles.

The second urgent reform is the elimination of customs duty on renewable energy equipment. This should apply to Solar PV Module, Photovoltaic Cell, Solar Inverter, DC Cable, Data Logger, Aluminium Mounting Structure, Battery Pack, Battery Cell, BMS Circuit Board, PV DG Controller, Hybrid Controller, Solar Plant Safety Aluminium Walkway Mesh, Safety Accessories, and related components.

Current TTI rates are high. Solar PV Module carries 26.90 percent, Photovoltaic Cell 25.75 percent, Solar Inverter 28.73 percent, DC Cable 58.40 percent, Data Logger 37.25 percent, Aluminium Mounting Structure 58.40 percent, Battery Pack and Battery Cell 58.40 percent, BMS Circuit Board 31.50 percent, pack materials 37.25 percent, PV DG Controller or Hybrid Controller 89.08 percent, and Solar Plant Safety Aluminum Walkway Mesh 37.25 percent. These should be reduced to zero percent for renewable energy expansion.

The third reform is a tax holiday. Rooftop solar power producers and project companies should receive benefits comparable to those of utility-scale renewable energy producers.
